commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] READ mode restore the cached recurrent state for hybrid prefixes that end on a block
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO READ mode serving a hybrid model with P/D disaggregation, a prompt whose first N-1 tokens end at a block boundary leaves the Mamba state block that decode caches for it unwritten, so a later request with the same prompt resumes from stale state and generates different text. This PR reads the prefill instance's state into that block as well, and skips the transfer when decode already has the whole prompt cached.



## Claims

- A repeated prompt resumes from the prefill instance's recurrent state, and a full prefix hit on decode posts no READ.
- Repeated prompts get the same answer again. In an experiment with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on MI355X sending 32 prompts twice with greedy decoding, on main only 8 of the second answers match the first, and with this PR all 32 do, the same as a server without a connector.
- GSM8K accuracy does not change, scoring 0.955 / 0.955 (strict-match / flexible-extract) with this PR, against 0.955 / 0.955 without a connector.
- Prompts that do not end on a block boundary are transferred exactly as on main.



## Validation

### Unit tests

Changed and added new tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py`. Three of them drive the real `Scheduler` with a MoRIIO READ consumer, one full-attention group and one `align`-mode Mamba group of block size 16. A 33-token request is admitted with 32 external tokens, and a second request with the same prompt with 32 locally computed tokens. Reverting the connector change makes the first two rows fail.

| Behavior | Tests | Main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| A READ of a prompt whose N-1 tokens end a block also writes the block that a later full local hit resumes from | `test_hybrid_read_writes_the_state_block_a_full_local_hit_resumes_from` | 1 failed (`[5] == [3, 5]`) | 1 passed |
| A full local prefix hit reads nothing, and the zero list keeps every page | `test_hybrid_read_full_local_prefix_hit_schedules_no_read`, `test_update_state_full_local_hit_queues_no_hybrid_reads`, `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block`, `test_glm5_next_mtp_read_pairs_every_group` | 7 failed, 13 passed | 20 passed |
| A prompt whose N-1 tokens do not end a block reads only the running slot, and an empty hybrid payload only releases P | `test_hybrid_read_of_a_prompt_not_ending_a_block_reads_only_the_running_slot`, `test_read_blocks_without_destination_only_releases_the_producer` | 2 passed | 2 passed |

### End-to-end verification with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

All runs use one MI355X node with P and D on one GPU each (TP1), and MoRIIO READ over xGMI through the example moriio proxy with `transfer_timeout` 2 s. Both instances use TRITON_ATTN, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, prefix caching and no async scheduling, with `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`, the convolution-state layout MoRIIO transfers. The scheduler block size is 1,088 tokens.

The repeated-prompt load sends 32 prompts of k·1,088+1 random token ids (k = 1 to 4, eight each) through the proxy at concurrency 1, with `temperature=0` and `max_tokens=32`, all 32 once and then all 32 again. On every second send D's prefix cache holds the first k·1,088 tokens, so no prompt token is external. Both builds include #67074, which makes a synchronous READ wait for the Mamba state copies on the compute stream, because without it the first send's own state read can race that copy. A logging hook on both builds records the blocks D queues and the READs it posts, and the proxy adds `min_tokens=1` to the prefill leg so that a prefill whose one token is EOS does not fail the request. Neither is part of this PR.

| | Main | This PR | No connector |
|---|---|---|---|
| State blocks read per Mamba group on first sends | 1 | 2 | |
| READ statuses posted on second sends (attention + Mamba) | 2,240 + 1,920 | 0 | |
| Second output identical to the first | 8 of 32 | 32 of 32 | 32 of 32 |
| Request errors | 0 | 0 | 0 |

On main every second send resumes from the unwritten block and posts a state READ after the forward has started, and 24 of 32 outputs differ from the first send. The first outputs of the two builds are identical for all 32 prompts.

GSM8K runs on this PR alone, without #67074, on the full test set (1,319 questions), 5-shot, with 64 concurrent requests. Cells show strict-match / flexible-extract. The baseline is the same model without a connector at TP1.

| | PR | No connector Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.955 / 0.955 | 0.955 / 0.955 |


<details>
<summary>commands</summary>


```bash

HOST_IP=<node IP>
P_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8100", "handshake_port": "8104", "notify_port": "8120", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'
D_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8200", "handshake_port": "8204", "notify_port": "8220", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'

python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001

# P on GPU 0 and D on GPU 1. Each instance lists the other's GPU after its own,
# so that MoRI can reach the peer's memory over xGMI.
export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS
Q36='Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 1 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"} --no-async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching'
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve $Q36 --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve $Q36 --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"

# without a connector (repeated prompts, and the GSM8K baseline without the extra flags)
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve $Q36 --port 8300
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --port 8300 --tensor-parallel-size 1

# repeated prompts: 32 lists of k*1088+1 random token ids (seed 0, ids 1000-149999), each sent once,
# then all 32 again, one at a time, with PORT=8000 (the proxy) or 8300
curl -s http://$HOST_IP:$PORT/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B", "prompt": [<token ids>], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}'

# GSM8K on all 1,319 questions, with a copy of the gsm8k task named gsm8k_nothink whose
# doc_to_text is "Question: {{question}}\nAnswer: <think>\n\n</think>\n\n"
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k_nothink --include_path <task dir> --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B,base_url=http://$HOST_IP:$PORT/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=1,tokenized_requests=False,timeout=3600

```

</details>



## Details

In MoRIIO READ mode, a hybrid decode instance loads the first N-1 prompt tokens from the prefill instance in a synchronous load and computes token N itself in the same step. The `align`-mode Mamba manager gives such a request null blocks for the skipped tokens, then one block for the state after the N-1 loaded tokens, and then a running-state slot for token N. `allocate_slots` registers the middle block in the prefix cache for the first N-1 tokens. Before the forward pass, the model runner copies the state from block `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // block_size` into the running slot (`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` and `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel`).

`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.update_state_after_alloc` reads the prefill state only into the running slot, because `split_block_groups` keeps just the running-state slot of each Mamba group. When N-1 is not a multiple of the block size, the running slot is the registered block, and that read covers it. When N-1 ends a block, the running slot is one block further and the registered block is never written. Mamba blocks are not zeroed, so that block keeps whatever its previous owner left in it, and a later request with the same prompt gets a full prefix hit and resumes from it.

On main that later request also takes the zero-external-token branch, which reads the prefill state once more. With no external tokens the scheduler marks no synchronous load, so this read is posted only after the forward pass has been launched (`ActiveKVConnector.post_forward`) and rarely lands in time. The validation prompts are k·1,088+1 tokens long, so N-1 always ends one of the 1,088-token blocks.

This PR fills the registered block during the original transfer and drops the late read.

- `MoRIIOConnectorScheduler._cached_prompt_state_blocks` finds, for each Mamba group, the block registered for the first N-1 prompt tokens when they end a block. In the external-token branch of `update_state_after_alloc`, that block is read from the prefill state slot along with the running slot. The worker already reads several state slots per group, so the number of posted READs stays the same.
- When no prompt token is external, `update_state_after_alloc` queues one empty block list per transfer group for every model, and `MoRIIOConnectorWorker._read_blocks` only releases the prefill instance. The cached state already matches the prefill state for those tokens, and a read posted after the forward pass would overwrite state that the forward pass has already advanced. `_attn_group_is_state` had no other reader and is removed.

Only this one block needs the extra read. The Mamba group gets null blocks below it, and no earlier boundary of a READ prefix is ever cached. Connectors that load asynchronously allocate no slot for token N during the load, so for them the running slot already is the registered block.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

commits.pr_title: [HY4 Flash] Allow fp8_ds_mla KV cache on Flash sliding-window MLA
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #68296. HY4 Flash SWA uses indexed sparse MLA and forces the paged FP8 kernel, which does not gather evicted SWA pages.

Allow `fp8_ds_mla` for HY4 Flash through a model-specific `MLAAttention` subclass. The shared MLA layer retains its default sliding-window restrictions, and `nvfp4_ds_mla` remains rejected for SWA.

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `fp8_e4m3` are accepted. `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` stores both as `fp8_ds_mla`, and the sliding-window check runs after that rewrite.

## Test plan

- `tests/models/hy_v4/test_flash_swa_kv_cache_dtype.py`: 20 passed. Shared `MLAAttention` still rejects sliding-window `fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_ds_mla`, and `nvfp4_ds_mla`. `HYV4FlashMLAAttention` allows the three FP8 spellings and still rejects `nvfp4_ds_mla`.

Eager TP8 on 8×H200, Hy4-flash-FP8, `--language-model-only --enforce-eager`.

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, greedy, `reasoning_effort=no_think`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `max-model-len 8192`):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Questions | 1319 |
| Correct | 1277 |
| Accuracy | 96.8% |
| Invalid | 0 |

AIME 2024, 30 problems, greedy, default long reasoning, concurrency 16, `max-model-len 32768`, `max_tokens 24576`:

| KV cache | Correct |
| --- | --- |
| bfloat16 | 29/30 |
| fp8_ds_mla | 29/30 |

The only miss is the same problem on both sides. Both generations stopped at the 24576-token cap.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Match ignored unexpected keys after renaming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Transformers backend matched `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected` against raw checkpoint keys, but Transformers matches them against renamed keys, so patterns written for renamed keys never matched. Needed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67277 (A.X-K1).

## Claims

- `Base._drop_ignored_unexpected` matches the patterns after Transformers' renamings, so A.X-K1's `mlp\.post_mlp_layernorm` (stored as `post_mlp_layernorm` and renamed into `mlp`) now drops the dense layers' unused norms instead of failing to load.
- A weight that a parameter loads is still kept, as before.

## Validation

Tiny random A.X-K1 checkpoint in the released layout (every layer stores `post_mlp_layernorm`, layer 0 is dense), 1x B200, Transformers 5.24.1:

```python
llm = LLM(path, model_impl="transformers", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enforce_eager=True,
          max_model_len=256, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3)
out = llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4]}],
                   SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=4, detokenize=False))
print("OK", out[0].outputs[0].token_ids)
```

`main` (0085facc58):
```
INFO 11-25 06:22:36 [model.py:788] Resolved architecture: TransformersMoEForCausalLM
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.mlp.post_mlp_layernorm' in TransformersMoEForCausalLM. The available parameters belonging to model.layers.0.mlp (AXK1MLP) are: {'model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight', 'model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight'}
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

This PR (78d22be102):
```
INFO 11-25 06:18:34 [model.py:788] Resolved architecture: TransformersMoEForCausalLM
INFO 11-25 06:18:38 [default_loader.py:570] Loading weights took 0.01 seconds
INFO 11-25 06:18:38 [model_runner.py:461] Model loading took 0.13 GiB memory and 1.241078 seconds
OK [331, 471, 471, 471]
```

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint script</summary>

```python
import sys

import torch
from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
from transformers import AXK1Config, AXK1ForCausalLM

out = sys.argv[1]
config = AXK1Config(
    vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, moe_intermediate_size=128,
    num_hidden_layers=2, mlp_layer_types=["dense", "sparse"],
    num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=4, q_lora_rank=64, kv_lora_rank=512,
    qk_nope_head_dim=128, qk_rope_head_dim=64, v_head_dim=128,
    n_routed_experts=8, num_experts_per_tok=2, n_shared_experts=1, n_group=1, topk_group=1,
    max_position_embeddings=512, bos_token_id=0, eos_token_id=1,
)
torch.manual_seed(0)
AXK1ForCausalLM(config).to(torch.bfloat16).save_pretrained(out)
weights = load_file(f"{out}/model.safetensors")
# The released checkpoints also store the norm on the dense layer, which does not use it
weights["model.layers.0.post_mlp_layernorm.weight"] = torch.ones(256, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
save_file(weights, f"{out}/model.safetensors", metadata={"format": "pt"})
```
</details>

`pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_ignored_unexpected_patterns_match_renamed_keys` on 78d22be102: 1 passed in 0.74s (fails without the fix).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Tile whole kernel rows of groups to persist logical block for drafter blocks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Claude and I hit this while benchmarking P/D for Kimi K3 with its DSpark draft model on GB300. 

Every engine that loaded `NixlConnector` died at startup in `register_kv_caches`, on every topology we tried, including a plain 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 with no DCP. 

The cause seems to be a mismatch between two layers of vLLM:
- The model runner picks a kernel block size for each KV cache group, but `NixlConnectorWorker` picks one physical/logical block ratio and applies it to every layer. 
- When one group keeps the full logical block as a single row, NIXL cannot split that group's cache into the blocks it expects. 

#59586's row split should also accept a row that ends in padding: its tokens only have to fit in the row. Such a row is then registered as byte pages through #59586's existing path, and the handshake refuses a peer whose rows are laid out differently. This means we just outright reject mismatches, which might be wrong for DP -> TP (I haven't tested this extensively, and I'm currently working on it).

Seems like #63997 (Gemma 4) has the same root cause. 
#59586 (merged) splits dense token-major kernel rows into NIXL pages and rejects every other row. Kimi K3's draft row is padded (917504 B of tokens in a 1032192 B row), so on main it is now refused at startup with #59586's `NotImplementedError ... cannot split`. 

#59586's dense-row path and its rejection of head-major rows stay as they are. Once the drafter gets its own KV cache pool (#64611) the draft row is no longer padded, and both the flag and the guard can go (there is a TODO). #64067 covers contiguous views.

_Note that this also might just be K3-specific, so I haven't tested with other models just yet_.

## Claims

- Kimi K3 with the DSpark draft on `FLASH_ATTN` now starts and serves P/D over `NixlConnector`. On main every engine refuses at startup (#59586's `NotImplementedError`), and on nightly `7c3a9302` it asserts, before it accepts a single request.
- The draft KV arrives intact. Over 8 more 15-minute runs at concurrency 32 (30,032 transfers), decode saw 0 failures and an acceptance rate of 0.151-0.174, around the 0.158-0.160 we measured for aggregated serving, where no KV moves at all!
- It costs nothing measurable against our earlier workaround that registers the same geometry: 0.975x geometric mean over 4 order-swapped pairs (t = -0.94).
- A peer with a different TP, DCP, block size or ratio now gets a `NotImplementedError` at handshake, where it would otherwise have received bytes from the wrong heads or tokens. On K3 a DCP mismatch never reaches it, since the existing KDA check (`base_worker.py:2936`) already refuses one with a `RuntimeError`.
- The change touches only NIXL registration and the handshake, so hopefully no regression in terms of MLA groups and Mamba states.

## Validation

We ran on GB300 NVL72 trays (4 GPUs each) with `vllm-project/Kimi-K3-pruned75` and the draft `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`, on the image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7c3a9302`. 

Claude backported the change in this PR and patch in place lol.

```bash
vllm serve vllm-project/Kimi-K3-pruned75 \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-cumem-allocator --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"transfer_mode":"pull","backends":["UCX"]}}'
```

**Before.** with 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 and no DCP
- Prefill dies 44 s before decode, so the failure happens before any handshake and has nothing to do with the P/D topology:

```
engine-p0  12:37:32  AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions: layer=model.layers.93.self_attn.attn, cache_nbytes=4242538496, num_blocks=129472, block_stride=1032192, physical_page_size=36864, cache_shape=(4624, 4, 1792, 128), cache_stride=(1032192, 128, 512, 1)
engine-d1  12:38:16  AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions: layer=model.layers.93.self_attn.attn, cache_nbytes=4128768000, num_blocks=126000, block_stride=1032192, physical_page_size=36864, cache_shape=(4500, 4, 1792, 128), cache_stride=(1032192, 128, 512, 1)
```

**After.** AgentX multi-turn load at concurrency 32 (mean input about 100k tokens). The decode engine's `/metrics` show:

| transfers | GB moved | failed | MB / transfer | descriptors / transfer | transfer p50 | spec accept rate | mean accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2180 | 3650 | 0 | 1674 | 1718 | 43.6 ms | 0.163 | 2.30 |

The baseline is aggregated TP4 serving of the same load, which accepts at 0.158-0.160. 
- If transfers scrambled the draft rows, the draft would mispredict on every transferred prefix and the acceptance rate doesn't fall below that band in the logs. 
- **IMPORTANT**: This is indirect evidence, since we have not compared the draft KV bytes on P and D.

**With #59586.** Claude backported #59586 alone, and #59586 plus this PR, onto the same image, and ran both on two GB300 clusters:

| | cluster A | cluster B |
|---|---|---|
| #59586 alone, K3 single engine | dies: `NotImplementedError: Layer model.layers.93.self_attn.attn uses kernel blocks of 1792 tokens, which NIXL cannot split into its 154168 transfer blocks (cache_shape=(5506, 4, 1792, 128), ...)` | same |
| #59586 + this PR, single engine | ready | ready |
| 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 | serves | serves |
| prefill TP4 -> decode TP8 | refused at handshake | same |

**After aarnphm/vllm#4.** The same backport with Nicolo's version, on cluster B:
- single engine: ready
- 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 probe: serves, `nixl_num_failed_transfers=0` on P and D
- prefill TP4 -> decode TP8: `NotImplementedError: NIXL kernel rows ending in padding require matching TP, DCP and block sizes on both peers.`
- 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 at concurrency 32 for 15 minutes: 345.0 tok/s, 2680 transfers, 0 failed, acceptance 0.152, 1616 descriptors per transfer, all in line with the A/B legs below (330-356 tok/s, 1613-1644 descriptors per transfer).

**Handshake probes.** On top of the table above: TP8 -> TP8 serves, and TP4 -> DCP4 is refused by the existing KDA check (`RuntimeError: Hybrid MLA+Mamba NIXL transfers require matching DCP sizes, got local=4, remote=1`), before it reaches the new guard.

**Repeat A/B.** 1P1D TP4 at concurrency 32, seed 42, against the f8ff50b workaround, each pair in both orders:

| pair | profile | workaround tok/s | this PR tok/s | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 warmup request per lane | 338.4 | 335.1 | 0.990 |
| 2 | 1 warmup request per lane | 355.5 | 330.2 | 0.929 |
| 3 | default warmup | 426.4 | 400.2 | 0.939 |
| 4 | default warmup | 419.6 | 438.8 | 1.046 |

The warmup profile moves both arms together (ITL ~46 ms vs ~22 ms), and the arms differ by less than either one varies.

**PP -> TP.** This one is not reachable on K3. Even with prefill as `kv_producer`, main refuses a PP > 1 prefill for MLA under HMA before registration (`base_worker.py:2962`: "NixlConnector (pull) supports pipeline_parallel_size > 1 with hybrid KV cache layouts (HMA) only for attention KV without MLA or CSA-linear caches"), so the PP unit test below is the only coverage of that path.

**Unit test.** In `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`:
- `test_token_major_kernel_rows_split_into_transfer_blocks` gets a padded LBNHC case (Nicolo): the descriptors and the flag.
- `test_padded_kernel_rows_reject_a_peer_with_another_row_layout` (Nicolo): a TP2 or DCP2 peer gets the `NotImplementedError`.
- A scaled-down K3, an MLA target split into 4 kernel pages next to a draft that keeps one padded row per block (pad starts inside byte page 3, as it does inside page 24 on K3):
  - `test_whole_row_draft_next_to_split_target_pulls_every_row_byte`: D pulls one request from P, the recorded descriptors run as memcpy, and every row byte lands in both groups, pad included, with nothing else in D touched.
  - `test_whole_row_draft_pulls_every_row_byte_from_prefill_pp_stages`: same pull from a PP2 prefill (target on stage 0, draft on stage 1).

With main's `base_worker.py` (75d8770263, after #59586), the K3 tests fail on #59586's refusal, the same one the GB300 engine hits:

```
NotImplementedError: Layer draft uses kernel blocks of 16 tokens, which NIXL cannot split into its 24 transfer blocks (cache_shape=(6, 2, 16, 5), cache_stride=(192, 5, 10, 1), physical_page_size=48). ...
4 failed, 369 deselected, 46 warnings in 3.79s
```

At 471e9860ca, the whole file:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
375 passed, 1 warning in 83.76s
```

_Note that I ran this on macOS, with a small pytest plugin that makes the Mac look like vLLM's CPU platform (the `cpu_test` setup CI uses)._

## Details

### Request path and where it fails


1. The model runner picks a kernel block size per KV cache group (`prepare_kernel_block_sizes`, `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:681`). With K3's 1792-token logical blocks, the MLA target group gets 64-token pages, while the `FLASH_ATTN` draft group accepts 1792 and keeps one row per block.
2. `NixlConnectorWorker._sync_block_size_with_kernel` (`base_worker.py:1265`) then picks a single common size, 64, and sets `_physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block = 28` for every layer, the draft layers included.
3. `register_kv_caches` (`base_worker.py:1697`) splits each layer's view into `num_blocks = rows * 28` blocks of `physical_page_size`. On main, #59586's `_splits_kernel_rows` (`base_worker.py:137`) raises for the draft view, because a 36864 B page is not a run of whole 512 B tokens (64 x 512 = 32768), and the engine never gets to serve.
4. On the first request, decode handshakes with prefill in `_validate_remote_agent_handshake` (`base_worker.py:2968`), which is where the new guard lives.
5. On every request, decode expands each logical block id `b` to the kernel ids `28b .. 28b+27` (`_logical_to_kernel_block_ids`, `base_worker.py:4029`) and reads those descriptors from prefill. The fix leans on this step.

### One logical block in bytes

```
              0                                  917504                   1032192 B
MLA target    |   p0  |   p1  |   p2  |  ...  |  p24  |  p25  |  p26  |  p27  |   28 pages, 64 tokens x 576 B each
FA draft      | 1792 tokens x 4 heads x 128 B (fp8) |           pad           |   1 row, stride (1032192, 128, 512, 1)
NIXL expects  | 36864 | 36864 | 36864 |  ...  | 36864 | 36864 | 36864 | 36864 |   28 blocks of 36864 B per row
```

The hybrid allocator hands every group the same page size, so the draft row is padded from 917504 B up to 1032192 B. The MLA view has a stride of one 36864 B page. The draft view has 4500 rows at a stride of 1032192 B, while NIXL is looking for 126000 blocks of 36864 B, and the segment check fails on that mismatch.

### Fix

`_splits_kernel_rows` (`base_worker.py:162`) used to require that a NIXL page be exactly a run of whole tokens. It now only requires that the row's tokens fit in the row (`token_stride * N <= split * physical_page_size`). Dense rows behave as before. A padded row is registered through #59586's path as `split` pages of `physical_page_size` each, and `_splits_padded_kernel_rows` is set (`base_worker.py:1908`).

These pages ignore the draft's own layout. 
- Page 0 holds tokens 0-71 across all 4 heads, and the padding starts partway through page 24. 
- That is fine because of step 5: a logical block always expands to all 28 page ids of its row, so a transfer copies the whole row, padding included, byte for byte, and the decode row ends up identical to the prefill row.

Byte pages line up only with an identical row: a different TP puts other heads at the same offset, a different DCP / block size / ratio puts other tokens there. So when the flag is set, the handshake raises `NotImplementedError` for such a peer (`base_worker.py:3044`).

### Cost

The new checks run once per layer at registration, so they add no host-device sync and leave the steady-state step untouched. 

Draft layers post 28 descriptors per logical block, the same count as the MLA layers next to them. 

The one tradeoff is the padding: about 114688 B per row (~11%) travels with every transfer. Packing draft rows without padding would avoid that, but it belongs to the KV layout work and the KVConnector refactor work.

### Gaps

We have not compared draft KV bytes between P and D, so acceptance stands in as the evidence. 

We have not tested Gemma 4 from #63997, ROCm, or the push transfer mode.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Preserve Clef SystemOne probabilities with raw pooling outputs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Clef-Flash and Clef-Omni share the same `/v1/systemone` read. If the server is started with `--pooler-config '{"use_activation": false}'`, the endpoint currently returns raw logits in its probability fields. This can produce negative confidence and a score outside the requested scale.

## Validation

### Reproducer

One NVIDIA H100 80 GB, BF16, one GPU, pretrained `Cloudflare/clef-flash`. Both runs used the same locally downloaded snapshot (four backbone shards and the joint head), the same precompiled extension binaries, and Python source from the respective revision. The equivalent Hub command is:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash \
  --revision 22b75507981345858dd152fbd9a6f8c0c4068b0a \
  --runner pooling --language-model-only --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 1024 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 \
  --seed 123 --pooler-config '{"use_activation": false}'
```

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '
{
  "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
  "state": "The customer wants a refund.",
  "questions": {
    "route": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which team?",
      "criteria": {
        "returns": "Refunds",
        "sales": "Purchases"
      }
    },
    "receipt": {
      "type": "noul",
      "instructions": "Is there a receipt?"
    },
    "urgency": {
      "type": "score",
      "instructions": "How urgent?",
      "criteria": [
        "routine",
        "urgent",
        "critical"
      ]
    }
  }
}
' | jq -c .answers
```

### Output on main / on branch

Both requests returned HTTP 200. Main:

```json
{"route":{"type":"choice","choice":"returns","probabilities":{"returns":0.52734375,"sales":-3.921875},"confidence":0.52734375},"receipt":{"type":"noul","noul":-2.28125,"probabilities":{"yes":-2.28125,"no":-0.1298828125},"confidence":-0.1298828125},"urgency":{"type":"score","score":-7.4453125,"legend":{"0":"routine","1":"urgent","2":"critical"},"probabilities":{"0":0.7109375,"1":-1.4140625,"2":-3.015625},"confidence":0.7109375}}
```

Branch:

```json
{"route":{"type":"choice","choice":"returns","probabilities":{"returns":0.988447368144989,"sales":0.011552671901881695},"confidence":0.988447368144989},"receipt":{"type":"noul","noul":0.10420353710651398,"probabilities":{"yes":0.10420353710651398,"no":0.8957964777946472},"confidence":0.8957964777946472},"urgency":{"type":"score","score":0.14655237644910812,"legend":{"0":"routine","1":"urgent","2":"critical"},"probabilities":{"0":0.874501645565033,"1":0.10444433242082596,"2":0.021054022014141083},"confidence":0.874501645565033}}
```

As a control, removing `--pooler-config` on main produced the same answers as the fixed branch above. The maximum absolute difference between the branch probabilities and a per-question softmax of main's raw logits was below `4e-8`. The real-checkpoint HTTP run covered Clef-Flash. Clef-Omni uses the same decision read and was covered by the existing strategy and pooler tests.

### Test plan

On one H100 80 GB at `d0784053240f54f0dfb429a9e961262ecda6e80f`, run the Qwen module and then the Clef module in the same pytest process. This exercises Qwen server teardown before Clef starts.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_structured_decisions_e2e.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_clef_raw_pooling_e2e.py --tb=short
# 15 passed in 71.50s (0:01:11)
```

On the original base with the Clef test copied in, running just the second file produced:

```text
E   assert 0.97265625 == 1.0 ± 1.0e-06
1 failed in 44.63s
```

The existing strategy test also checks the internal request for both Clef strategies. Run with GPUs hidden:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py::test_joint_schema_reads_every_question_at_once --tb=short
# Base with the new assertion: AssertionError: assert None is True (both strategies)
# 2 failed in 5.11s
# PR: 2 passed in 4.73s
```

The Clef regression uses a two-layer dummy-weight server and downloads no checkpoint weights. The split still uses one server startup per model.

Related checks on the original H100-tested revision (`0f86424fd884e7902c14adf274ee71d1dacdd8e3`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k 'joint_schema' tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_clef_omni.py --tb=short
# 12 passed, 82 deselected in 20.90s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_clef_omni.py --tb=short
# 1 passed in 1.58s
```

### AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6) drafted the code.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Remove Mamba1 models and kernels
[Bugfix][Frontend] Refresh echoed text after prompt truncation
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When `/v1/completions` truncates a text prompt with an explicit `truncation_side`, `echo=true` still returns the original text. This change updates the echoed text to match the tokens sent to the engine, following up on #61876.

## Claims

The fix applies to streaming and non-streaming responses. Text prompts without actual post-tokenization truncation keep their original text, including padding-only requests. Requests that do not need prompt detokenization do not perform an additional decode. Tokenizer-added special tokens are excluded from the rebuilt text and echoed logprobs, while user-supplied special tokens, model input IDs, prompt usage and `return_token_ids` behavior are preserved.

## Validation

With `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` served as `qwen`:

The role labels below are plain text in the completion prompt.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen",
       "prompt":"Role: You are a helpful geography assistant. Answer in one sentence.\nUser: What is the capital of France?\nAssistant:",
       "echo":true,"truncate_prompt_tokens":12,"truncation_side":"left"}'
```

The prompt has 27 tokens and is truncated to 12. Compare the echoed prefix of `choices[0].text`, omitting the generated continuation. Before the fix, it still includes the discarded system-style instruction:

```text
Role: You are a helpful geography assistant. Answer in one sentence.
User: What is the capital of France?
Assistant:
```

After the fix, the echoed prefix contains only the retained user question and assistant label:

```text
User: What is the capital of France?
Assistant:
```

Both versions report 12 prompt tokens; only the echoed prefix was compared.

Real OPT-125m tests on NVIDIA GB10 (float32, eager, `TRITON_ATTN`) cover added BOS, user-supplied special tokens and empty echoes across both response modes, with and without generation: **12 HTTP/SSE cases**, checking text, offsets, input IDs and usage.

Tested: `564f7e3fe2ea202c98f035b71cafbd103ed9cdce`.

- HTTP/SSE: `12 passed, 3 warnings in 17.45s`.
- Renderer, preprocessing, offset/error and API utility tests: `183 passed, 16 warnings in 109.90s (0:01:49)`.
- Cohere/Mistral renderers: `117 passed, 14 warnings in 27.46s`.
- Tokenizer compatibility: `6 passed, 4 deselected, 14 warnings in 1.04s`.
- All applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy, passed.

The HTTP regression fails on upstream `99b0b0b0f` (12 failures). The padding regression fails on `428d703f0` and passes with this patch (2 cases). Additional real OPT and HF/native Mistral inference checks also passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_completions.py \
  tests/renderers/inputs/test_preprocess.py \
  tests/renderers/test_token_offsets.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -q \
  -k truncated_echo_excludes_only_added_special_tokens
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/test_cohere.py tests/renderers/test_mistral.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_hf.py -q \
  -k 'special_tokens_mask or legacy_proxy or unrelated_jinja or standard_chat_template'
git diff --name-only -z 99b0b0b0f | \
  xargs -0 .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files
```

## Details

Post-tokenization validation truncates the token IDs but leaves the original `prompt` string in place. The detokenization added by #61876 is skipped because that string is still present. `BaseRenderer` now also detokenizes when a truncation slice is present, rebuilding the text from the retained tokens in both synchronous and asynchronous paths. Padding alone does not invalidate cached text.

For text prompts, an encoding-time `special_tokens_mask` distinguishes automatically added tokens from special tokens in the user's text. The mask is sliced alongside IDs by the existing `TokenizeParams` machinery and consumed when rebuilding text. Both response modes use one helper to filter echoed prompt IDs and their logprobs together before the existing formatter runs. Model input IDs remain intact. Empty echoed prefixes are preserved when creating engine inputs.

HF-family renderers share tokenization and sync/async detokenization through a renderer mixin. `MistralRenderer` retains its SentencePiece-specific decode. One encoding helper requests the mask without changing cached tokenizer inheritance.

This covers explicit `truncation_side` with `truncate_prompt_tokens` in the Python Completions API, during post-tokenization validation rather than inside the tokenizer. These truncation controls are vLLM extensions; their echo behavior is documented in the Completions serving guide. Existing per-token decoding rules are unchanged.

This is separate from #61876, which fixes detokenization order for token-ID inputs, and #62684, which handles Rust echo with `return_token_ids=true`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Model] Nemotron Shortcut SDSA: convert NVFP4 K/V once per request by key position
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Nemotron Shortcut's SDSA backend cannot serve an NVFP4 KV cache on any FlashInfer release. Its token-sparse core converts the selected NVFP4 K/V to FP8 with `flashinfer.sdsa.token_sparse.gather_nvfp4_kv_cache`, which came from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9321. That PR was closed without merging, so the backend refuses an NVFP4 KV cache at init. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9527 replaced it (merged, in FlashInfer 0.7.6rc1 and later) with a conversion by key position. This PR moves the backend to that API, and converts each selected key once per request instead of once per query row.

All changes are in `vllm/models/nemotron_shortcut/nvidia/sdsa/`.

## Claims

- An NVFP4 KV cache works on FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9527 (0.7.6rc1 and later). On a FlashInfer without it, the backend still raises at init, now naming the functions it needs. Other KV cache dtypes take the same code paths as before.
- Fewer conversions:
  - **Decode:** all rows are converted in one `gather_nvfp4_kv_cache_by_position` launch. From 16 requests that verify drafts (MTP), each request's selected keys are converted once for all of its 1 + k rows (`compact_nvfp4_kv_cache`).
  - **Prefill:** each request's selected keys are converted once per step and layer (`compact_nvfp4_kv_cache`), so NVFP4 prefill rows hold key positions instead of cache slots.
- Same numerics as the per-row gather:
  - The attention reads the same FP8 values, still divided by 6, in the same order.
  - trtllm-gen still runs in launches of 32 decode and 256 prefill rows, the per-row gather's launch sizes, so it picks the same kernels.

## Validation

**pre-commit** on the changed files: ruff, typos, mypy and the repo's own checks pass.

**New tests**, in `tests/models/nemotron_shortcut/sdsa/test_sdsa_backend.py`:
- `test_nvfp4_prefill_launches` checks how prefill requests split into compaction groups and launches.
- `test_nvfp4_writer_and_conversion_roundtrip` checks that vLLM's NVFP4 cache writer followed by FlashInfer's conversion by key position gives back the BF16 inputs. It skips without flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9527, as on CI's FlashInfer 0.7.4.

**GB300 runs.** One node of 4x GB300, with vLLM's compiled extensions from the wheel of `main` `eb42ba6` and transformers 5.20.2. This PR runs on FlashInfer 0.7.6rc2 (PyPI). The baseline is `main` on FlashInfer `main` + flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9321, which has the per-row gather.

- **`tests/models/nemotron_shortcut`:**
  - FlashInfer 0.7.6rc2: 169 passed, including both new tests.
  - FlashInfer 0.7.4 (CI's pin): 167 passed, 2 skipped. The skips are the round trip, and the NVFP4 experts test, which needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9260.
- **Serving with an NVFP4 KV cache, gsm8k against the baseline** (lm_eval 0.4.13). Every result is within the standard error of the baseline's:
  - A BF16 checkpoint with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`, TP4: 500 questions, 0-shot with the chat template.
  - The same with MTP 3. Draft acceptance is also unchanged. The server log shows all three paths ran: per-row decode, once-per-request decode (16+ requests verifying drafts) and once-per-request prefill.
  - An NVFP4 checkpoint whose KV cache scheme is NVFP4: 400 questions, 5-shot. Once at TP4, and once at DP4 + EP with the all-gather/reduce-scatter transport.
- **DP startup stress:** the BF16 checkpoint at DP4 + EP, with the all-gather/reduce-scatter transport overlapped with attention on a side stream, an NVFP4 KV cache and MTP 3.
  - 5 of 5 starts came up clean.
  - Each start then served a 192-question gsm8k burst at 64 concurrent requests. Each burst ran the once-per-request decode and prefill paths, and logged no CUDA errors.

## Details

- **`backend.py`:**
  - The NVFP4 workspace is one FP8 `[K | V]` region of 512 MiB, plus a zero row.
  - `compact_nvfp4_kv_cache`'s scratch comes from the workspace manager. Its key bitmap is persistent: it is zeroed once, and every compaction leaves it zeroed.
  - `_nvfp4_prefill_launches` splits a step's prefill requests into compaction groups. A group is a run of one request's tokens. It is dense when its rows select at least as many keys as its context holds; otherwise it holds the union of its rows' selections.
  - The doctest in `_nvfp4_prefill_launches` covers the split.
- **`prefill.py`:**
  - `SdsaPrefillPlan` keeps the request lengths for the compaction.
  - For an NVFP4 KV cache, `_token_slots` writes key positions (`keep_positions`) instead of cache slots.
- **`flashinfer_ops.py`:** `has_nvfp4_kv_conversion` checks for `compact_nvfp4_kv_cache` and `gather_nvfp4_kv_cache_by_position`.

vLLM pins FlashInfer 0.7.4, which has neither the old function nor the new ones. So CI behaves as it does on `main`: no CI test uses an NVFP4 KV cache. Bumping the pin to a FlashInfer release with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9527 is left to a separate PR.

Ported from amitz-nv's change (co-author).

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Support ROCm AITER fused shared experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support ROCm AITER fused shared experts (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`) on the Transformers modeling backend, so models moved off native implementations (e.g. A.X-K1 in #67277) keep it.

## Claims

- With FSE enabled, a fused MoE block's shared expert runs as extra routed experts, loaded from the checkpoint's shared expert weights, as in native DeepSeek and Qwen3-Next.
- It applies only where it is exact: internal routing, a bias-free SiLU GLU shared expert as wide as `n_shared_experts` routed experts, and whatever `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` allows (EP, quantization). Other blocks keep the separate shared expert.
- `maybe_fuse_shared_experts` takes the experts' name instead of assuming `mlp.experts`; native callers are unchanged.

## Validation

No AMD hardware was available, so this relies on ROCm CI. The new test (tiny DeepSeek-V3 checkpoint whose routed expert 0 copies the shared expert) is added to the MI355 Quantized MoE job, since the MI300/MI355 Quantization jobs that would run `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` are disabled (#66672 re-enables them).

On a B200 with FSE forced on, the test passes: the shared expert is built as slot 4 and its loaded weights match expert 0. It fails when the weight renaming is disabled. Routing tokens to the fused slot is AITER-only, so CUDA cannot check outputs; MI355 CI has to.

`pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/ tests/models/test_utils.py`: 148 passed.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor][SleepMode] Make the allocator data copy a subclass hook
commits.pr_body:
## Modification

Move the host/device copy out of `_put_to_sleep` and `wake_up` into an overridable `_copy(src_ptr, dst_ptr, nbytes)` hook, so out-of-tree allocators can reuse both methods instead of reimplementing them around their own copy API. `_put_to_sleep` stays deliberately non-overridable: the CPU-backup policy it encodes is device independent.

## Claims

Behavior is unchanged on CUDA/ROCm: the default hook issues the same `libcudart.cudaMemcpy(dst, src, n)` call at the same two points.

## Overview

Complete kv-C from #49569 and enable MyPy for `tests/v1/kv_connector`, following the [approved claim](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-6312150429). PR 9's parent/root scope in #62891 is unchanged.

## Claims

- All 108 connector Python files pass MyPy 1.20.2 targeting Python 3.11 and 3.12.
- Route the directory through `SILENT_GROUPS`, preserving parent and other routing.
- Restore the previously uncollected MLA notification test using the current handshake contract and a local config, with no Hub download.

## Validation

Rebased onto `831dd92674`; current head `15410f26c4`. Validated Python source: `10eed50d38` on main `2f8c840032`; the final rebase adds only upstream Rust/release changes. All Python sources, tests and check configuration are identical. After that rebase, all **15 affected entry-point cases** and the directory MyPy/pre-commit checks pass again.

- Complete directory MyPy 1.20.2 for Python 3.11/3.12: **108 sources, zero errors**. The actual all-files MyPy hook, applicable pre-commit and commit hooks pass.
- CPU selection: **1232 passed, three skipped**. Untouched validation main: **1231 passed, the same three skips**. JUnit comparison finds no missing upstream case or changed common outcome; the additional pass is the restored MLA test.
- Store connector/worker/scheduler/HMA: **473 passed, five existing layout skips**.
- NIXL Push, descriptor geometry and MLA: **365 passed**, including all three new block-size rejection parameters from #59747.
- MyPy with `--platform darwin` passes for the repaired NIXL file.
- MLA with an empty HF cache, no credentials, offline flags and a Python outbound-connection guard: **one passed**, zero connection attempts and no HF cache files.
- Temporary wrong-ID controls fail at the original broadcast and READ payload assertions. No deliberate defect is retained.

These selections overlap. Local GPU/NCCL, physical NIXL/RDMA and ROCm/MORI validation remains unavailable: driver 550.144.03 cannot initialize the installed PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 build, and ROCm/MORI dependencies are absent. The results above are local. Check the current GitHub Actions and Buildkite runs for hosted execution; these local counts do not establish GPU/ROCm execution.

```bash
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff upstream/main...HEAD --name-only)
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -m cpu_test -q -rs --timeout=90 -W error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_mla_broadcast_notif_uses_remote_request_id -q --timeout=90
```

</details>

## Details

The MLA test was nested inside `test_handshake_decode_errors`, so pytest never collected it. Its registration call and READ assertions had drifted. The restored test runs the real asynchronous handshake: decode TP=1 reads from prefill rank 0 and notifies ranks 1–3. Both the READ completion and broadcasts must carry the remote prefill request ID, rather than the local decode ID. Only external transport is faked.

Its config is now a real one-layer `DeepseekV2Config` saved under `tmp_path`, retaining the MLA dimensions used by the fixture. With no HF cache or credentials, the test still passes. Replacing either notification ID in memory makes it fail with `decode-req-AAAA:1` versus required `prefill-req-BBBB:1`. This restores coverage; it does not claim a production request-ID defect. The active `v1-others-cpu` command selects it; collection with that working-directory and marker convention confirms one case.

The review cleanup removes 88 redundant scheduler hash wrappers, keeps 13 required by typed `ReqMeta` boundaries, and adds `_hashes()` for repeated worker lists. Scheduler `BoundaryPut` construction now matches upstream. The three specified lifetime-sensitive method overrides use `type: ignore[method-assign]`, and monkeypatch parameters are regular arguments. Original assertions, decorators and async cleanup are preserved. No production change, relaxed assertion, retry or new skip is included.

This rebase keeps #59747's rejection of different physical P/D block sizes and removes its obsolete ratio stub while retaining scoped monkeypatches. It also fixes four type errors in the new async Mooncake lookup tests from #61292, using concrete fixture checks and a single stored lookup result. Existing assertions and async cleanup remain intact.

I checked the issue and related work before opening this PR; #62891 covers the separate parent/root rollup. AI assistance was used for implementation and local checks.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Cap Qwen3-VL videos at 32 per prompt by default
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Apply a model's default per-prompt item cap when `--limit-mm-per-prompt` gives no count for a modality, as Python does since vllm-project/vllm#69098: Qwen3-VL and the architectures that inherit its processing info accept at most 32 videos per prompt by default. The Rust frontend fell back to 999 items for every model, so on these models it accepted up to 999 videos where Python returns 400.

## Claims

- `MultimodalModelInfo` resolves each modality's item limit once, at model load: the configured count, else the model's default, else 999. `validate_modality_limits` reads the resolved limit, so chat, `/inference/v1/generate` features and `vllm-rs render` enforce the same count.
- The defaults live in a `DEFAULT_ITEM_LIMITS` table in `rust/src/chat/src/multimodal/models.rs`, keyed by the checkpoint's `model_type`: video capped at 32 for `qwen3_vl`, `qwen3_vl_moe`, `qwen3_5`, `qwen3_5_moe` and `qwen4_exp`, the `Qwen3VLProcessingInfo` architectures that llm-multimodal's `qwen3_vl` spec serves. An explicit count still overrides the default; an options object without `count` (for example `{"video": {"num_frames": 4}}`) keeps it.
- The `rust/README.md` sentences and the closing paragraph of the media-budget section in `docs/usage/security.md`, which told Rust frontend users to set a video count of 32 by hand, are deleted (the second commit).

## Validation

On head `2ec053beca` (base `main` `93873e7aca`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [  23.738s] 2925 tests run: 2925 passed, 13 skipped` (the docs commit changes nothing under `rust/`).

New test `validate_mm_limits_applies_the_model_default_without_a_configured_count`, ported from Python's `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py::test_chat_render_video_options_keep_default_count_limit` (which starts the Python render server, so it cannot run against Rust):

- Qwen3-VL accepts 32 videos and rejects 33 with Python's message, `At most 32 video(s) may be provided in one prompt.`; the same holds with a count-less `{"video": {"num_frames": 4}}` entry.
- An explicit `{"video": 64}` still allows 64.
- A Qwen2.5-VL checkpoint (`model_type: qwen2_5_vl`) whose path selects the `qwen3_vl` spec keeps 999, as in Python.

Red-green: with the `qwen3_vl` row removed, the test fails at the 33-video case; with a row that also matches `qwen2_5_vl`, it fails at the path-matched case.

## Details

**Why `model_type`, not the resolved spec.** Python picks the processor by architecture, while the `qwen3_vl` spec also matches a model by its path: a Qwen2.5-VL checkpoint under a `qwen3-...-vl` directory resolves to that spec, and it must keep 999.

**Layering.** The consumer is `MultimodalModelInfo::validate_modality_limits`. The default is vLLM's per-model serving policy, not processing behavior, so it stays in the vLLM tree next to the local specs instead of going into llm-multimodal, and applies whichever crate provides the spec.

**Scope.**

- LLaVA-OneVision also defaults to 32 videos in Python, but the Rust frontend serves no LLaVA-OneVision video input.
- Python also caps counts at the processor's supported limit (`get_supported_mm_limits`); unchanged here, and Qwen3-VL's supported limits are unbounded.
- Python's 400 also sets `error.param` to `"video"`; the Rust `MmLimitExceeded` error carries no `param`. That gap predates this PR.
- On `/inference/v1/generate`, Rust counts supplied features and raw media parts together against the limit, while Python counts only the raw tail. This is the existing whole-prompt policy, now also applied to the 32-video default.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR applies model default item limits in the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex in two rounds: keying the defaults by the resolved spec gave a path-matched Qwen2.5-VL checkpoint 32 (fixed by keying on `model_type`), and stale 999 help text (fixed); a request to add a Cosmos3 entry was declined, since Cosmos3 resolves no Rust spec under its own id. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Echo null logprobs for prompt tokens the engine never scored
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make `/v1/completions` with `echo: true` and `logprobs` return a `null` logprob for every prompt token the engine never scored, as Python does since vllm-project/vllm#68605 (issue vllm-project/vllm#68601), instead of failing with 500. This covers a request that finishes before its prefill completes, such as an engine-side abort, and a one-token prompt, which has no position to score.

## Claims

- **Request finished during prefill.** The engine sends prompt logprobs only once prefill is done, so such a request reaches the frontend with none. The Rust frontend now returns 200 with `finish_reason: "abort"` and one echoed entry per prompt token with a `null` logprob, streaming and non-streaming, as Python's `_padded_prompt_logprobs` does.
- **One-token prompt** (`"hi"`, `[9707]` with Qwen3-0.6B): the first prompt token is never scored, so a one-token prompt gets no prompt logprobs even on a normal completion. Non-streaming echo with generated tokens returned 500 (`echoed completion logprobs require prompt logprobs but generation returned none`, reproduced on GB200); it now returns the token with a `null` logprob.
- The `prompt_logprobs` field is `[null]` when no prompt logprobs arrived, like Python (shared with chat, which gets the same fix for a request that ends during prefill). An output without generated tokens reports empty logprobs instead of failing; generated tokens without logprobs still fail, now also when echoed.
- Streaming still ends with the engine's error alone when the first update fails, as in Python, which raises before echoing.

## Validation

On head `3f59b3516e` (base `main` `93873e7aca`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [  19.072s] 2928 tests run: 2928 passed, 13 skipped`

Tests, ported from `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py` (in-process, not server-level) plus router-level checks:

- `completions_echo_logprobs_of_request_aborted_during_prefill` (router; a mock engine finishes the request as aborted with no tokens and no prompt logprobs, streaming and non-streaming): 200, `["H", "i", "!"]` with `null` logprobs, `finish_reason: "abort"`, no error frame, and non-streaming `prompt_logprobs: [null]`.
- `collect_completion_pads_echoed_prompt_logprobs_of_request_aborted_mid_prefill` and `completion_chunk_stream_pads_echoed_prompt_logprobs_of_request_aborted_mid_prefill` (Python's `test_echo_logprobs_of_request_aborted_mid_prefill` and `test_stream_echo_logprobs_of_request_aborted_mid_prefill`, same `[9, 1, 2, 3]` prompt with `return_tokens_as_token_ids`).
- `collect_completion_echoes_single_token_prompt_logprobs_with_generated_tokens`: one-token prompt plus a generated token, `[null, -0.5]`.
- `collect_completion_rejects_echoed_generated_tokens_without_logprobs`: echo no longer hides a generated token's missing logprobs.
- `engine_request_errors_map_to_http_status` checks that every streamed completions error case starts with the error frame, with two new cases (echo without `logprobs`; echo with string-form `logprobs` of a prompt token the tokenizer cannot decode).
- `completion_chunk_stream_rejects_missing_prompt_logprobs` is removed: it pinned the 500 this PR replaces.

Red-green: making the no-prompt-logprobs branch fail again fails the padding and one-token tests; sending the prompt chunk before its update fails the error-route test; dropping the `[null]` fails the router abort test; and `main` fails all new tests.

## Details

**Change.** `echoed_prompt_logprobs_to_openai` gives every prompt token an entry when the engine sent no prompt logprobs: a `null` logprob and `top_logprobs`, and the token decoded on its own (`tokenizer.decode(&[id], false)`, like Python's `_create_completion_logprobs`), or `token_id:<id>` with `return_tokens_as_token_ids`. Non-streaming echo builds its prompt part through the same function, so the old one-token special case, which used the prompt text as the token, is gone. `collected_logprobs_to_openai` loses its offset argument, which was always 0 without echo.

**Streaming order.** Streaming used to defer a missing-prompt-logprobs error (vllm-project/vllm#55399); that error is gone, so to keep what the deferral gave, the chunk built from the first update's prompt (the echo, or `prompt_token_ids`) is sent together with that update's text. An engine error on the first update therefore ends the stream alone, now also without `logprobs`, where Rust used to send the echo first. The text layer yields the start and the first delta back to back, so this adds no latency.

**Layering.** The padding is completions-echo policy (Python applies it only there), so it lives in the completions route next to the existing echo rendering; the separate `prompt_logprobs` field keeps Python's unpadded `[null]`, and raw generate is unchanged.

**Limitations.** Chat with `logprobs: true` and `/inference/v1/generate` with `prompt_logprobs` still return 500 for a request aborted during prefill; that is a separate change. A Tekken-only checkpoint cannot decode a byte-fallback token on its own, so padding a prompt with such a token fails; the first prompt token already goes through the same isolated decode on every echo today. Python's partial case (logprobs for only some prompt tokens) does not arise in Rust, which takes the prompt logprobs from the first output carrying them.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#68909 and #68488 change other parts of completions logprobs (the echoed `top_logprobs` width and colliding `top_logprobs` keys); no open PR handles missing prompt logprobs.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex in three rounds (final verdict approve with nits): the `prompt_logprobs` field still returning 500, the echo chunk preceding a first-update engine error, and the echo branch hiding missing generated logprobs were fixed; the Tekken-only limitation above was accepted. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] keep the prompt prefix cacheable in agent workloads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**goal:** document how agent apps keep vllm's prefix cache hitting when they shrink context (closes #63741).

**context:** dropping or rewriting an early message changes the hash of every later block, so only the system prompt still hits: 9% vs 99% in the setup below.

## Claims

- new section "keeping the prefix cacheable" in `docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md`: what breaks the prefix, how to compact without losing it, how to measure the hit rate.
- docs only.

## Validation

the section's numbers: 1x a100, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, vllm main 4527515cd, a synthetic 16-turn conversation then one follow-up, prefix cache reset before each, 3 runs (hit rates identical; ttft median):

| follow-up | prompt tokens | prefix cache hit | ttft |
|---|---|---|---|
| conversation unchanged | 15,607 | 99.2% | 0.11 s |
| oldest turn dropped | 14,722 | 9.0% | 1.27 s |

pre-commit passes. preview: https://vllm--66683.org.readthedocs.build/en/66683/

re-checked against main 28fb136: both linked pages, the `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` / `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` counters (tokens), `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and `/v1/responses` `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` are unchanged; the pr merges cleanly.

<details>
<summary>repro script</summary>

```python
"""Repro for vllm-project/vllm#63741: agent context compaction vs automatic prefix caching.

Sends one long agent conversation to a running `vllm serve`, then a follow-up request built two ways:
  dropped:   an early message is removed (what many compaction schemes do) -> prefix shifts
  identical: the prefix is kept token-identical and the new content is appended
For each, reports prefix-cache hit rate (from /metrics counter deltas) and TTFT.
Needs the server started with VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 (for /reset_prefix_cache).
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
import urllib.request

WORDS = ("alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa lambda mu nu xi omicron pi rho "
         "sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega").split()


def text(seed: int, n_words: int) -> str:
    return " ".join(WORDS[(seed * 7 + i * 13) % len(WORDS)] + str((seed + i) % 97) for i in range(n_words))


def metrics(base: str) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for line in urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}/metrics").read().decode().splitlines():
        for key in ("vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total", "vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total"):
            if line.startswith(key):
                out[key] = out.get(key, 0.0) + float(line.rsplit(" ", 1)[1])
    return out


def post(base: str, path: str, body: dict | None = None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}{path}", data=json.dumps(body or {}).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req)


def chat(base: str, model: str, messages: list) -> float:
    """Streams one chat completion; returns time to first token in seconds."""
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = post(base, "/v1/chat/completions",
                {"model": model, "messages": messages, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0, "stream": True})
    for raw in resp:
        line = raw.decode().strip()
        if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]" and json.loads(line[6:])["choices"][0]["delta"].get("content"):
            ttft = time.perf_counter() - t0
            for _ in resp:  # drain
                pass
            return ttft
    return time.perf_counter() - t0


def measure(base: str, model: str, warm: list, follow: list) -> tuple[float, float]:
    post(base, "/reset_prefix_cache")
    chat(base, model, warm)
    m0 = metrics(base)
    ttft = chat(base, model, follow)
    m1 = metrics(base)
    q = m1["vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total"] - m0["vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total"]
    h = m1["vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total"] - m0["vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total"]
    return (h / q if q else 0.0), ttft


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:8000")
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--turns", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--words-per-turn", type=int, default=200)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    system = {"role": "system", "content": "you are a coding agent. " + text(0, 600)}
    history = []
    for t in range(a.turns):
        history.append({"role": "user", "content": f"turn {t}: " + text(2 * t + 1, a.words_per_turn)})
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": f"result {t}: " + text(2 * t + 2, a.words_per_turn)})
    new_msg = {"role": "user", "content": "next step: " + text(999, 50)}

    warm = [system] + history
    dropped = [system] + history[2:] + [new_msg]   # compaction drops the oldest turn pair
    identical = [system] + history + [new_msg]     # prefix unchanged, new content appended

    for name, follow in (("identical prefix", identical), ("early message dropped", dropped)):
        hit, ttft = measure(a.base, a.model, warm, follow)
        print(f"{name:24s} prefix cache hit {hit:6.1%}   ttft {ttft * 1000:8.1f} ms")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

- not a duplicate: no pr references #63741. #65962 edits the same file without overlap.
- ai-assisted (metamate). i reviewed every line and ran the repro.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Export `vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads` from the Rust frontend's `/metrics`, as the Python frontend does since vllm-project/vllm#66011. The Rust NIXL decoder has no such field, so serde drops it and the family is missing.

## Claims

- `NixlStats` decodes `num_declined_expired_reads` (`#[serde(default)]`, like `num_notifications_after_expiry`).
- `vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads` is exported with Python's name and help text, incremented by the sum of the reported list, next to `vllm:nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry`.

## Validation

On head `b28ae4ff2a` (base `main` `93873e7aca`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [  18.705s] 2924 tests run: 2924 passed, 13 skipped`

- `kv_connector_series_appear_on_first_report` (`vllm-metrics`) renders the new series from a NIXL payload, and `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` (`vllm-engine-core-client`) decodes the field from a Python-encoded NIXL payload and checks the exported counter. Red-green: with the counter increment removed, both tests fail.
- Python's tests for the field are connector unit tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_remote_read_expiry.py`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_multi_connector.py`); no server-level test covers it.

## Details

**What the counter means.** Remote KV reads the consumer declined, or completed reads it discarded, because it could no longer trust the producer's KV lease: the read would fall within the lease's safety margin (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py`).

**Layering.** The NIXL module (`rust/src/metrics/src/scheduler/kv_connector/nixl.rs`) owns the payload, the families and the recording since vllm-project/vllm#68974; this adds one field and one counter there. The connector's log summary line (`Num declined expired reads`) is not mirrored: the Rust frontend has no per-connector log summary for NIXL.

**Help text.** `prometheus-client` appends a period to every help text, so the literal has none. The neighboring `vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` and `vllm:nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry` help texts end in a doubled period today; that is left to a separate change.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR exports this family from the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex (approve with nits, both fixed: the doubled help-text period and a description that overstated what the counter proves). I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Count vllm:num_preemptions from scheduler stats
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Count `vllm:num_preemptions` from the scheduler's `SchedulerStats.num_preempted_reqs`, as the Python frontend has since vllm-project/vllm#65317, instead of from `PREEMPTED` request events. Today a request preempted and then aborted is never counted by the Rust frontend, and every count lags until the preempted request resumes.

## Claims

- `SchedulerStats` decodes `num_preempted_reqs`, and `vllm:num_preemptions` is incremented from it. Name and help text are unchanged.
- `PREEMPTED` events now feed only the per-request `vllm:request_num_preemptions` histogram, as in Python (they still move a tracked LoRA request's adapter to the waiting set for `vllm:lora_requests_info`).
- The periodic log's `Preemptions` reads the same counter, so it gets the same fix.

## Validation

On head `4b141c7ba8` (base `main` `93873e7aca`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [   9.104s] 2924 tests run: 2924 passed, 13 skipped`

A first run, made while three other workspace builds ran on the same node, failed `vllm-engine-core-client` `tests::client::connect_times_out_without_ready_message` once; that test's handshake has a 50 ms engine delay against a 100 ms ready timeout, and this PR does not touch the handshake. Five isolated runs of the test and a full rerun of the suite alone passed.

- `generate_records_request_metrics_in_prometheus_output` (`rust/src/llm/tests/generate.rs`) now has the mock engine report `num_preempted_reqs: 2` in a stats-only batch while the request carries one `PREEMPTED` event: the counter reads 2 (from the scheduler) and the histogram sum stays 1 (from the event). 300 repeated runs passed. Red-green: with the events counting into the counter again and the decoded field unused, the test fails at the counter assertion (1 instead of 2).
- The Python tests that pin this (`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_preemption_of_aborted_request_is_counted`, `tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py::test_preemptions_and_corrupted_render`) are scheduler and logger unit tests; the server-level `test_metrics.py` only checks that the family exists, which it still does.

## Details

**Root cause.** Python's scheduler counts each preemption when it happens (only when stats are collected) and reports the count since the previous stats in `SchedulerStats.num_preempted_reqs`; `PrometheusStatLogger.record` and `LoggingStatLogger.record` read it there. The Rust `SchedulerStats` had no such field, so serde dropped it, and the counter was driven by `PREEMPTED` events, which reach the frontend only with the request's next output.

**Layering.** The counter's input is now a `SchedulerStats` core field, so the family moves from the request metrics (`vllm-metrics` `request.rs`) to the scheduler state group (`scheduler/state.rs`), which records the other core fields (`num_running_reqs`, `num_waiting_reqs`, ...) through `SchedulerStatsRecorder::record`. Per-engine series are created when the recorder resolves its handles, as for the other state metrics, and, as in Python, only when engine stats are enabled.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes how the Rust frontend counts preemptions.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex (changes needed: the test raced the dispatcher, which records a batch's scheduler stats after delivering its outputs; fixed by sending the stats in a stats-only batch before the final output). I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export OffloadingConnector KV offload metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Export the `OffloadingConnector` metrics (`vllm:kv_offload_*`, `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_*` and `vllm:kv_offload_config_info`) from the Rust frontend's `/metrics`, as the Python frontend does. Today the Rust frontend has typed decoders only for NIXL, Mooncake (transfer and store), UMBP and SimpleCPUOffload, so the offloading payload decodes as `KvConnectorStats::Multi` and is dropped: a Rust-frontend deployment with this connector shows none of its metrics. Addresses the `kv_offload` metrics item of vllm-project/vllm#68784.

## Claims

- **Commit 1, OffloadingConnector** (`OffloadingConnectorStats`): the connector's own families (`get_connector_metric_definitions`), the `CPUOffloadingSpec` families, the deprecated `vllm:kv_offload_{total_bytes,total_time,size}` families (`transfer_type` label) fed from the flat transfer families as Python does for CPU-derived specs, and `vllm:kv_offload_config_info`. Exported both for a bare `OffloadingConnector` and as a `MultiConnector` child.
- **Commit 2, TieringOffloadingSpec**: the 21 `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_*` families (`tier`, and `tier`+`result` for promotion latency). Definition rows only.
- **One Python change** (commit 1): `OffloadingConnectorStats.set_info` stringifies the config info values, as the Prometheus label values they become. The Python frontend already labels the series with `str()` of each value, so its `/metrics` output is unchanged, and the Rust frontend reads the same strings instead of reimplementing Python's `str()` for ints, floats and bools.

## Validation

On head `7f60c6ea58` (base `main` `9e8b3fb83e`), each of the two commits on its own:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

| Commit | nextest |
|---|---|
| `a95f31e1f5` OffloadingConnector | `Summary [  13.803s] 2925 tests run: 2925 passed, 13 skipped` |
| `7f60c6ea58` TieringOffloadingSpec | `Summary [   8.991s] 2925 tests run: 2925 passed, 13 skipped` |

- **Wire shape.** The Python msgpack fixture (`python_compat.py`, run by `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding`) now encodes a CPU-spec `OffloadingConnectorStats` payload with `info` (stringified, as `set_info` now sends it), bare and as a `MultiConnector` child. Before this PR it decoded as `Multi`; the test pins the decoded `OffloadingStats` and checks a rendered series.
- **Exposition.** A unit test in `kv_connector/offloading.rs` records the connector bare and as a `MultiConnector` child and snapshots the flat, deprecated, tiering, gauge-latest and `config_info` series; an unknown family and a sample with the wrong label count are dropped. Red-green: before each commit, its families are absent from the rendered output.
- **Python.**

  ```
  pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_metrics.py
  ============================= 39 passed in 12.23s ==============================
  ```

  Two `set_info`/`aggregate` tests now assert string values; they fail with the `set_info` change reverted.

No live server run: the change is the decoding and export of the engine's stats payload, and the Python msgpack fixture pins the wire shape.

## Details

**Layout.** Everything is one module, `vllm-metrics/src/scheduler/kv_connector/offloading.rs`, in the per-connector layout of vllm-project/vllm#68974: the payload decoder (`OffloadingStats`, re-exported from `protocol::stats`), the families and their recording. `engine-core-client` has no OffloadingConnector code. The payload is the same `types`/`data` envelope as SimpleCPUOffload plus `info`; its `KvConnectorStats` variant comes after `SimpleCpuOffload`, which requires `vllm:simple_kv_offload_used_blocks`.

**Table-driven families.** The families depend on the configured offloading spec, and Python declares them as metadata tables (`OffloadingMetricMetadata`) and keys the payload by metric name. `offloading.rs` mirrors those tables as one `DEFINITIONS` table, so each family reviews against its Python row, and records a payload by looking each metric name up in it. The alternative was a struct field and a registration per family for about 40 families. This connector is the only table-driven one because its payload is self-describing and its family set varies by spec; the other connectors' fixed payloads stay typed structs.

**Differences from Python.**

- **Unknown or malformed samples.** A family Rust does not define, a sample whose label count differs from its definition, or a sample of the wrong shape is dropped, where Python asserts. Families from specs or secondary tiers outside the built-in CPU and tiering specs are not exported.
- **`vllm:kv_offload_config_info` labels.** Python labels every series with the names the spec declares (`config_info_keys`), empty where a series fills none. Rust cannot see the spec, so it uses the names the series fill, sorted. The two agree unless a declared name is filled by no series, which Python warns about.
- **When series appear.** Python creates the deprecated `transfer_type` series per engine at startup; Rust creates them on the first transfer, like the flat families.
- **Registration.** As for the other connectors, the families are registered whatever connector is configured; their series appear once the connector reports.
- **Number formatting.** The counters are float counters, as Python sums ints and floats into them.

**Size.** About 600 production lines, about 300 of them declarative: the definition rows and bucket edges, with help strings copied verbatim from Python (minus the final period, which `prometheus-client` appends). Roughly 450 in commit 1 and 150 (rows only) in commit 2, which can be dropped on its own.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR exports these families from the Rust frontend's typed decoders. vllm-project/vllm#58563 (draft) takes a different route, a Python-side metrics descriptor for connectors Rust has no code for. vllm-project/vllm#60038 initializes offload gauges at startup on the Python engine side and does not overlap.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex (approve with nits: it matched all 35 offloading definition rows against Python's name, kind, HELP, labels and buckets, and probed MessagePack-to-exposition on both dispatch paths, red on base and green on head). I reviewed every changed line.
