commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Score the sparse-indexer prefill on ShardQ token slices
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, let the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-indexer prefill follow `sparse_mla_shard_q` (#63956): each TP rank scores only its ShardQ slice of the prefill tokens, including the two-level candidate layers (the candidate source and its consumers), and the ranks all-gather the int32 top-k back into token order. Attention stays head-sharded. #63956 does not reach DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, whose attention does not go through `MLAAttention`, so after it DeepSeek-V4.1 has no prefill-indexer sharding on either platform; this restores it on ROCm on top of ShardQ's split instead of the removed row sharding.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, single-prompt TTFT at 1M: −20% at TP4 and −9% at TP2 on the recipe configuration (MXFP4 indexer cache, `indexer_sparse_logits`); −48% at TP4 with the FP8 indexer cache and `--no-swa-bounded-replay`, where the candidate layers index every prefill row.
- Accuracy unchanged (GSM8K, passkey).
- Follows upstream's defaults (`sparse_mla_shard_q=True`, `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens=1024`); `sparse_mla_shard_q=false` restores the replicated indexer. CUDA behavior is unchanged.
- On the InferenceX AgentX TP2 recipe (concurrency 1–64) serving metrics show no resolved difference between on and off.

## Validation

MI355X, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, DSpark (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, prefix caching off; image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly with this branch's `vllm/` on top. Arm "off" is `sparse_mla_shard_q=false`, arm "on" the default. TTFT: one random-token prompt, `max_tokens=1`, median of 3 (spread < 0.5% on the 256K and 1M rows). The TP4 recipe and FP8 rows and their GSM8K are on the current base, which also shards the MXFP4 indexer's decode rows (#66047) and skips repeated K gathers in the FP8 prefill loop (#63878); the TP2, no-spec and passkey rows are from an earlier base. The 2K–128K rows are medians of 22 runs per arm at this head, the two arms running side by side on four GPUs each and swapping GPU sets halfway (the sets differ by up to 10 ms at 2K/4K, more than the arms do); the split breaks even around 32K and pays from 64K.

| Config | Prompt | off | on | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, MXFP4 + sparse logits (recipe) | 256K | 3.451 s | 3.274 s | −5.1% |
| | 1M | 17.20 s | 13.82 s | −19.7% |
| TP2, MXFP4 + sparse logits (recipe) | 256K | 5.532 s | 5.406 s | −2.3% |
| | 1M | 25.63 s | 23.35 s | −8.9% |
| TP4, FP8 indexer cache, `--no-swa-bounded-replay` | 256K | 8.258 s | 6.621 s | −19.8% |
| | 1M | 66.59 s | 34.89 s | −47.6% |
| TP4, MXFP4 + sparse logits (recipe) | 2K / 4K / 8K / 16K | 0.096 / 0.090 / 0.115 / 0.209 s | 0.094 / 0.090 / 0.116 / 0.209 s | within ±1 ms from 4K; 2K within GPU-set jitter |
| | 32K / 64K / 128K | 0.398 / 0.797 / 1.619 s | 0.396 / 0.787 / 1.577 s | −0.5% / −1.3% / −2.6% |
| TP4, MXFP4 + sparse logits, no spec decode | 1M | 17.27 s | 13.77 s | −20.3% |

Batched short prompts (closed loop, `--max-num-seqs 32`, 13–30 requests of 520–1250 tokens filling a 16K-token step): throughput on vs off is within the ±10% run-to-run variation, with no consistent sign.

With bounded SWA replay (the CDNA4 default) layers 21–39 prefill only each request's last 128 tokens, so most of the gain comes from the ratio-2 indexers; without it the candidate source and consumers are sharded too.

**Serving (InferenceX AgentX, TP2).** `infx.bench agentic` (`cc-traces-weka-062126`, 900 s per point) on the `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp` TP2 recipe with its per-concurrency overrides, a fresh server per point, prefix caching on. Both arms run this branch on the `nightly-rocm100-eff4de9be3` image and differ only in `sparse_mla_shard_q`. Four servers run side by side, two per arm, and the arms swap GPU pairs between rounds. Means over the servers of an arm, off → on:

| conc | servers per arm | output tok/s | TTFT mean / P50 / P90 (s) | TPOT mean (ms) |
|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | 140.6 → 141.0 (+0.3%) | 0.688 / 0.174 / 1.416 → 0.680 / 0.172 / 1.441 | 1.865 → 1.857 |
| 2 | 6 | 215.5 → 215.0 (−0.2%) | 0.888 / 0.169 / 1.464 → 0.921 / 0.165 / 1.453 | 1.837 → 1.835 |
| 4 | 6 | 244.6 → 245.4 (+0.3%) | 1.428 / 0.124 / 4.190 → 1.388 / 0.120 / 4.585 | 1.870 → 1.845 |
| 8 | 4 | 425.6 → 420.8 (−1.1%) | 0.719 / 0.133 / 2.115 → 0.769 / 0.128 / 2.118 | 2.277 → 2.260 |
| 16 | 4 | 671.9 → 673.4 (+0.2%) | 2.104 / 0.684 / 5.984 → 2.150 / 0.779 / 6.012 | 3.410 → 3.433 |
| 32 | 4 | 1280 → 1284 (+0.3%) | 7.122 / 7.714 / 14.97 → 7.061 / 7.320 / 15.17 | 5.965 → 5.873 |
| 64 | 4 | 2197 → 2218 (+1.0%) | 0.371 / 0.149 / 0.734 → 0.370 / 0.150 / 0.767 | 12.36 → 12.45 |

No difference is resolved: output throughput is within ±1.2% at every concurrency, and every on-arm mean lies inside the range of the off-arm servers, which is wide for the latency tails (TTFT P90 at c4 is 2.4–6.7 s across the six off servers). TTFT P90 is higher with the split in six of the seven rows (+0.1% to +9.4%), inside that spread. Requests average 107K–171K input tokens depending on concurrency, at a 96% prefix-cache hit rate, so this workload rarely prefills the long cold prompts where the split pays (table above).

**Accuracy** (sharding engaged: up to 64 batched requests per step):

| Config | GSM8K, 1319 q, chat, thinking off (off → on) | passkey 256K, 6 depths (off → on) |
|---|---|---|
| TP4, MXFP4 | 0.975 → 0.971 | 6/6 → 6/6 |
| TP4, MXFP4, no spec decode | 0.971 → 0.974 | — |
| TP4, FP8, no replay | 0.974 → 0.970 | 6/6 → 6/6 |
| TP2, MXFP4 | 0.973 → 0.970 | — |

**Stability.**
- 2 × 8 consecutive 1M prompts with ShardQ on (TP4, FP8, no replay), on the node where the pre-#66052 builder hung most often: 16/16.
- A short chunked-prefill tail (2–7 tokens) scheduled ahead of another long prompt, no spec decode, so the short request has no tokens on some ranks: 12/12 at TP4 for MXFP4 and FP8, ShardQ on and off.

**Tests** (MI355X, one GPU playing every rank):
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv41_indexer_shardq.py` (new, FP8 op) and `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py::test_prefill_shardq_split_matches_replicated` (new, MXFP4 dense and gather): each rank of a 2- and 4-way zigzag split, over a multi-chunk prefill whose rank slices cut requests and chunks, runs the ratio-2 layer, the candidate source and a consumer whose candidate rows of other ranks hold junk. Each rank's rows must select what the replicated run selects (as sets: the top-k order within a row depends on the batch shape), and after the exchange the whole buffer must match.
  The MXFP4 test's first request has 2 tokens, so at 4 ways some ranks hold none of it.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py::test_prefill_plans_on_shardq_query_ranges` (new, CPU): `RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadataBuilder.build` plans the chunks on the renumbered query ranges, for a rank that holds none of the first request.
- Existing `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py` and `tests/v1/attention/test_shardq.py` pass.

## Details

- **Gate.** `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` marks its indexer K cache `use_shardq` and `gather_shardq_topk` when `sparse_mla_shard_q` is on, TP > 1, without DCP/PCP or a FULL mixed CUDA graph. The shared indexer builder then builds the ShardQ split, gather indices, per-token positions and renumbered query ranges as it does for CUDA.
- **Indexer ops.** The FP8 op (`rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`) and the MXFP4 ops gather q (and the MXFP4 scales) and weights by `shardq_gather_indices`; the MXFP4 builder plans on the renumbered query ranges. After the prefill loop `exchange_shardq_topk` all-gathers each rank's compact top-k rows and `index_copy_`s them into token order, only for layers marked `gather_shardq_topk`: other models on the FP8 op (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5) keep upstream's compact top-k for a token-sharded attention. The builder keeps the split and the renumbered ranges (host-side only) on the prefill metadata for this.
- **Chunk planning.** A short request can have no tokens on a rank, which makes the renumbered query ranges ambiguous at a chunk boundary, so the MXFP4 builder takes each chunk's first request from the new `req_start` on the chunk metadata instead of locating it in the ranges.
- **Candidate layers.** The source (layer 20) writes its candidate rows in the rank's compact order and its consumers (24/28/32/36) read them in the same order, so candidates are never exchanged.
- **Why not full ShardQ.** ROCm sparse MLA does not pad heads, so token-sharding attention would mainly add two q/out all-to-alls per compressed layer (RCCL; symmetric memory is CUDA-only), far more traffic than the top-k exchange. That is left for a follow-up measured against this.
- **Memory.** For sharded layers the profiling run reserves the gathered indexer inputs and a top-k-buffer-sized gather, held together.
- **Relation to #56944.** #56944 shards the FP8 op's prefill rows on ROCm with its own row split and an AllReduce(MAX) of the top-k, and keeps candidate-block layers and the MXFP4 indexer replicated. This PR uses the ShardQ split that #63956 introduced (it postdates #56944) and also covers DeepSeek-V4.1's candidate layers and the MXFP4 path (the recipe default). Both change the FP8 op's prefill loop, so only one design should land there.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Bump FlashKDA to a32181e (codegen opts + 132→9 variant pruning)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bump [`vllm-project/FlashKDA`](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA) from `9d9e928` to `a32181e` ([FlashKDA#17](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/17) + [FlashKDA#18](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/18)) and update vLLM's `_flashkda_C.fwd` registration and call sites for the reordered required `cu_seqlens` argument.

## Claims

- **4.4× faster 3-arch build & -23% extension size** ([FlashKDA#18](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/18)): prunes FlashKDA's compiled kernel matrix from **132 → 9 kernels per architecture** (`396 → 27` across `sm_90a`, `sm_100f`, `sm_120f`).
- **+6.8% to +9.8% geomean kernel speedup on GB300, +8.7% on H200, +7.8% on SM120** ([FlashKDA#17](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/17)): 128B-swizzled TMA layouts, vectorized FP32↔BF16 state conversion, reduced K2 spills, SM100+ `FFMA2`, and V-split occupancy cleanup (bitwise-identical outputs).
- **Backward-compatible precompiled wheel calls:** `kimi_k3` and `glm5next` pass `cu_seqlens`, `initial_state`, `final_state`, `checkpoint_state`, and `checkpoint_offsets` by keyword so `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` editable installs work with both the old and new schemas.

## Validation

Tested on commit `10e8b0b8d1` (`_flashkda_C` built from source against `a32181e` on NVIDIA GB300, `sm_100f`, CUDA 13.0):

1. **Unit tests (1× NVIDIA GB300):**
   ```bash
   pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -k flashkda -x -q
   # 5 passed, 110 deselected in 7.30s

   pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -k flashkda -x -q
   # 12 passed, 16 deselected in 13.43s
   ```
2. **End-to-end serving accuracy smoke (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, 4× NVIDIA GB300, TP4 + EP):**
   ```bash
   vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --port 8000 -tp 4 -ep \
     --enable-ep-weight-filter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
     --additional-config '{"kda_prefill_backend":"flashkda"}'
   ```
   - GSM8K (5-shot, `v1/completions`, `temperature=0.0`, `max_tokens=4096`, `n=1319`, `0` request errors, `57.18s`): **`0.9333` (`93.33%`)** exact match (strict & flexible).

## Details

- `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`: bump `GIT_TAG` to `a32181e2efebb75d500912a53a98b8b2a6866e03`.
- `csrc/flashkda_registration.cpp`: move required `Tensor cu_seqlens` right after `lower_bound` (before optional `initial_state` / `final_state`) to match FlashKDA#18's C++ signature.
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py` & `vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`: pass `cu_seqlens`, `initial_state`, `final_state`, `checkpoint_state`, and `checkpoint_offsets` by keyword (all vLLM callers already supply contiguous `int32` `cu_seqlens` and `checkpoint_offsets`).
- **Trade-offs / limitations:** FlashKDA#18 makes `has_state_in` and `has_state_out` runtime booleans; calls without `final_state` are slightly slower on SM90, which does not affect vLLM serving (all vLLM KDA prefill callers pass `final_state`).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Align CUDA graph capture input_ids and inputs_embeds with execute_model
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Align `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture()` with `GPUModelRunner.execute_model()` so CUDA graph capture passes the exact same `input_ids`, `inputs_embeds`, and `model_inputs` key ordering as runtime replay on the first PP rank.

Fixes #68870.

> **Note on existing PR #63733:** Previously open PR #63733 attempted a related fix. Rather than duplicating #63733, this PR resolves #68870 with a cleaner, less invasive design: zero modifications to `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, no new parameter on `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture()`, a single `dummy_inputs_embeds()` call per capture descriptor, exact `model_inputs` dict ordering and override parity with `execute_model()`, symmetric `DefaultModelState.prepare_dummy_inputs()`, and an end-to-end `LLM` regression test.

## Claims

- When `supports_multimodal_inputs` or `enable_prompt_embeds` is enabled on the first PP rank and `model_state.dummy_inputs_embeds(num_tokens)` returns a tensor while `not requires_raw_input_tokens(model)`, `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture()` sets `input_ids=None` alongside `inputs_embeds`, matching `GPUModelRunner.execute_model()`.
- `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._replay()` under `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` no longer fails with `AssertionError: Input tensor addresses changed between capture and replay` (3 capture tensor args vs 2 replay tensor args) for multimodal models (e.g. Qwen3.5) or `--enable-prompt-embeds` models.
- Non-first PP ranks, models with `requires_raw_input_tokens=True`, text-only models without prompt embeds, and `ModelState` subclasses that return `dummy_inputs_embeds() -> None` and supply `inputs_embeds` via `prepare_dummy_inputs()` (`DiffusionGemmaModelState`, `LongcatNgramModelState`) preserve their exact `execute_model()` input contract.
- Greedy decoding outputs on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` (BF16) under `INFO` logging remain bit-identical before and after the fix.

## Validation

- **Base commit:** `ddcf64b36f` (`upstream/main`)
- **PR commit:** `28b5ba64674973c539b79141b4c9a36aa7250ba8`
- **Hardware / Env:** Single NVIDIA H20-3e (141GB), PyTorch `2.14.0+cu132`, CUDA `13.2`
- **AI Assistance:** AI assistance (Antigravity) was used to investigate the root cause, write the fix and tests, and run the validations below.

### 3. Issue #68870 Reproduction (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` BF16 on NVIDIA H20-3e)

Model `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`. The repro script runs 1 single prompt (`max_tokens=1, temperature=0.0, logprobs=1, prompt_logprobs=1`) followed by a batch of 16 prompts (`max_tokens=32, temperature=0.0`).

- **Before fix (`ddcf64b36f`), `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`:** Failed on the first `llm.generate()` call (`DEBUG_EXIT=1`) with:
  ```text
  (EngineCore pid=1913928) ERROR 11-25 11:05:38 [v1/engine/core.py:1766] AssertionError: Input tensor addresses changed between capture and replay for BatchDescriptor(num_tokens=24, num_reqs=None, uniform=False, num_active_loras=0). Expected [140640373460992, 140640374584320, 140637093494784], got [140640374584320, 140637093494784].
  ```
- **Before fix (`ddcf64b36f`), `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO`:** Completed cleanly (`INFO_EXIT=0`, `REPRO_OK`).
- **After fix (`28b5ba64674973c539b79141b4c9a36aa7250ba8`), `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`:** Completed cleanly (`QWEN_DEBUG_EXIT=0`, `REPRO_OK`), no `AssertionError`.
- **After fix (`28b5ba64674973c539b79141b4c9a36aa7250ba8`), `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO`:** Completed cleanly (`QWEN_INFO_EXIT=0`, `REPRO_OK`).
- **Output equivalence vs pre-fix `INFO` baseline:**
  - `postfix_info` vs `prefix_info`: **17/17 prompts identical** (both text and token IDs).
  - `postfix_debug` vs `prefix_info`: 16/17 identical; `batch[1]` (`"Explain why the sky is blue in one sentence:"`) shifted at token 17 (`"shorter blue wavelengths of light more effectively..."` vs `"shorter wavelengths of light (blue) more effectively..."`) due to expected non-batch-invariant floating-point differences across async IPC batching steps under heavy `DEBUG` logging overhead.

### 4. Linters and static checks

All `pre-commit` hooks (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `check-test-tethering`, `mypy`, SPDX headers, root lazy imports, docstring style, `signoff-commit`) passed on commit `28b5ba64674973c539b79141b4c9a36aa7250ba8`.

## Details

### Root Cause

1. In `GPUModelRunner.execute_model()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`), when `self.uses_inputs_embeds and self.is_first_pp_rank`, the runner calls `self.model_state.dummy_inputs_embeds(...)` (for dummy runs) or `prepare_inputs_embeds(...)` (for real batches). If `inputs_embeds is not None` and `not requires_raw_input_tokens(self.model)`, it sets `input_ids = None` before constructing `model_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids, "positions": ..., "inputs_embeds": inputs_embeds, "intermediate_tensors": None, **self.model_state.prepare_inputs(...)}`.
2. In `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), capture previously always populated `"input_ids": input_buffers.input_ids[:num_tokens]` without `"inputs_embeds"` in the base dictionary, and relied on `DefaultModelState.prepare_dummy_inputs()` to insert `"inputs_embeds"`. As a result, capture passed both `input_ids` and `inputs_embeds` (3 tensor arguments instead of 2) and placed `"inputs_embeds"` after `"intermediate_tensors"`.
3. `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._capture()` records `entry.input_addresses = self._collect_tensor_addresses(args, kwargs)`, and `_replay()` asserts `new_addresses == entry.input_addresses` whenever `logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)` is true, crashing on the first breakable PIECEWISE replay.

### Implementation & Design Comparison

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`: `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture()` reads `uses_inputs_embeds = model_config.supports_multimodal_inputs or model_config.enable_prompt_embeds` from `self.vllm_config.model_config` (already stored on `CudaGraphManager`) and replicates `execute_model()`'s first-PP-rank `input_ids` / `inputs_embeds` selection and exact `model_inputs` dict order before unpacking `**model_state.prepare_dummy_inputs(num_reqs, num_tokens)`.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py`: `DefaultModelState.prepare_dummy_inputs()` is simplified to only provide `"positions"` when `self.rope_state is not None`, symmetrical with `DefaultModelState.prepare_inputs()`.
- **Compatibility across `ModelState` variants:**
  - `DefaultModelState` / `MambaHybridModelState` (MM or `enable_prompt_embeds`): `dummy_inputs_embeds()` returns buffer; `input_ids` is cleared unless `requires_raw_input_tokens(model)` is `True`.
  - Raw-token VL models (`requires_raw_input_tokens = True`, e.g., `DeepseekV41ModelState`, `Qwen4ExpModelState`, `HYV4` VL): keep both `input_ids` and `inputs_embeds`.
  - `DiffusionGemmaModelState` (`dummy_inputs_embeds() -> None`, self-supplies `inputs_embeds` in `prepare_dummy_inputs()`): `inputs_embeds` overrides `None` in dict unpacking and `input_ids` stays non-None, matching `execute_model()`.
  - `LongcatNgramModelState` (text-only `uses_inputs_embeds=False`, self-supplies `inputs_embeds` in `prepare_dummy_inputs()`): `dummy_inputs_embeds()` is not called and `input_ids` stays non-None.
  - `EncoderDecoderModelState` (`dummy_inputs_embeds() -> None`): `input_ids` stays non-None, `inputs_embeds` stays `None`.
  - Non-first PP ranks: `if not self.is_first_pp_rank:` clears `input_ids` (unless `requires_raw_input_tokens`) and `inputs_embeds`, and sets `intermediate_tensors`, matching `execute_model()`.
  - DBO (`desc.num_ubatches > 1`): `model_inputs` is built identically before `ubatch_runner.prepare()` and `begin_capturable_run()`.
- **CI Coverage:** `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py` runs in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (`cpu-small`); `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_mode.py` and `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py` run in `.buildkite/test_areas/cuda.yaml` (`cudagraph`).

commits.pr_title: [Model] Enable data-parallel multimodal encoder for HY4
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose

Enable the existing `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` for HY4 VL and HY4-Flash VL. The vision tower already builds with replicated weights in this mode (`disable_tp=use_dp`), but the wrapper neither advertised `supports_encoder_tp_data` nor sharded media items, so the mode was rejected and fell back to `weights`.

- Eager path: whole media items are load-balanced across TP ranks by patch count, each rank encodes only its share with the replicated tower, and one padded all-gather restores per-item embeddings in the original order on every rank.
- Per-item output rows follow `vision_token_count` (merger newline/extra tokens, video temporal pooling), which the generic `run_dp_sharded_mrope_vision_model` contract cannot express — hence a HY4-specific sharding helper, mirroring DeepSeek-VL's per-family helper.
- Empty ranks all-gather placeholders in the tower's parameter dtype (`visual.dtype`, the patch-embedding weight dtype for HYV4; the tower is homogeneous-dtype, so this equals its output dtype — runtime-verified below). A tower with split dtypes would need its merger's weight dtype instead (cf. DeepSeek-VL's `aligner.w2.weight.dtype`).
- Encoder CUDA graph path: no code change needed; `EncoderCudaGraphManager` handles the mode generically (both replay and eager fallback verified below).
- The `weights` path is unchanged whenever the vision tower is TP-shardable. `is_vit_use_data_parallel()` also returns True when the vision heads are not divisible by the TP size (tower already built replicated in that case, via `disable_tp`); with this change such configurations now take the sharded path instead of every rank redundantly encoding the full batch. For HY4/HY4-Flash (vision heads = 16, LLM heads = 64/32), every TP size that can shard the LLM (2, 4, 8, 16) also divides the vision heads, so this branch is unreachable for those configurations and first triggers at TP = 32 (the LLM still shards, the vision heads do not), exercising the same sharded path validated below.

### Test Plan

- Local focused tests (not included in the submitted diff or Buildkite CI): capability advertisement (fails before this change), TP2/TP4 sharding with original-order restore, content-tagged per-item outputs (a rank encoding the wrong item's pixels fails the test), variable output rows (extra/newline tokens, video temporal pooling), empty-rank placeholder dtype.
- Real-weight E2E on H200 with greedy visual probes whose answers depend on image content (digits/colors), for both HY4-Flash VL (TP4) and HY4 VL base (TP8).
- Real-encoder embedding parity, weights vs data: rank-0 dumps of the per-item tower outputs for identical inputs (single image with empty ranks, heterogeneous 4-image and 6-image batches, three real MP4 videos with distinct grids incl. a two-video prompt), compared as max abs error / cosine similarity in fp32; real tower output lengths checked against `vision_token_count` per item in both modes.
- Encoder CUDA graph mode (`data` + `cudagraph_mm_encoder`): capture + 100% replay run, and a forced-miss run (capture budget 96 < 110 rows of the smallest probe image) exercising the eager fallback.
- Bounded eager A/B for both models, distinct images per request (encoder cache cold).

### Test Result

All runs on H200, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The original validation used the nightly wheel at `f2f9edcac` (parent of the original base commit `14e9c30d`) plus this change overlaid. After rebasing onto `b3bad87eb1` (hy_v4 was restructured into `common/` by the ROCm enablement in between), the focused tests were re-run on the exact new-baseline wheel (`0.34.1rc1.dev77+gb3bad87eb`) with the rebased change overlaid: `3 passed in 63s`.

- Local focused tests (subsequently removed from the PR): `3 passed` (TP2 empty-rank + reorder; TP4 uneven + video pooling + empty ranks).
- **HY4-Flash VL** (FP8 checkpoint), TP4: probes weights 5/5, data 5/5, all final answers identical across modes.
- **HY4 VL base** (FP8 checkpoint), TP8: probes weights 5/5, data 5/5, all final answers identical across modes (6-image prompts exercise empty ranks).
- **Real-encoder embedding parity** (rank-0 tower outputs, weights vs data, fp32): 6/6 structural cases PASS per model. Real tower output rows equal `vision_token_count` for every item in both modes; output dtype equals the tower parameter dtype in both modes. Numeric parity: HY4-Flash VL max abs err ≤ 0.50, cosine ≥ 0.9994; HY4 VL max abs err ≤ 0.65, cosine ≥ 0.9916. Cases cover single image (empty ranks at TP4/TP8), 4- and 6-image heterogeneous batches, and real MP4 videos with grids `[13,28,28]`, `[8,20,20]` and a `[4,28,28]+[6,32,32]` two-video prompt (temporal pooling executed by the real tower).
- **Encoder CUDA graphs** (HY4-Flash VL, TP4, `data`): manager init `use_dp=True` on all ranks; default budgets → 72 graphs captured, probes 5/5 with identical answers, 100 distinct-image requests → `hits=100, misses=0, hit_rate=100.0%`. Forced-miss run (`encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget=96`, 6 graphs captured): 100 distinct-image requests → `hits=0, misses=100, hit_rate=0.0%` — every request took the eager fallback under DP, no hang, probes still 5/5.
- **Bounded eager A/B** (max_tokens=8, 8–32 requests per case, encoder CUDA graphs off; flash at TP4, base at TP8). Case design — A: 1 image per request, the worst case for `data` (the encoder runs on one rank, TP−1 ranks idle for it); B: 4 images per request, the basic fan-out; C: images per request equal to the TP size, the balanced one-image-per-rank assignment with no empty ranks (coincides with B at TP4, distinct only in the TP8 run); D/E: the same single-/multi-image shapes at 16 concurrent clients. Every request uses distinct images so the encoder cache stays cold.

**HY4-Flash VL**, TP4:

| case | imgs/req | conc | TTFT p50, weights→data (ms) | TTFT p95, weights→data (ms) | req/s, weights→data |
|------|----------|------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------|
| A | 1 | 1 | 263→252 (−4.2%) | 269→256 (−4.8%) | 3.16→3.28 (+3.8%) |
| B | 4 | 1 | 272→274 (+0.7%) | 329→360 (+9.4%) | 3.06→2.82 (−7.8%) |
| C | 4 | 1 | 232→233 (+0.4%) | 234→266 (+13.7%) | 3.51→3.39 (−3.4%) |
| D | 1 | 16 | 534→427 (−20.0%) | 580→587 (+1.2%) | 25.5→27.8 (+9.0%) |
| E | 4 | 16 | 712→716 (+0.6%) | 943→850 (−9.9%) | 15.8→18.1 (+14.6%) |

**HY4 VL base**, TP8:

| case | imgs/req | conc | TTFT p50, weights→data (ms) | TTFT p95, weights→data (ms) | req/s, weights→data |
|------|----------|------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------|
| A | 1 | 1 | 484→475 (−1.9%) | 505→494 (−2.2%) | 1.68→1.71 (+1.8%) |
| B | 4 | 1 | 430→456 (+6.0%) | 568→575 (+1.2%) | 1.52→1.67 (+9.9%) |
| C | 8 | 1 | 484→466 (−3.7%) | 495→493 (−0.4%) | 1.63→1.63 (0.0%) |

| E | 4 | 16 | 1696→1191 (−29.8%) | 2713→1721 (−36.6%) | 6.75→8.72 (+29.2%) |

Single-request cases (conc=1) show no consistent improvement across the three metrics; concurrent cases improve. HY4-Flash VL: D TTFT p50 −20% / +9% req/s, E TTFT p95 −10% / +15% req/s. HY4 VL base (larger tower, more TP ranks to spread over): D TTFT p50 −8% / +7% req/s, E TTFT p50 −30%, p95 −37%, +29% req/s. Probe images are small (~110–272 merged tokens per image), which bounds the visible win; without repeated runs we do not claim a noise band for the single-request deltas.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: size video frames from the image processor config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vLLM resized Nemotron 3.5 Super VL video frames to 512x512 squares because it read video sizing only from `vision_config`. This PR loads the checkpoint's size and aspect ratio at model setup. It also supports requests with videos that resize to different dimensions.

## Claims

- Super VL video frames are sized by `video_target_num_patches` and `video_maintain_aspect_ratio` from `preprocessor_config.json`.
- A checkpoint that sets a video frame size in `vision_config` gets the same frame sizes as before.
- A request can hold several videos of different frame sizes, on Nano Omni and on Super VL.

Resized frame shape (width x height) for Super VL, before and after:

| Source clip | Before | After | Tokens per frame pair |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | 512x512 | 672x384 | 256 to 252 |
| 360x640 (portrait) | 512x512 | 384x672 | 256 to 252 |
| 512x512 | 512x512 | 512x512 | 256, unchanged |

Other models, same clips:

| Model | 1920x1080, before and after | 360x640, before and after |
|---|---|---|
| Nemotron Nano 12B V2 VL | 512x512 | 512x512 |
| Nemotron 3 Nano Omni | 672x384 | 384x672 |

## Validation

### Model setup hook

- On `d004d415e0`, the revised sizing tests found both fallback fields missing from `vision_config`. Three precedence cases passed.
  - Command: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py -k video_frame_size`
  - Result: `2 failed, 3 passed, 42 deselected, 1 warning in 16.41s`
- On `0820eeed6c`, all five sizing cases passed under the `core_model` selection.
  - Command: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py -m core_model -k video_frame_size`
  - Result: `5 passed, 42 deselected, 1 warning in 15.27s`
- The full test file passed on `0820eeed6c` with CV-CUDA enabled. The commit hooks also passed.
  - Command: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py`
  - Result: `47 passed, 2 warnings in 66.73s (0:01:06)`
- A preprocessing smoke test on `0820eeed6c` used the Super VL BF16 checkpoint configuration. It produced 672x384 and 384x672 frames from landscape and portrait clips, respectively. The processor rejected both sizing overrides.

### Earlier Python frontend serving tests

These runs used nightly image `7c3a9302f` and preceded the move to the model setup hook. The serving tests used 23 chat requests per run across images, single videos, and multiple videos.

- Nemotron 3 Nano Omni on one GPU. The three requests with videos of different sizes returned HTTP 400 before the fix and HTTP 200 after it. The other 19 accepted requests kept the same prompt token counts and greedy text.
- Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on four GPUs. A single 16:9 or 9:16 video with 16 frame pairs went from 4,597 to 4,533 prompt tokens. A 512x512 video stayed at 4,597.
- Super VL with two videos (640x360 and 360x640). Both runs returned HTTP 200. The prompt went from 9,163 to 9,035 tokens.
- Image-only requests kept the same prompt token counts on both models.

Accuracy at the new Super VL frame sizes remains unmeasured.

## Details

Where each checkpoint keeps the video fields:

| Field | Nemotron 3 Nano Omni | Nemotron 3.5 Super VL |
|---|---|---|
| `video_target_num_patches` (1024) | `config.json`, under `vision_config` | `preprocessor_config.json` and `processor_config.json` only |
| `video_maintain_aspect_ratio` (true) | `config.json`, under `vision_config` | `preprocessor_config.json` and `processor_config.json` only |
| `video_temporal_patch_size` (2) | `config.json`, under `vision_config` | `config.json`, top level and under `vision_config` |

- `NemotronHNanoVLV2Config.verify_and_update_model_config` runs after `ModelConfig` loads `preprocessor_config.json`. If `vision_config` sets neither size field, the hook copies `video_target_num_patches` and `video_maintain_aspect_ratio` into `vision_config`. The hook skips `null` and preserves explicit `false`.
- `NanoNemotronVLProcessor` reads the sizing fields from `vision_config`. Server and request `mm_processor_kwargs` cannot override them.
- **Effect.** The sizing rule is the one Nano Omni already uses. The token count per frame pair changes slightly for non-square clips (256 to 252 for 16:9).
- **Videos of different sizes.** The processor joined the frames of all videos of a request into one tensor, which needs one frame size. It now returns one tensor per video with its frame size, and the field is batched per video. The model already embeds videos of different sizes one at a time for device resize, and that path now serves both pixel inputs.
- **Why not keep the joined tensor for equal sizes.** The layout must not depend on the other videos of a request. A cached video and a new one can meet in one batch, and a flat field pads tensors of different shapes.
- **Duplicate check.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `video_target_num_patches`, `video_maintain_aspect_ratio`, and Nemotron video. None covers this.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Qwen4Exp: stage CPU-offloaded PLE rows on the host when UVA is unavailable
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Qwen4Exp PLE `cpu_offload` currently requires UVA. When UVA is unavailable, the NVIDIA path now keeps the table in host memory and stages each step's rows through the staging path that #59958 added for disk offload, instead of failing at init. This lets Qwen3.8-Flash-Next run on one H100 under NVIDIA Confidential Computing, where #59981 turns UVA off.

Closes #62815. Related: #57224 (root cause: under CC, pinned host memory reports `is_pinned() == False` and UVA views of it go stale), #59981 (CC detection that disables UVA), #59958 (PLE disk offload, whose staging this PR shares), #54371 (UVA PLE offload).

**Not a duplicate.** #59958, #58815 and #58439 read PLE rows from the checkpoint files (disk / page cache). This PR keeps the table in anonymous host memory and needs neither UVA nor file-backed reads; in a confidential VM, storage I/O patterns are visible to the host, so disk-backed tables are not an option there. Since #59958 has landed, this PR reuses its per-step staging and only adds the host-memory row source.

## Claims

- With `cpu_offload` on and `is_uva_available()` false, Qwen4Exp (NVIDIA) selects a new `Qwen4ExpPLEHostMemoryEmbedding` instead of raising `Engram CPU offload requires UVA support`. BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 tables are supported.
- The per-step staging of disk offload moves into a shared `Qwen4ExpPLEHostStagedEmbedding` base in `nvidia/host_staged_embedding.py`, unchanged in behaviour. Disk offload and the new host-memory table differ only in how `_gather_host_rows` fills the host buffers. When pinned memory is unavailable, the staging buffers fall back to pageable memory with synchronous copies.
- The forward only reads persistent device buffers, so the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs are kept.
- No change when UVA is available: the pinned UVA path and its prefetch are untouched.
- Without UVA, the fallback is also taken when `dp_shared_memory` is on (#60390), since the shared table is read through UVA as well. Each DP replica then keeps its own host table.

## Validation

Except for the CPU unit tests, all on one H100 NVL 94 GB in CC mode (Azure `Standard_NCC40ads_H100_v5`, driver 580.95.05), on the current head `5711d2ae8` with main nightly `b26e0840` merged. Main wheels are CUDA 13.2 builds (#55387), so the end-to-end run used the CUDA 13.2 forward-compatibility package (`cuda-compat-13-2`); without it `vllm serve` stops in the Marlin MoE repack with `the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain`.

**Unit tests, CPU (current head)**: with main `b26e0840` merged. On a machine without a GPU, `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` and `test_config.py`: 67 passed, 8 failed, 94 skipped. The 8 failures are the same set on main there (6 metadata tests that need a device type, 2 disk-offload file checks). The fallback selection test covers `dp_shared_memory` on and off.

**Unit tests, GPU (current head)**: `python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py` on that GPU: 153 passed, 11 failed, 5 skipped. Without this PR: 143 passed, with the same 11 failures (tests of the pinned-host/UVA paths on NVIDIA and AMD, plus one config test that needs PP=2 on a one-GPU node). The new and renamed cases pass: the graph-replay comparison against the resident table for every row source (disk, host memory, pageable host memory) in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4, the ETP owner masking, and the fallback selection with `dp_shared_memory` on and off.

**End to end (current head)**: V2 model runner, `VnimanieAI/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16`, default CUDA graphs. Startup logs `UVA is unavailable; staging the CPU-offloaded PLE rows from host RAM.`, the PLE table stays on the CPU, and PIECEWISE and FULL graphs are both captured. The first version of this PR (nightly `8e2beaa3` + #59981) gave the same results within noise.

**Correctness**: per-token prompt logprobs of 30 fixed texts (5,756 tokens). The reference is a naive lookup inside the forward (rows fetched synchronously with `F.embedding(ids.cpu(), weight)`, `--enforce-eager`). The serving engine is not bit-deterministic here (two reference runs differ), so the comparison is against that run-to-run noise:

| Run | Mean NLL | Mean \|Δlogprob\| vs reference run 1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Reference, run 1 / run 2 | 0.689 / 0.684 | — / 0.052 |
| This PR (CUDA graphs on), run 1 / run 2 | 0.686 / 0.682 | 0.055 / 0.054 |
| Control: staged rows left at zero | 0.922 | 0.387 |

**Performance**: `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, one run per point, total output tok/s / mean TPOT ms / mean TTFT ms:

| Concurrency | input 1024 / output 1024 | input 4096 / output 512 |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 121.0 / 8.1 / 133 | 113.6 / 8.2 / 311 |
| 8 | 640.7 / 12.0 / 556 | 510.1 / 12.9 / 1,415 |
| 32 | 1,325.9 / 22.9 / 1,273 | 884.9 / 30.9 / 2,681 |

There is no baseline on this hardware: without this PR the model does not start (the table does not fit on the GPU, and the UVA offload refuses to run).

Cost of the staging itself (measured on the first version, which used the same `index_select` gather; gather + copies only, 16 heads × 160 dims BF16, median of 20 on the same VM): 0.14 ms for 32 tokens, 12–19 ms for an 8,192-token prefill chunk. The H2D runs at about 4.1 GB/s, the bounce-buffer limit under CC.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve VnimanieAI/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16 \
  --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --moe-backend marlin --language-model-only

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $((3 * C)) --max-concurrency $C   # min 8 prompts

# prompt logprobs: /v1/completions with max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=0 and a fresh cache_salt per request
```

`--moe-backend marlin` avoids the MoE HUMMING conversion OOM on a 94 GB GPU (noted in #62815), unrelated to this PR.
</details>

## Details

**Design.** PLE lookups depend only on token IDs, so the rows a step needs are known before its forward. #59958 stages them in `Qwen4ExpModelState.prepare_inputs`: n-gram IDs to the host, one stream sync, distinct rows read per storage plane, one H2D per plane into fixed device buffers, NVFP4 decoded on the GPU. This PR moves that into `Qwen4ExpPLEHostStagedEmbedding` (`nvidia/host_staged_embedding.py`) with one abstract `_gather_host_rows(ids)` that fills the host buffers in token and head order. `Qwen4ExpPLEDiskOffloadEmbedding` reads the distinct rows with `preadv` there and expands them. `Qwen4ExpPLEHostMemoryEmbedding` gathers from the ETP-sharded host table with `index_select` on raw bytes, zeroes rows owned by other ETP ranks, and reduces after the lookup like the pinned-host table (the reduction helper moves to the common base). `stage_checkpoint_rows` becomes `stage_host_rows`. `docs/features/engram.md` notes the fallback.

**Tradeoff: one host sync per step on this path.** The IDs hash the tokens sampled by the previous step on the GPU, so the read-back waits for that step to finish, which removes some async-scheduling overlap. This is the same sync disk offload already makes. Only the fallback pays it; the UVA path is unchanged. I could not measure the overlap loss on CC, since there is no UVA path to compare against there. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` could not be exercised on CC either: it first stops in #59981's staged input copy, because pinned host memory reports `is_pinned() == False` under CC.

**Limitations.**
- NVIDIA path only. The AMD Qwen4Exp path still requires UVA.
- ETP spanning DP ranks (`embedding_across_dp`) is rejected with `NotImplementedError`. TP/ETP within one DP rank is supported (rows owned by other ranks are zeroed, then reduced). Unlike disk offload, each rank keeps only its own rows in host memory.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Engram is not covered.
- `dp_shared_memory` is not used on this path, so co-located DP replicas each hold a copy of their table rows in host memory.
- The NVIDIA Qwen4Exp model selects this path only when UVA is unavailable, for example under CC, where #59981 (on main and in v0.34.0) turns UVA off.

**CI.** The new tests live in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` and `test_config.py`, which the existing Qwen4 Exp lanes run. The ETP owner-masking test also runs on CPU. CC hardware is not available in CI; the end-to-end results above were collected outside CI.

commits.pr_title: [XPU][LoRA] Use dense GEMM for single-adapter prefill batches
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Use dense GEMMs instead of per-token BGMV for XPU LoRA linear layers when a prefill-sized batch uses a single adapter. Works under the default compile + graph mode.

## Claims

- Single-adapter prefill with LoRA is **~40% faster** on Qwen3.6-27B (TP2), as fast as the same prompts without an adapter.
- Multi-adapter workloads gain whenever a scheduled step happens to contain one adapter; mixed steps keep BGMV.
- Decode is unchanged: steps that may replay a captured graph always use BGMV.
- XPU only (`PunicaWrapperXPU`); no kernel changes or new dependencies.

## Validation

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_punica_xpu_ops.py tests/lora/test_layers.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py
```

179 passed, 98 skipped (main: 156 / 98). The new tests check which path ran via `torch.profiler`.

**Prefill latency.** Qwen3.6-27B FP16, TP2, Intel Arc Pro B-series, default compile + `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs. `max_loras=2`, `max_lora_rank=32`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`. 4 prompts × 2048 tokens, 1 output token. Median of 5 runs after 2 warmups; two A/B pairs in opposite order.

| Requests | main (s) | PR (s) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| no adapter | 2.31 / 2.29 | 2.29 / 2.27 | ~0% |
| rank-8 adapter | 3.79 / 3.78 | 2.26 / 2.24 | −40.3% / −40.7% |
| rank-32 adapter | 3.82 / 3.82 | 2.26 / 2.25 | −40.9% / −41.1% |
| alternating r8 / r32 | 3.83 / 3.87 | 3.06 / 3.06 | −20.1% / −21.0% |

The alternating case gains because 2 of its 3 scheduled steps contain a single adapter.

**Decode throughput** (128 input / 128 output tokens, same config): rank-8 B8 131.1 → 133.2 tok/s, mixed B8 130.1 → 129.8, rank-8 B1 18.8 → 18.9.

**Correctness.** Synthetic adapters strong enough to change the output, greedy, 16 tokens per request. All adapter cases (rank 8, rank 32, mixed, switching) match main token for token in graph and eager mode. With graphs captured up to 512 tokens, 300-token (graph replay, BGMV) and 1024-token (GEMM, switching slots) prompts also match. No-adapter batches use the same BGMV kernels as main. One of them flips at token 13 in eager mode, but main itself flips that request at token 4 or 13 in 3 of 4 repeated runs (TP2 run-to-run non-determinism).

## Details

**Why.** XPU BGMV computes LoRA token by token. At rank 32 and 2048 tokens it costs 0.8–2× as much as the layer's base projection. For a batch with one adapter, `x @ A^T @ B^T` is two dense GEMMs per slice. Measured per layer, these break even with BGMV around `num_tokens * rank = 8192` and are up to 20× faster for large batches.

**Design.**
- `update_metadata` records the slot used by every token (or -1) in a 1-element **host** tensor. It uses the per-token mapping, because a chunked-prefill step need not sample.
- A new `vllm::xpu_lora_linear` custom op reads that slot at runtime. torch.compile does not freeze the branch, and there is no device sync; `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK` is CUDA-only, so this holds by construction.
- GEMM requires `num_tokens * rank >= 8192` and `num_tokens > max_cudagraph_capture_size`, so captured graphs always contain BGMV. It is disabled without a current vLLM config and for mixed-precision weights.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- With compile + graphs and a warm Inductor cache, startup measures about 0.13 GiB more non-torch memory per device, which comes out of the KV cache. It is reproducible, absent in eager mode and unchanged with GEMM disabled; the source is not identified.
- With `max_loras >= 2` the profile run never takes the GEMM path, but GEMM's transient peak never exceeds BGMV's: 2 MiB vs 3 MiB per layer at 8192 tokens, rank 64.
- Only single-adapter steps gain; mixed prefill would need a segmented-GEMM kernel. `XPU_USE_TRITON_KERNEL=1` also speeds up prefill, but its LoRA decode is 29–37% slower.
- Follow-ups: under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` prefill never replays graphs, so its threshold could be lower. Tower/connector wrappers inherit the language model's capture size, while encoder graphs use `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`. XPU currently rejects tower/connector LoRA; revisit this when it is enabled.

**Related.** #51613 (draft) moves BGMV to multi-slice kernels. At prefill sizes those are 10–90% slower than the current BGMV, and this PR's GEMM path is 2–5× faster than either. The two are complementary but conflict textually.

Validated with torch 2.14.0+xpu and vllm-xpu-kernels main.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tokenizer] Route skip_special_tokens=False through Tekken byte fallback (#67755)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #67755.

This PR ensures Tekken byte-fallback recovery runs even when `skip_special_tokens=False` in `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`. Without this, multi-byte characters like emoji and CJK text get garbled into replacement characters (``), and trailing multi-byte tokens get dropped completely during incremental detokenization.

## Details

### Root Cause
When `skip_special_tokens=False`, `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens` took an early exit that called `id_to_piece` directly on each token ID:
```python
if not skip_special_tokens:
    return [self.tokenizer.id_to_piece(token_id) for token_id in ids]
```
For Tekken models (`Tekkenizer`), individual byte-fallback tokens are raw UTF-8 bytes that cannot be decoded in isolation. Calling `id_to_piece` on them turns each byte into `` on the spot, bypassing the `id_to_byte_piece(token_id, SpecialTokenPolicy.KEEP)` path that runs when `skip_special_tokens=True`.

This caused two issues downstream in `detokenize_incrementally`:
1. Multi-byte characters in the middle of generation were permanently corrupted into `` (e.g., `"Hi 🤖 数学 ok"` came out as `"Hi  学 ok"`).
2. If a multi-byte character finished the sequence, the detokenizer saw trailing ``, assumed it was waiting for byte continuation, and never emitted the final delta—dropping the character entirely (e.g., `"URGENCY🌶️"` came out as `"URGENCY"`).

### Relation to #65118
#65118 previously worked around this symptom in `/v1/responses` by preventing `MistralParser.adjust_request` from forcing `skip_special_tokens=False`. While that masked the issue on tool-calling endpoints, the author explicitly noted that clients or workflows passing `skip_special_tokens=False` directly would still hit the byte-fallback bug in `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`. This PR addresses that root cause.

### Changes
- Removed the early exit in `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`. When `skip_special_tokens=False`, we keep all IDs (`ids_kept = list(ids)`) while still letting them pass through the Tekken byte-fallback block if any `` is detected.
- Switched `_vocab_dict` construction in `MistralTokenizer.__init__` to `self.tokenizer.id_to_piece(i)`, avoiding a premature call to `convert_ids_to_tokens` before `_special_token_ids_set` is initialized.
- Added byte decoding with replacement fallback in `ServingTokenization` (`serving.py`) so `/tokenize` with `return_token_strs=True` always returns valid strings.
- Added regression test in `tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py` (`test_mistral_edge_case`) covering multi-byte and trailing emoji characters across `skip_special_tokens=[True, False]`.

## Validation

### 1. Parity against `tokenizer.decode` (`mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409`)
Tested incremental streaming token-by-token against `tokenizer.decode`:

| Input | `skip_special_tokens` | `main` | This PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `'Hi 🤖 数学 ok'` | `True` | `'Hi 🤖 数学 ok'` | `'Hi 🤖 数学 ok'` | Pass |
| `'Hi 🤖 数学 ok'` | `False` | `'Hi  学 ok'` | `'Hi 🤖 数学 ok'` | Fixed |
| `'URGENCY🌶️'` | `True` | `'URGENCY🌶️'` | `'URGENCY🌶️'` | Pass |
| `'URGENCY🌶️'` | `False` | `'URGENCY'` (dropped) | `'URGENCY🌶️'` | Fixed |
| `<s>` + `'URGENCY🌶️'` | `False` | `'<s>URGENCY'` | `'<s>URGENCY🌶️'` | Fixed (keeps `<s>`, decodes emoji) |

### 2. Tests and Lint
```bash
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py -k "test_mistral_edge_case"
ruff check vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/serving.py tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py
ruff format --check vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/serving.py tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py
```
All passed cleanly.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] **Design Fit:** Surgical fix in `convert_ids_to_tokens` reusing existing Tekken byte-fallback recovery; clean vocab initialization and string handling.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Added regression tests in `test_detokenize.py` covering both `skip_special_tokens` settings with multi-byte and trailing emoji characters.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Formatted and linted with `ruff`.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Links #67755 and #65118 with before/after repro data and tokenizer init fix.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Share replicated MLA KV per host
commits.pr_body:
CPU offload stores one copy of fully replicated MLA KV per TP rank when an engine spans hosts. This extends the single-host deduplication in #48906 and #50301 to multi-node multiprocessing.

Each host's first rank writes a shared copy, and every local rank can restore from it. With TP8 across two four-GPU hosts, eight copies become two. The configured CPU budget still covers the whole engine.

## Tests

- On two hosts with two H100s each, the same 16 MiB held 512 chunks, up from 256. All four ranks restored the original bytes. After a GPU prefix-cache reset, two DeepSeekV2 prompts each reloaded 512 tokens from CPU and reproduced all 48 output tokens across both runs (`cf1efb905d`).
- All 179 tests in the three affected modules passed on H100 (`f284d7cfd7`).

```sh
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/{test_config,test_worker}.py
```

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Return pending work, events and stats from on_schedule_end
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Item 4 of #68678. At the end of each step, the offloading manager now returns its pending work, KV events and stats together, in one `StepResult` from `on_schedule_end()`. This replaces the separate `has_pending_work()`, `take_events()` and `get_stats()` calls.

## Claims

- Each step, the connector gets pending work, events and stats from one manager call instead of four. The engine's liveness check, the event drain and the stats report no longer take the manager lock.
- Events and stats from transfers that finish after `on_schedule_end()` are reported one step later, and the engine keeps stepping until they are out.
- Out-of-tree managers now return from `on_schedule_end()` what their `has_pending_work()`, `take_events()` and `get_stats()` used to return.

## Validation

Manager calls per engine step. One request runs through the connector test harness with a mocked manager, and `has_requests()` is checked after every step, as `EngineCore` does (66 steps):

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Manager calls for pending work, events and stats | 3.02 | 1.00 |
| Manager lock entries | 4.02 | 2.00 |

The two lock entries left are the step region in `schedule()` and `update_connector_output()`.

<details>
<summary>Count script (run from the repo root)</summary>

```python
"""Count connector->manager calls per engine step (run from a vLLM worktree).

Drives one request through the offloading connector's test harness with a
mocked manager, asks has_requests() after every step as EngineCore does, and
reports the per-step manager calls and lock entries made outside schedule().
"""

from collections import Counter

from tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.offloading_connector.utils import (
    EOS_TOKEN_ID,
    RequestRunner,
    generate_store_output,
)

STEP_CALLS = ("on_schedule_end", "has_pending_work", "take_events", "get_stats")
DECODE_STEPS = 64

runner = RequestRunner(block_size=4, num_gpu_blocks=100, async_scheduling=False)
manager = runner.manager
manager.prepare_store.side_effect = lambda keys, req_context, trigger: (
    generate_store_output([])
)
lock = manager.lock
steps = 0
lock_outside = 0


def after_step() -> None:
    global steps, lock_outside
    steps += 1
    entered = lock.__enter__.call_count
    runner.scheduler.has_requests()
    lock_outside += lock.__enter__.call_count - entered


manager.reset_mock()
before = lock.__enter__.call_count
runner.new_request(token_ids=[1] * 8)
runner.run(decoded_tokens=[2] * DECODE_STEPS + [EOS_TOKEN_ID], post_step_fn=after_step)

calls = Counter(name for name, _, _ in manager.method_calls)
print(f"steps={steps}")
for name in STEP_CALLS:
    print(f"{name}: {calls[name]} ({calls[name] / steps:.2f}/step)")
print(f"step-call crossings/step: {sum(calls[n] for n in STEP_CALLS) / steps:.2f}")
print(f"lock entries/step: {(lock.__enter__.call_count - before) / steps:.2f}")
print(f"lock entries/step in has_requests(): {lock_outside / steps:.2f}")
```

</details>

Tests on `68af6573e2` and on its base, `main` at `e6109f064a`. Linux aarch64, CPU only (torch 2.14.0+cpu):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py
```

```text
main:    44 failed, 1672 passed, 35 skipped in 314.77s (0:05:14)
this PR: 44 failed, 1675 passed, 35 skipped in 315.86s (0:05:15)
```

Both runs fail the same 44 tests, which need a GPU, the compiled `_C` ops or model weights. The new tests:

```text
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
    -k "cascade_after_the_last_store or follows_the_step_result or reported_once or reset_drops_undrained or schedule_end_reports"
5 passed, 521 deselected in 1.43s
```

## Details

The connector stores each result. Events and stats add up until they are drained, because with async scheduling `schedule()` can run more than once before an output is processed.

The engine checks `has_pending_push_work()` after it processes a step's output, which is later than `on_schedule_end()`. A transfer that finishes in between can give the manager new work, such as a tiering cascade to a secondary tier. So when a finished transfer reaches the manager, the connector keeps the engine stepping until the next result arrives. Before the first step there is no result yet, so the connector reports pending work and the engine runs one step. Without this, a tiering manager with the tier-poll thread disabled would not step until the first request arrived.

Because stored events now wait one step, a cache reset in between would publish them after their chunks are gone. The CPU manager drops its undrained stored events on reset.

`StepResult` has no `finished_jobs` field yet. No manager reports finished jobs to the connector today, so the field would have nothing to fill it and nothing to read it.

No open PR covers this. I searched for `StepResult`, `on_schedule_end` and #68678, and claimed this item in the RFC.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Clean up dead and redundant KV cache planning code in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` (and its `hisparse/layout.py` and `kv_cache_interface.py` touchpoints): remove unused ungrouped memory checks, eliminate redundant `may_override_num_blocks` / `saved_override` indirection and the `available_memory` wrapper in config materialization, and remove dead grouping helpers.

Follow-up to #31260, #53558, #61183, and #61452.

## Claims

- **Remove dead ungrouped memory checks:** Deletes unused `max_memory_usage_bytes`, `estimate_max_model_len`, `check_enough_kv_cache_memory`, and `KVCacheGroup.max_memory_usage_bytes` (zero production callers); simplifies `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` to call the grouped helpers directly instead of taking `Callable`/`partial` callbacks.
- **Honor exact `num_blocks` in config materialization:** Changes `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` and `get_hisparse_kv_cache_config` to take `num_blocks` directly (matching `KVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`), removing `may_override_num_blocks`, the `num_blocks * bytes_per_block -> // bytes_per_block` roundtrip, the duplicated empty-group branch, and the `saved_override` in-place mutation workaround in `_pool_bytes_per_block_from_builder`. Also fixes `--num-gpu-blocks-override` leaking into `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling`.
- **Remove dead grouping helpers:** Removes the unreachable `can_share_block_table` check in `_try_get_full_allocation_fallback_groups`, single-caller wrappers `is_kv_cache_type_attention_free` and `get_uniform_page_size`, redundant `Counter` recomputation in `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups`, and a stale docstring reference in `KVCacheConfig`.
- **Update unit tests:** Migrates affected unit tests off the removed dead helpers and updates direct `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` callers to pass `num_blocks` directly.

## Validation

Tested on commit `90ce87d3de`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -x \
  tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_embedded.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_dsv4_packed_zeroer_geometry.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_replayssm_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py::test_sparse_flashmla_prefill_on_the_kv_cache_at_allocation \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_ssu_dispatch.py::test_replayssm_materializes_only_accepted_boundary_with_compacted_rows \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py::test_replayssm_precopy_moves_packed_state_and_trackers \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_bind_and_copy_replayssm_cache_by_group \
  -k "not test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short"
```

```text
=== 433 passed, 65 skipped, 2 deselected, 163 warnings in 430.96s (0:07:10) ====
```

(`test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short` is a pre-existing `cpu_test` expecting CPU-default `resolved_gpu_memory_utilization < 1.0`, whereas on a CUDA host extensible KV cache defaults to `1.0`; untouched by this PR. The 65 skipped tests are optional-dependency/platform-gated connector tests such as `mori`/UMBP.)

All pre-commit hooks (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, `check-docstring-style`, `check-test-tethering`, `signoff-commit`, etc.) passed.

## Details

- **No duplicate PR:** Searched open PRs in `vllm-project/vllm` (`check_enough_kv_cache_memory OR estimate_max_model_len OR kv_cache_planning`); none address this cleanup.
- **Why removing the ungrouped memory checks is safe:**
  - Full-repo grep confirms zero production callers in `vllm/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, or `benchmarks/` for `max_memory_usage_bytes`, `estimate_max_model_len`, `check_enough_kv_cache_memory`, and `KVCacheGroup.max_memory_usage_bytes`. (`KVCacheLayerConfig.max_memory_usage_bytes` still has a caller in ROCm warmup and is kept.)
  - Production has exclusively used `_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups` and `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` since #31260.
- **Why removing `may_override_num_blocks` and the `available_memory` wrapper is safe and fixes a bug:**
  - `get_kv_cache_configs` already applies `num_gpu_blocks_override` up front before auto-fit, memory checks, and block-count sizing.
  - `KVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`'s contract is to materialize tensors for *exact* `num_blocks`. Having `may_override_num_blocks` inside the underlying `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` / `get_hisparse_kv_cache_config` forced `_pool_bytes_per_block_from_builder` to temporarily mutate `vllm_config.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks_override = None` and silently broke `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling` (`cudagraph_utils.py`) when `--num-gpu-blocks-override` was set.
  - Module-level `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` had zero production callers left outside `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`, so it now takes `num_blocks` directly (mirroring `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`), and its unit-test callers have been updated accordingly.
- **Test updates:**
  - `tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py`: calls real `get_kv_cache_configs` with real `VllmConfig` instead of `MagicMock` + monkeypatched `max_memory_usage_bytes`.
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py`: asserts `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(..., num_blocks=1).num_blocks == 1` even when `num_gpu_blocks_override=500`.
  - Direct unit-test callers of `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` now pass `num_blocks` directly instead of `available_memory` (or `num_gpu_blocks_override` + dummy memory budget).
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: replaces the `KVCacheGroup.max_memory_usage_bytes` assertion with `max_allocated_blocks_per_request` and `page_size_bytes`.
- **AI assistance:** AI assistance (Antigravity) was used to audit call sites, implement the cleanup, and run validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Keep extensible KV with RDMA-capable peermem allocations
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Mooncake rejects extensible KV with nvidia-peermem at startup even when the CUDA device supports GPUDirect RDMA for VMM allocations. Allow the combination on supported devices.

## Claims

- Reuse the allocator's per-device VMM GPUDirect RDMA query in Mooncake.
- Raise a startup error for unsupported devices and retain the DMA-BUF default when `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM` is unset.

## Validation

**Hardware and network.** Two nodes with 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs each (driver 535.161.08), connected over RoCE with `nvidia_peermem` loaded and four RDMA HCAs visible per node. The P and D nodes could reach each other's Mooncake peer ports and the Prefill bootstrap endpoint.

**Image.** `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-eff4de9be3c901c6ad12cb651de64e4b10ced219` with Mooncake CUDA 13 0.3.14. A used the original image source. B applied the two-file patch from `a26dd5e4c8`.

<details>
<summary>Prefill and Decode startup commands</summary>

Both arms used the same launch arguments for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. The commands omit test instrumentation.

```bash
# Run the common setup on each node, then run its role command.
# Set MODEL and VLLM_HOST_IP to the local checkpoint path and reachable node IP.
export MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
export VLLM_HOST_IP="<replace-with-local-node-ip>"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME='=eth0' NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
export WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=180 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
ulimit -l unlimited

COMMON=(
  --host 0.0.0.0 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --disable-custom-all-reduce
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 --enable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
  --enable-extensible-kv-cache --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill
  --max-model-len 147456 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-num-seqs 32
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --no-async-scheduling
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"prefill_context_kv_only":false}'
)
RDMA_DEVICES=mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4  # Set to the local RoCE HCAs.
mc_config() {
  printf '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"%s","engine_id":"%s","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","device_name":"%s"}}' \
    "$1" "$2" "$RDMA_DEVICES"
}

# Prefill
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=28998 vllm serve "$MODEL" "${COMMON[@]}" \
  --port 28001 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config "$(mc_config kv_producer h20-prefill)"

# Decode
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=28999 vllm serve "$MODEL" "${COMMON[@]}" \
  --port 28002 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":192}' \
  --kv-transfer-config "$(mc_config kv_consumer h20-decode)"
```

</details>

**A/B.** TP8 with DSpark on both nodes, eager Prefill and FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs on Decode. Extensible KV and peermem were explicitly enabled in both arms.

| | A: unmodified nightly | B: with patch |
|---|---|---|
| Startup | P and D both failed with `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=1 is incompatible with the extensible KV cache` | P and D both started and retained extensible KV on all 16 ranks |
| PD requests | Blocked by startup failure | 5/5 HTTP 200, including cold 8K, cold 128K and a partial prefix hit. Both 8K requests imported 8,191 tokens each, and the 128K request imported 131,071. All 40 RDMA writes succeeded. |

**GSM8K.** Full test split (1,319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, thinking disabled, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 32. Decode-local used the same patched server and sampling settings with local prompt computation.

| | Accuracy | Request errors | Length-limited responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Patched PD | **96.97% (1,279/1,319)** | 0 | 0 |
| Patched Decode-local | **96.82% (1,277/1,319)** | 0 | 3 |

PD imported 101,119 external KV tokens across 7,320 RDMA writes with zero errors. Decode recorded CUDA graph replays and DSpark accepted draft tokens in both runs.

## Details

The CUDA VMM allocator already sets `gpuDirectRDMACapable` on supported devices. Mooncake now uses that same device capability before initializing the transfer engine with peermem and extensible KV. The cache mode stays as configured, and the transfer engine still reports actual memory registration failures.

This addresses the startup gate. #67158 handled cleanup after a failed startup, and #64363 used the manual opt-out in its RDMA validation.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for diagnosis, implementation and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC] Let Mooncake consumers encode requests without EC params locally
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A Mooncake EC consumer waits for a push for every multimodal item, even when the request has no `ec_transfer_params` and no encoder will push. A raw-media request sent straight to the consumer waits `push_wait_timeout_s` (60s) and returns 500. Like `ECCPUConnector`, the consumer now leaves such requests to the local encoder, unless a pushed copy of the item is already there.

## Claims

- Raw-media requests to a Mooncake EC consumer are encoded locally: 200 in about 1s instead of 500 after 60s.
- If the consumer already holds a pushed copy of the item, it is loaded as before.
- Requests that carry `ec_transfer_params` (the normal EPD path) are unchanged.

## Validation

1 GPU per server, Qwen3-VL-4B, one raw-image `/v1/chat/completions` request, greedy, 16 tokens. The consumer runs `ECMooncakeConnector` as `ec_consumer` over TCP. The control is the same server with no EC config.

| server | main (1acec5c009) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Mooncake consumer | 500 after 60.2s, `waited 60.0s for a push ... that never arrived` | 200 in 0.7s, same text as control, no EC warnings |
| control (no EC) | 200 in 1.0s | 200 in 0.7s |

A second run uses 1 E + 1 PD (consumer) + proxy, with raw requests sent straight to the PD. All outputs match a plain server.

| step | 7de6354261 (first version) | 93e51fd401 |
|---|---|---|
| raw image | 200 | 200 |
| EPD request via proxy, then the same image raw (same uuid) | 200 | 200 |
| encode-only push of Z, then Z raw (same uuid) | 500, `Encoder cache miss for uuid:img-z` | 200 |

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_mooncake_reset_local_cache.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_cross_encoder_cache.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_epd_proxy_retry.py
# 125 passed
```

## Details

- `ensure_cache_available` still loads a pushed item for a request without `ec_transfer_params`. It no longer waits for a push that will not come. `has_cache_item` reports such items, so skipping the load would crash the engine with an encoder cache miss.
- `update_state_after_free` and `request_finished` skip transfer bookkeeping for these requests. Before, they logged an unresolved transfer id.
- An item with only placeholder metadata and no EC params is still rejected right away by the scheduler's existing `_reject_on_missing_encoder_input`.
- One existing test sent a request without EC params to cover a remote miss. It now passes a transfer id.
- Tradeoff: a proxy that drops `ec_transfer_params` by mistake no longer times out. The consumer encodes the media itself, which is correct but slower, the same as `ECCPUConnector`.
- Out of scope: the check covers the whole request. A raw item inside a request that has EC params still waits for a push, as on main.
- The `push_wait_timeout_s` row in `mooncake_ec_connector_usage.md` now says that requests without EC params do not wait.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Account for PCP size in DP supervisor device_ids
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix DP supervisor (`--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`) device-ID sharding to account for `prefill_context_parallel_size` (PCP) when computing `devices_per_rank`.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `dp_supervisor` and `prefill_context_parallel_size dp supervisor` and confirmed `upstream/main` (`669d308d60`) does not include this fix and no open PR addresses it.

## Claims

- Include `args.prefill_context_parallel_size` in `devices_per_rank` in `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/dp_supervisor.py:_build_device_ids`, matching `ParallelConfig.world_size` (`TP * PP * PCP`) and the direct attribute access style of `args.tensor_parallel_size` and `args.pipeline_parallel_size`.
- Update existing DP supervisor unit tests to populate `prefill_context_parallel_size=1` and add `TestDpDeviceIdSharding.test_dp_supervisor_device_ids_accounts_for_pcp` covering default env-relative allocation, user-provided `--device-ids` sharding, and out-of-range validation with `PCP > 1`.

## Validation

Tested on commit `73e3b049` (Windows workstation; full `pytest` suite will run on Linux CI):

- Direct verification of `_build_device_ids` with `TP=2, PP=1, PCP=2` (fails on `upstream/main` `669d308d60` returning `[0, 1]` / `[2, 3]` instead of `[0, 1, 2, 3]` / `[4, 5, 6, 7]`, passes on `73e3b049`):
  - Default `device_ids=None`: `local_rank=0 -> [0, 1, 2, 3]`, `local_rank=1 -> [4, 5, 6, 7]`
  - User `device_ids=[0..7]`: `local_rank=0 -> [0, 1, 2, 3]`, `local_rank=1 -> [4, 5, 6, 7]`, `local_rank=2 -> ValueError("needs devices")`
- Linters & type checks:
  - `ruff check` & `ruff format --check` on all 3 changed files: `All checks passed! / 3 files already formatted`
  - `mypy --platform linux --python-version 3.11 --ignore-missing-imports vllm/entrypoints/launchers/dp_supervisor.py`: `Success: no issues found in 1 source file`
  - `pre-commit` hooks (`ruff`, `typos`, `check-test-tethering`, `SPDX`, `signoff-commit`, etc.): Passed
- Model evaluation: Not applicable (CLI/launcher device-ID sharding fix only; no model math or serving behavior change for `PCP=1`).

## Details

### Root Cause

In `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/dp_supervisor.py`, `_build_device_ids()` previously computed:

```python
devices_per_rank = args.tensor_parallel_size * args.pipeline_parallel_size
```

However, a single DP rank's `ParallelConfig.world_size` is `pipeline_parallel_size * tensor_parallel_size * prefill_context_parallel_size` (`vllm/config/parallel.py`). Regular DP paths (`set_assigned_physical_gpu_ids_for_dp_rank` / `_set_assigned_physical_gpu_ids`) slice devices using `parallel_config.world_size`, which already includes PCP.

Under `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb` with `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`, `_build_vllm_dp_server_args()` copies `prefill_context_parallel_size` to each child process, but `_build_device_ids()` only assigns `TP * PP` devices per child (and advances `[start, stop)` by `TP * PP`), causing `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` to be too short for `local_world_size` and triggering assertion failures in `GPUWorker.init_device` / `XPUWorker.init_device`.

### Implementation

Multiply by `args.prefill_context_parallel_size` directly in `_build_device_ids()`, keeping it consistent with `args.tensor_parallel_size` and `args.pipeline_parallel_size`, and update the test `argparse.Namespace` fixtures in `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` and `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Enforce --max-num-queued-reqs and --max-num-queued-tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend now enforces `--max-num-queued-reqs` and `--max-num-queued-tokens`, which it used to reject at startup as unimplemented. Related: #61296, inactive since October.

## Claims

- A request that would exceed either limit is rejected before it reaches the engine, with HTTP 503 (gRPC `UNAVAILABLE`) and the Python frontend's message.
- Same accounting as Python: a request with `n` samples takes `n` slots, and its prompt tokens count toward the backlog until its first output.
- Slots and backlog follow the outputs engine-core-client receives, not how fast each response stream is read, so a slow client does not hold capacity after the engine is done.
- `--max-num-queued-tokens` accepts human-readable values such as `32k`.

## Validation

New tests cover the admission counters, the client's observer contract (outputs, then drop on finish, abort and close), both limits rejecting and recovering against the scripted engine with the released requests' streams left unread, and the 503 on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`. Each fails with its check removed, and the scripted-engine test also fails on a release tied to stream reads. `cargo nextest` over `vllm-engine-core-client`, `vllm-llm`, `vllm-text`, `vllm-server`, `vllm-cmd` and `vllm-managed-engine` at `35f91be860`: 1245 passed.

## Details

- `EngineCoreLlm::generate_n` admits all `n` samples in one compare-and-swap after `prepare`, so validation errors stay 400 and concurrent requests cannot overshoot the limit.
- Each sample's guard goes to engine-core-client through a new `RequestObserver` hook (`call_observed`). The request registry shows it each output as the dispatcher receives it and drops it when the request leaves the client: finish, abort or a dropped stream, failed send, or shutdown. This matches Python, whose `OutputProcessor` updates request state in the background.
- Python sums per-process counters in shared memory across API server processes; the Rust frontend is one process, so two atomics suffice.
- Differences from Python: the check runs only after rendering, so a rejected request is still tokenized; `vllm:admission_rejections` is not incremented yet, since the metric is added in #69119.
