commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Bench] Fix KV cache planning for pipeline forwards
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix KV cache planning for `vllm bench forward` with pipeline parallelism under the external launcher.

Addresses the failure in [Buildkite build 105046](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105046#01a20739-8a8a-4191-88bb-8e37ed050086), following vllm-project/vllm#67998.

## Claims

- Provide globally ordered worker metadata to the KV cache planner instead of a rank-local singleton.
- Initialize each local worker with the KV cache configuration for its world rank.
- Keep the change confined to the forward benchmark executor; serving executors, planner contracts, CLI defaults, and steady-state execution are unchanged.

## Validation

**Publication blocked:** real two-GPU base/fix validation and human review are still pending. Do not publish this description as a completed validation report.

Fix commit: `5e232bc5c990daa9136cd563024ff3024c681a23`

Base commit: `ee1d07c7b2c30dc0eb686bdb00a8ce94f4e4c071`

The previous handoff reports all applicable pre-commit hooks passing, including Ruff and mypy, and the following focused test result on the fix commit:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_pipeline_stages_describe_every_stage \
  -k '(not bench_forward_muse and not bench_forward_hybrid and not bench_forward_drafter and not test_bench_forward and not balanced_routing) or test_bench_forward_pipeline' -q
```

```text
14 passed, 1 skipped, 12 deselected, 3 warnings in 2.71s
```

The skipped test was `test_bench_forward_pipeline`: that environment exposed only one GPU. These results do **not** establish that the fix passes the two-GPU regression.

The existing regression test uses `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, PP=2, CUDA graphs, and profiling. It checks finite outputs, last-stage-only sampling, NCCL transfers, exact pipeline/eager comparisons, and timing consistency.

Run the following command in isolated base and fix worktrees with two available CUDA GPUs, using each worktree's uv-managed environment:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<two-authorized-GPU-indices> \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_pipeline -v -s
```

Before publication, replace this pending-validation text with both runs' exact commands, GPU/software configuration, raw failure/success output, and pytest summary lines including time. Confirm that the base fails for the reported reason and the fix passes.

Current resource limitation: all eight visible NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell GPUs have approximately 54 GiB in use. The shared environment is awaiting two available GPUs; no GPU workload was started.

## Details

The planner expects KV cache configurations ordered globally by PP, PCP, and TP rank. The external launcher owns one local worker per torchrun process, so its inherited RPC returns a singleton. With PP=2, `get_pipeline_stages()` computes `workers_per_stage = 1 // 2 = 0`, then raises:

```text
ValueError: slice step cannot be zero
```

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][XPU] Tensor-descriptor Q loads in Triton MLA decode attention
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On Intel XPU, `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (TRITON_MLA decode) now loads its Q and Q-PE tiles through tensor descriptors instead of masked pointer loads, for the 576-wide MLA tile (`kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64) only. The K/V loop and the math are unchanged. The KV gather stays on pointer loads: this is a Q-tile change, not a descriptor path for the paged gather.

Context: RFC vllm-project/vllm#42545 recorded that this kernel could not use descriptors because of its paged KV gather. That still holds for K/V; the change here covers only the Q tile, which is a plain strided 2D tile, and only on XPU.

Scope: the gain applies to XPU runs that use `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` explicitly, or that reach it as the fallback when `XPUFlashAttnMLABackend` rejects a config (`vllm/platforms/xpu.py`). The default XPU MLA backend (FlashAttnMLA) is faster than TRITON_MLA even with this change, and it is not affected. End-to-end numbers are on one model (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat); most are with `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` forced, plus one real fallback configuration (`--block-size 16`, where FlashAttnMLA rejects the config). Fp8 KV was not measured end to end. CUDA and ROCm launch the unchanged kernel.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds tensor descriptors to this kernel. 18 other open PRs touch `triton_decode_attention.py` or its test file. Those that change the same code:
- vllm-project/vllm#51861 (draft) rewrites the Q-PE load; after it lands the descriptors here (`shape=[q_head_num, Lk]`) must be rebuilt for the split Q / Q-PE layout.
- vllm-project/vllm#51685 lets TRITON_MLA take a native fp8 KV cache and an fp8 query; the descriptor path would then see an fp8 Q, which is not tested here.
- vllm-project/vllm#52019 changes the stage-1 launcher signature and call site.
- vllm-project/vllm#61068, vllm-project/vllm#60173, vllm-project/vllm#54013 change `num_stages` handling next to the gate.
- vllm-project/vllm#63795, vllm-project/vllm#63796, vllm-project/vllm#48605 add a sliding-window constexpr to the same kernel next to `USE_TD`.
- vllm-project/vllm#57094, vllm-project/vllm#62725, vllm-project/vllm#40705, vllm-project/vllm#63623, vllm-project/vllm#57902, vllm-project/vllm#52472, vllm-project/vllm#50629 touch other parts of the kernel file and/or append tests; vllm-project/vllm#64783 and vllm-project/vllm#64534 touch only the test file.

Whichever lands second needs a mechanical rebase.

## Claims

- On XPU, `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` unset (the default) or `1` loads the Q / Q-PE tiles of the 576/512 MLA tile (one KV head) through descriptors. `0` keeps the pointer load. Outputs are bit-identical to the pointer load. The 288/256 tile keeps the pointer load for now: with descriptors its kernel-level result is mixed (faster on 8 of 12 shapes, 5.2-6.5% slower on the other 4), and no 288/256 model was run end to end.
- On 2× Intel Arc Pro B60 (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, TP=2, TRITON_MLA), the decode step is 4.3-6.0% faster at batch 1 and 17.7-24.0% faster at batch 8/32. Serve median TPOT drops by 4.4% / 17.7% / 22.2% at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. gsm8k showed no significant difference (1 run per arm, see Accuracy).
- Per launch, the kernel is faster on all 24 bf16 and all 12 fp8-KV shapes of the 576/512 tile (table below, default arm).
- CUDA/ROCm: no behaviour change. The descriptor branch is a `tl.constexpr` that is always `False` there, and the gate checks the platform before reading the env var. `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` does not enable this path outside XPU.

## Validation

Software: image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:14d76deea7c2abab18ce13f0031c8fc765736a39bdd4252014fa1255b2c1db88` (vLLM `3966924d5`, torch 2.14.0+xpu, triton-xpu 3.8.0 as pinned in `requirements/xpu.txt`, IGC 2.38.2, compute-runtime 26.27.39122.11). The image's `triton_decode_attention.py` is byte-identical to `main` before this PR. Every run puts a copy of the measured revision of that file (and of the test file for pytest) first on `PYTHONPATH` (XPU) or over the image's install (CUDA).

Unit tests on this revision (rebased on `main` `377c4d7e5b`; kernel file md5 `8705448e`, test file md5 `bbba0d77`, `vllm/triton_utils/tensor_descriptor.py` md5 `38a11798`), with images built from vLLM `8ca766326`, whose other files used here match `main`: XPU `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:45096d16dab790ced3c0c622ed9a1854d2020683864a93da4eff85b9b1b55154` (torch 2.15.0+xpu, triton-xpu 3.9.0, IGC 2.40.16), CUDA `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:b6d1cfc60cce1f6405d37ea77645a36a46065230fb643abc2eeb93a5dc8fb79b` (torch 2.14.0, triton 3.8.0):

```bash
env -u VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0 pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1 pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
```

| device | unset | `0` | `1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1× Intel Arc Pro B60 | 142 passed, 147 skipped | 142 passed, 147 skipped | 142 passed, 147 skipped |
| 1× NVIDIA H200 (sm90) | 142 passed, 147 skipped | 142 passed, 147 skipped | 142 passed, 147 skipped |

146 skips are the ROCm-only verify tests; the other is the fp8-KV non-MLA case, which is not wired. B200 was not re-run on this revision. The tests ran from a directory without a `vllm/` source tree, with the kernel and test files imported from a copy (the printed `vllm.__file__` and file md5s were checked in every run).

ROCm was not run. `test_decode_attention_mla_tensor_descriptor` covers the 576/512 descriptor path (32 and 8 heads, bf16 and fp8 KV) and the pointer fallbacks (288/256, GQA, non-MLA, row stride not 16-byte aligned, base pointer not 16-byte aligned; 13 passed and 1 skipped per run). For each case it asserts that `_use_q_tensor_descriptor()`, whose result the launcher passes as `USE_TD`, equals "XPU and not `0`", that the output equals the pointer load bit for bit, and that it matches a float32 torch reference. `test_use_q_tensor_descriptor_strided_last_dim` checks that a Q with a strided last dim keeps the pointer load; it checks the decision only, because the kernel reads that dim with unit stride on every path. `test_use_q_tensor_descriptor_warmup_fake_tensor` checks the decision on the FakeTensors JIT warmup passes, for an aligned and a misaligned one, without reading their data pointer. On CUDA, `=1` selects the pointer path (the test asserts it), so the CUDA columns show that the kernel is unchanged there; they do not validate the descriptor path. On H200 and B200, the TTIR, TTGIR and PTX of `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (line info stripped) are identical to `main` for five shapes at unset/0/1 (checked before the rebase).

Kernel time on 1× Intel Arc Pro B60, kernel file of this PR. Measured with kernel file md5 `546fc408`. Since then the gate was narrowed (`Lk in (576, 288)` to `Lk == 576`) and `main` added a `SLIDING_WINDOW` constexpr to the kernel, which is 0 on this path. A re-measurement of the current `@triton.jit` kernel with triton-xpu 3.9.0 (same shapes, `torch.profiler` device time, 3 processes x 5 rounds) gave a median of -6.9% for 576/512 bf16, with 20 of 24 shapes faster and batch 32 at 1k context 4.7-8.1% slower, and -9.3% for fp8 KV (12 of 12 faster). Method: `torch.profiler` device time per launch, page 16, `num_kv_splits` as chosen by TRITON_MLA. Runs: 3 processes with a fresh Triton cache × 5 rounds, median of medians. Spread is (max-min)/median of the process medians, at most 8.3% and below 4% on most shapes. The TD arm is the shipped default (variable unset); baseline is TD `0`, which is within -0.1% (median) of `main`.

| tile (Lk/Lv) | KV | shapes (heads × batch 1/8/32 × context 1k/8k) | faster with TD | change vs TD `0` | median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 576/512 | bf16 | 24 (heads 16/8/4/2) | 24/24 | -7.6% … -32.5% | -10.3% |
| 576/512 | fp8 e4m3 | 12 (heads 16/8) | 12/12 | -6.9% … -28.7% | -8.8% |

End to end on 2× Intel Arc Pro B60: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` revision `85864749cd`, TP=2, bf16, bf16 KV, `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA`, `max_model_len=5120`, no prefix caching, seed 42, default XPU graphs. Only `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` differs between arms: `0` (pointer load) vs unset (the default, descriptor load). Arms run interleaved in the order 0, unset, unset, 0.

These runs used an earlier revision of the kernel file (https://github.com/afierka-intel/vllm/commit/6672eaf2d7); later revisions narrow the gate to `Lk == 576`, which is the only shape this model uses, and take the `SLIDING_WINDOW` constexpr from `main` (0 here). Before the rebase, compiling the stage-1 kernel with the earlier and the then-final file on the same B60 gives identical Triton cache keys for the TD-off arm (5 of 5 variants) and for the 4 descriptor variants of the unset arm; the fifth (288/256) is now a pointer variant with the TD-off key, as intended. So the 576/512 E2E rows below applied to the pre-rebase file. The Triton cache of every `0` process holds only pointer variants of the kernel, and of every unset process only descriptor variants. `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` at input 4096, batch 8 gives a 157.1 ms decode step, the same as unset (157.5 ms).

Latency (output 256). Runs: 2 processes × 4 timed iterations after 1 warm-up = 8 values per arm. Batch 1 was repeated with 2 more processes per arm in BAAB order (4 processes per arm pooled): 1024 × 1: 22.7 -> 21.7 ms (-4.3%), 4096 × 1: 43.9 -> 41.1 ms (-6.3%); the 4 process medians per arm are separated, exact permutation p = 0.029 in both cases (smallest possible with 4 vs 4). Decode step = (latency at 256 output tokens - latency at 1 output token) / 255. Spread is (max-min)/median of the decode step.

| input | batch | latency s, TD `0` -> unset | decode step ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | spread `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 5.90 -> 5.65 | 22.7 -> 21.7 | -4.3% | 3.4% / 3.8% |
| 1024 | 8 | 22.80 -> 18.87 | 87.0 -> 71.6 | -17.7% | 3.7% / 4.4% |
| 1024 | 32 | 65.47 -> 51.34 | 248.0 -> 192.6 | -22.3% | 1.0% / 1.2% |
| 4096 | 1 | 11.49 -> 10.82 | 43.7 -> 41.1 | -6.0% | 2.3% / 2.9% |
| 4096 | 8 | 53.43 -> 42.54 | 200.2 -> 157.5 | -21.3% | 1.3% / 1.4% |
| 4096 | 32 (see note) | 188.07 -> 145.28 | 700.3 -> 532.5 | -24.0% | 1.5% / 1.0% |

Note on 4096 × 32: KV capacity is 91,488 tokens, so the engine ran 21-22 requests at a time (the rest waited); it is a valid A/B but not a batch-32 decode step.

Serve (random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`). Runs: 2 servers per arm × 2 runs after 1 warm-up = 4 values per arm. Every run completed all prompts.

| concurrency | prompts | median TPOT ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | output tok/s, TD `0` -> unset | change | spread TPOT `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 | 22.70 -> 21.71 | -4.4% | 43.1 -> 45.1 | +4.5% | 3.4% / 3.6% |
| 8 | 32 | 85.79 -> 70.64 | -17.7% | 90.6 -> 109.5 | +20.9% | 1.5% / 1.2% |
| 32 | 128 | 248.99 -> 193.77 | -22.2% | 126.1 -> 161.6 | +28.2% | 0.4% / 0.8% |

Accuracy: gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, lm-eval 0.4.12, greedy, seed 42, TP=2 TRITON_MLA. 4 independent processes per arm (3 on the final kernel file, 1 earlier on the same Triton cache keys), TD `0` vs TD unset (this PR):

| arm | strict-match per process | mean (range) | flexible-extract mean (range) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TD `0` | 0.6634, 0.6626, 0.6588, 0.6664 | 66.28% (65.88-66.64) | 66.85% (66.49-67.32) |
| TD unset (this PR) | 0.6588, 0.6558, 0.6664, 0.6603 | 66.03% (65.58-66.64) | 66.72% (66.26-67.17) |
| FlashAttnMLA (default backend), TD unset, 1 process | 0.6641 | | 0.6702 |

Each process has stderr ±0.0130. The noise floor is measured with TD-off vs TD-off pairs: the strict-match difference between two processes is 0.00-1.06 pt (median 0.38) for TD `0` vs unset, 0.08-0.76 pt (median 0.38) for TD `0` vs TD `0`, and 0.15-1.06 pt (median 0.53) for unset vs unset. Paired exact McNemar p ≥ 0.12 for every one of the 28 process pairs, TD `0` vs TD `0` included. Identical generations out of 1319 are 674-752 for every pair, and no higher for TD `0` vs TD `0` than for TD `0` vs unset. So generations are not reproducible across processes on this setup, and the TD-vs-pointer difference is inside that run-to-run noise. This does not prove a zero drop; it shows none that is resolvable at this sample size.

Default XPU MLA backend vs TRITON_MLA, decode step ms (same job and setup; FlashAttnMLA: 1 process × 4 iterations):

| input × batch | FlashAttnMLA (default) | TRITON_MLA, TD `0` | TRITON_MLA, TD unset (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 × 8 | 23.9 | 87.0 | 71.6 |
| 4096 × 8 | 25.1 | 200.2 | 157.5 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands (E2E)</summary>

The latency and gsm8k numbers came from one process per arm. Each process ran the `vllm bench latency` loop for all six configs, plus lm-eval (Python API) on the same engine. The equivalent CLI commands are:

```bash
export VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0   # TD arm: unset VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD
M=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
COMMON="--tensor-parallel-size 2 --attention-backend TRITON_MLA --max-model-len 5120 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code --seed 42 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9"

# latency; repeat with --output-len 1 for the decode-step estimate
vllm bench latency --model $M $COMMON --input-len 4096 --output-len 256 --batch-size 8 \
  --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 4

# serve
vllm serve $M --served-model-name dsv2lite $COMMON
vllm bench serve --model dsv2lite --tokenizer $M --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 42 --temperature 0

# accuracy
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=$M,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=2,attention_backend=TRITON_MLA,max_model_len=5120,enable_prefix_caching=False,trust_remote_code=True,seed=42,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 42
```

</details>

CI gap: no CI job runs the descriptor path of this PR. `.buildkite/intel_jobs/kernels_intel.yaml` has no step for `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py`, and the CUDA (L4, sm89) and ROCm (MI300, `optional: true`) "Attention Kernels" steps run the file on the pointer path only. The XPU results above come from local runs. Intel CI for the current head: pending when this was written.

Fallback configuration (no `--attention-backend`, `--block-size 16`): the engine log shows `FlashAttnMLA on XPU is not valid for this configuration (('block_size not supported',)); falling back to Triton MLA backend`. Same model, flags and methodology as above, arms interleaved 0, unset, unset, 0 (decode step: 1 process per arm-slot, 2 per arm):

| input | batch | decode step ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | process medians `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 22.7 -> 22.3 | -2.0% | 22.4, 23.0 / 22.3, 22.3 |
| 1024 | 8 | 87.2 -> 73.1 | -16.1% | 86.5, 87.4 / 73.2, 73.0 |
| 4096 | 1 | 43.9 -> 41.6 | -5.4% | 43.4, 44.2 / 41.6, 41.5 |
| 4096 | 8 | 199.9 -> 158.2 | -20.9% | 199.6, 200.9 / 158.5, 158.1 |

(The 1024 × 8 unset spread of 42.3% is a single outlier iteration; both process medians are 73.0-73.2 ms.) Serve, same setup (4 values per arm, all prompts completed): median TPOT 22.75 -> 21.73 ms (-4.5%) at concurrency 1, 85.79 -> 70.82 ms (-17.5%) at 8, 248.70 -> 193.90 ms (-22.0%) at 32. fp8 KV is the other fallback case and was not measured end to end (next paragraph).

fp8 KV: covered by the unit tests only. End to end, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` does not run on XPU today, for a reason unrelated to this PR: the MLA layer passes `skip_scale=True` when the checkpoint has no KV scales, and `concat_and_cache_mla` raises `NotImplementedError("skip_scale is not supported on XPU")`.

## Details

- **Why it is faster:** on XPU, the masked pointer load of the 16 × 512 Q tile lowers to an SLM relayout (288 SLM `d16u32` loads in the 576/512 kernel). The descriptor load lowers to 18 2D block reads that land directly in the DPAS operand layout, and the relayout disappears (288/256: 9 block reads, 144 SLM loads removed). With TP=2 on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, stage 1 is 83-87% of decode device time at input 4096 with batch 8/32, and its per-launch time drops from 8.08 ms to 6.08 ms at input 4096, batch 8 (`torch.profiler`, eager).
- **Gate:** `_use_q_tensor_descriptor(q, k_buffer, is_mla)`: `is_xpu() and is_mla and Lk == 576` with one KV head, `use_tensor_descriptor()`, and `tensor_descriptor_compatible(q)` from vllm-project/vllm#60801 (unit last stride, 16-byte-aligned base, row width and pitches multiples of 16 B and at least 64 B, pitches not below the row width). JIT warmup calls it with FakeTensors, so `tensor_descriptor_compatible()` now takes their alignment from the `_vllm_warmup_aligned` mark the warmup sets instead of reading their data pointer, which is deprecated for FakeTensors. The platform check comes first, so CUDA/ROCm do no env lookup. `use_tensor_descriptor()` supplies the `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` tri-state (unset: on for XPU, `0`: off), as in vllm-project/vllm#46340 and vllm-project/vllm#47205. Unlike those, this kernel's descriptor path is XPU-only: `1` does not force it on CUDA/ROCm, where it has not been validated. `vllm/envs.py` is not changed.
- **Masking:** with one KV head, the kernel's row mask reduces to `row < q_head_num`, and the descriptor's bounds pad exactly those rows with zeros. `BLOCK_DMODEL` is below `Lk`, so the column mask is all-true, and the Q-PE descriptor starts at column `BLOCK_DMODEL`. That is why the results match bit for bit. Descriptor loads take no `.ca` cache hint.
- **No allocator needed:** every XPU descriptor build here has `global_scratch_size = 0`, so no `triton.set_allocator` call is added.
- **Tradeoffs and limits:**
  - The 288/256 tile is mixed with descriptors: faster on 8 of 12 shapes (batch 1 at 1k and 8k context, batch 8/32 at 1k context), 5.2-6.5% slower on the other 4 (batch 8/32 at 8k context), and no 288/256 model was run end to end. It is left out of the gate until the slowdown is understood.
  - Only Intel Arc Pro B60 was measured; B70 and B580 were not.
  - The kernel spills about 98 KB on XPU in both paths. The descriptor load does not change that (576/512: 97,920 B vs 99,584 B).
  - Tuning `num_warps` (2/4/8) and the GRF mode did not beat the pointer path's gain from this change, and did not improve the descriptor path beyond `num_warps=4`.
  - gsm8k generations are not reproducible across processes on this setup even with the same compiled kernel (see Accuracy for the measured TD-off vs TD-off noise floor).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Render image and text parts in request order
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Python frontend, a Kimi-K3 / K3.1 chat message with images is not rendered the way the checkpoint's own processor renders it: every image is moved to the front of its message and followed by a `\n`. This PR renders the parts in request order with no separator, so the prompt is token-identical to the checkpoint's reference. Text-only messages with several parts now render the same way (third commit, from review). It also makes the K3 multimodal processor match image placeholders at token level only, with no text fallback.

## Claims

- Each image no longer costs one extra newline token, and text placed before an image stays before it.
- Chat prompts with images are token-identical to the checkpoint's `AutoProcessor` (new test), including all 13 vision cases of the Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV) prompt-token suite.
- Prompts with string content and no images are unchanged (58 KVV text cases: identical token ids before and after).
- Messages with several text parts render them with no separator and tokenize each part on its own, as `encoding_k3.py` and the Rust frontend do. This includes tool messages, which chat parsing had already joined with `\n`.
- The K3 / K3.1 multimodal processor no longer falls back to decoding and re-encoding the prompt when an image placeholder is not found in the token ids. It raises `PromptUpdateMismatchError` instead.
- Text prompts with images (offline `LLM.generate`, dummy inputs for profiling) keep working and produce the same token ids as before.
- No measurable score change: OCRBench 0.893 with the fix vs 0.887 without (n=1000 each).

## Validation

Tests were run on commit `5beb6783ad` (two commits on base `f2f9edcac3`), CPU only. The compiled extensions came from a main build at `8c17e4692a`, which is older than the base; the changed code is pure Python.

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py -q \
  --deselect tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py::test_mm_device_do_normalize
# this PR:                                  42 passed, 1 deselected
# first commit's tests on main (renderer):   3 failed, 37 passed, 1 deselected
#   FAILED test_chat_prompt_matches_hf_processor[interleaved]
#   FAILED test_chat_prompt_matches_hf_processor[markup_text_in_history]
#   FAILED test_chat_placeholder_text_is_not_an_image_slot
```

Third commit (`c546cf2266`, review fix for text-only parts), same environment except numpy 2.4.6 as pinned in `requirements/test/cuda.txt`:

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py -q \
  --deselect tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py::test_mm_device_do_normalize
# c546cf2266:                       43 passed, 1 deselected, 16 warnings in 41.72s
# same tests, renderer at 8ce3060b72: 2 failed, 41 passed, 1 deselected, 16 warnings in 41.06s
#   FAILED test_render_messages_keeps_text_parts_separate
#   FAILED test_chat_prompt_matches_hf_processor[text_parts_without_images]
```

I also compared the rendered tokens against the checkpoint's `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` on 27 edge cases (text, `input_text`, `output_text`, `refusal`, `thinking`, bare string and `None`-text parts, `tool_reference`, empty lists, billing-header system parts, for user, system, assistant and tool). 24 match token for token. The two image cases are unchanged from the second commit and covered by the `AutoProcessor` test above. A `developer` message still raises, as before.

For the second commit, with a counter on `BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates_via_text`: 0 calls over 1237 text-prompt, token-id-prompt, truncation and dummy-input cases per model, on Kimi-K3 and on the Kimi-K3.1-Pro tokenizer. Without the change the same cases use the fallback 749 times. All 149 text prompts whose placeholder count equals the image count give identical token ids and image ranges before and after, and match the checkpoint's `AutoProcessor(medias=..., text=...)`.

The deselected test needs a GPU and was not run. The new tests live in two existing test files that CI already runs. There is no server-level test with real weights: the parity test drives `renderer_from_config(...).render_chat`, the path `/v1/chat/completions` uses, with the checkpoint's real tokenizer and processor, which is the lightest path that reproduces the bug for a checkpoint of this size.

`pre-commit run --files <the changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering).

Model evaluation, Kimi-K3 on 8x MI355X, TP8, FP8 KV cache, Python frontend, KVV OCRBench (n=1000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking effort max):

| Tree | OCRBench | Prompt tokens per request |
|---|---|---|
| without the fix | 0.887 ± 0.010 (887/1000) | baseline |
| with the fix | 0.893 ± 0.010 (893/1000) | exactly 1 fewer on all 1000 requests |

These runs predate the second and third commits. The second does not change chat prompts. The third only changes messages with more than one text part and was not evaluated separately. The difference is inside one standard error (paired exact McNemar p = 0.33). Both runs used a development build at main as of 2026-11-07 plus unrelated ROCm commits. The "with the fix" server carried this renderer change together with our other local K3 frontend fixes (reasoning parser, tool parser, strict tool schema, transparent images), so it is not an isolated A/B of this change. MMMU Pro was not re-run with the fix.

<details>
<summary>KVV prompt-token cases (CPU, renderer + multimodal processor vs the checkpoint's processor)</summary>

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 13 vision cases, tokens vs KVV expected count | +4 to +13 | +3 on all 13 (the generation prompt) |
| 13 vision cases, token ids equal to the checkpoint's processor | 0 / 13 | 13 / 13 |
| 58 text cases, token ids | baseline | identical on all 58 |

Note for KVV users: its `--think-mode opensource` prompt-token rule currently expects one extra token per image for vLLM ("root cause under investigation"). With this PR those 13 cases come out exactly at the first-party count, so that offset has to go.

</details>

## Details

Root cause: `KimiK3Renderer` parsed messages with `content_format="string"`. vLLM then prepends the image placeholders to the message text and joins everything with `\n`. K3's encoder (`encoding_k3.py`) and the Rust frontend render content parts in order with no separator. As a side effect the placeholder merged with the newline at token level, so the token-level placeholder match failed and every image prompt took the slower text fallback of the prompt updates. With this PR the match succeeds directly.

Fix: parse with `content_format="openai"` and pass message content to the native encoder as part lists. For tool messages, chat parsing joins text-only content with `\n` before the renderer sees it, so `_keep_k3_content_parts` rebuilds those parts from the request with the parser's own part reader.

Second commit: K3 has no token for an image slot. `<|kimi_image_placeholder|>` is 8 ordinary tokens, also in the checkpoint's own encoder. When a text prompt is tokenized in one piece, the first or last of those tokens can merge with the neighbouring text (`"Describe " + placeholder`, or two placeholders in a row), so the placeholder is not found in the token ids. The processor then decoded the whole prompt, substituted the images in the text and encoded it again. K3 prompts are tokenized segment by segment and cannot be rebuilt from their text, so this PR removes that step for K3:

- `encode_k3_text_prompt` tokenizes a text prompt with every placeholder encoded on its own. It is used for text prompts that carry images (`KimiK3Renderer._tokenize_prompt`), for the dummy inputs, and when the processor is called with a string.
- `KimiK3MultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates` matches at token level only.

The image block starts and ends with special tokens, which already split the text during tokenization, so the resulting ids are the same as before.

Behaviour changes to be aware of:

- Prompts passed as token ids together with images must contain the placeholder's token ids once per image (`tokenizer.encode("<|kimi_image_placeholder|>", add_special_tokens=False)`). Token ids produced by encoding the whole text in one call, where the placeholder merged with the text around it, used to be repaired by the text fallback and are now rejected with `PromptUpdateMismatchError`. Pass the text prompt instead, or build the ids piece by piece.
- A text prompt with more placeholders than images now gives the images to the first placeholders in order. Before, the image went to whichever placeholder happened to tokenize cleanly.
- For a text prompt with images that is longer than the context, the error reports the exact token count instead of "at least N". One truncation case that already failed now fails with `PromptUpdateMismatchError` instead of the split-image validation error; both are 400-class.

- Adjacent text parts are concatenated with no separator, with or without images (as the checkpoint and the Rust frontend do). On main they were joined with `\n`.
- Not covered: `/v1/messages` joins multi-part `tool_result` text with `\n` in `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, before the renderer runs, so those still carry the newline.
- Text that spells `<|kimi_image_placeholder|>` is no longer used as a manual image slot in the common case; the image stays where its image part is. A text part that starts exactly with that string can still be matched as the slot, as on main.
- `--interleave-mm-strings` no longer has an effect for K3; parts are always in order.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes how K3 places images. #69256 and #66849 (video input) and #50543 / #53148 (tool arguments, developer role) edit neighbouring lines of `vllm/renderers/kimi_k3.py` but keep `content_format="string"`. Whichever of this PR and a video PR lands second needs a small rebase: video parts must be turned into text parts carrying the video placeholder in `_keep_k3_content_parts`, otherwise the native encoder rejects them.

No docs change: no flag, field or default is added.

AI assistance was used to write this change.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] SM100/SM103 skinny GEMM plans for Qwen3, Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE and Qwen3.8 decode projections
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds B200 (SM100) and B300 (SM103) cuteDSL skinny-GEMM plans for the BF16 decode projections of the Qwen3 family. It is table-only: no kernel or dispatch code changes, and shapes and token counts that are not listed keep cuBLAS.

At 1–8 tokens these projections run cuBLAS split-K (`nvjet_*_splitK` + `splitKreduce`, or `dot_kernel` + `reduce_1Block_kernel` for N = 1), at about 5 µs each for the small ones, where the skinny kernel takes 2–4 µs.

Per review feedback on #69750, the small-GEMM tuning PRs are folded into this one: #69743 (dense Qwen3), #69773 (Qwen3 MoE) and #69750 (Qwen3.8 router / LM head). Those are closed in favor of this PR. Further small-GEMM tuning will be added here rather than opened separately.

One commit per part:

| # | Commit | Table | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE | new `SM100_SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS` in `skinny_gemm_plans.py`, registered for `(10, 0)` | GDN `in_proj_ba`, shared-expert gate, router, LM head. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B TP1/2/4, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4/8. 14 shapes / 49 entries |
| 2 | B300 | registers the same table for `(10, 3)` | one line |
| 3 | dense Qwen3 | same table | qkv, o, gate_up, down, LM head. Qwen3-8B TP1/2, Qwen3-14B TP1/2/4, Qwen3-32B TP1/2/4/8. 41 shapes / 91 entries |
| 4 | Qwen3 MoE | same table | attention qkv / o, router, LM head. Qwen3-30B-A3B TP1/2/4, Qwen3-235B-A22B TP4/8. 15 shapes / 49 entries |
| 5 | Qwen3.8 | `QWEN4_EXP_SM100_GEMM_PLANS` in `low_latency_gemm.py` | router `(512, 2560)` at M = 2/8, TP4 LM head `(62080, 2560)` at M = 2, and a retuned M = 1 entry. +8/−5 lines |

**Selection rule** (parts 1, 3, 4, 5): an entry is kept only where the plan beat cuBLAS by at least 10% in a sweep and again in a separate verification. The verification used 4 seeds × 3 interleaved rounds, CUPTI, CUDA graph replay and a cold L2. Error against an fp32 reference equals cuBLAS's on every entry (max 3.8e-3).

## Results: this branch vs current main

This is the head of this branch, `ce7e3d5dd7`, against `main` at `04f0149d47`, on 1× B200 per arm with real weights.

Method:
- `main` and this PR are served **at the same time**, one GPU each.
- Short `vllm bench serve` bursts alternate between them: random 512 in / 512 out, `--ignore-eos`, 5 × concurrency prompts, order flipped each round, 6 rounds per concurrency.
- Both servers then restart with the GPUs swapped, and the bursts run again.
- The table shows the mean of the two passes (median TPOT). That cancels the GPU-to-GPU difference, which is up to a few percent at c1 on this node.
- `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`; the "Directly load AOT" count was 0 in every server log.

| Model (TP=1) | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | Pairs where the PR is faster, c1–c4 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | **−16.7%** | **−14.9%** | −2.2% | −0.2% | 36 / 36 | 0.907 → 0.908 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | **−12.1%** | **−10.5%** | −5.2% | −4.8% | 36 / 36 | 0.928 → 0.926 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 | −1.4% | −2.3% | **−6.2%** | **−4.6%** | 44 / 44 | 0.963 → 0.961 |

- Qwen3.6 c1 and c2 come from a separate run with 8 rounds per pass, on a different GPU pair with nothing else running.
- No concurrency regressed. The per-part tables below were measured on the individual commits before they were folded and rebased.

## Results: end to end

Setup for all runs:
- Real weights unless noted.
- `vllm serve --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, with `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`. The "Directly load AOT" count was 0 in every server log.
- `vllm bench serve`, random 512 in / 512 out, `--ignore-eos`.
- Base and PR alternate twice.
- The table shows median TPOT, mean Δ vs base.

Each part was measured against the commit before it, so each row is that part alone.

**B200**

| Part | Model | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | GSM8K base → PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 TP1 | −1.2% | −2.6% | **−5.7%** | **−4.7%** | 0.964 / 0.964 → 0.964 / 0.961 |
| 3 | Qwen3-8B TP1 | **−16.7%** | **−14.9%** | −1.8% | +0.2% | 0.908 / 0.905 → 0.904 / 0.907 |
| 3 | Qwen3-32B TP8 | **−14.0%** | **−10.4%** | −4.8% | −2.9% | 0.948 / 0.944 → 0.944 / 0.946 |
| 4 | Qwen3-30B-A3B TP1 | **−10.1%** | **−10.7%** | −3.5% | −6.2% | 0.926 / 0.926 → 0.927 / 0.926 |
| 4 | Qwen3-235B-A22B TP8 + EP, dummy weights | **−11.0%** | **−10.2%** | −5.9% | −1.6% | — |
| 5 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 TEP4, 1k / 1k | −0.1% | **−3.0%** | −0.0% | −0.8% | 0.966 / 0.970 → 0.970 / 0.969 |

Notes:
- **Dense Qwen3 at more TP sizes.** An earlier run also gave Qwen3-32B TP1 −15.7% and TP4 −17.5% at c1, with GSM8K unchanged.
- **Dense Qwen3 at c4–c8.** The gain is largest at c1–c2. Most decode batches at c4–c8 are 4–8 tokens, where cuBLAS is already competitive and fewer entries pass the 10% bar.
- **Part 1 at c1.** The shared-expert gate runs on the aux CUDA stream at decode, overlapped with the routed experts, so its entries are off the critical path there. The gain comes from the router, `in_proj_ba` and the LM head. The gate entries are kept for the cases where the shared expert runs on the main stream: EPLB with some backends, fully sharded LoRA, and `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM`.
- **Part 5 setup.** Recipe flags (TP4 + EP, fp8 KV cache, fp8 indexer cache), no speculative decoding, 1k in / 1k out. With the MTP3 drafter, `vllm bench forward` gives −3.4% at 2 decode tokens and −0.9% at 8. Router M = 4 / 16 and LM head M = 4 were measured and left out: they win at the kernel level but showed no gain or a loss in the full forward.

**B300** (part 1 + part 2, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, `main` vs the table registered for `(10, 3)`)

| | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | GSM8K base → PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TP1 | −2.4% | −3.2% | **−11.5%** | −3.7% | 0.964 / 0.958 → 0.964 / 0.964 |
| TP2 | −3.8% | | | **−5.1%** | 0.961 / 0.958 → 0.959 / 0.962 |

- The c4 gain at TP1 reproduced in a second set (−10.8%). Base TPOT rises unusually steeply from c2 to c4 on B300, and the plan removes that step.
- The two TP2 c1 base runs differ by 3%, so that delta is between −2.3% and −5.2%.

## Results: kernel level

Speedup over cuBLAS, as the median of 4 seeds × 3 interleaved rounds:

| Part | B200 | B300 |
|---|---|---|
| 1, Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE (49) | 1.11–3.29× | all 49 ≥ 1.10× |
| 3, dense Qwen3 (91) | 1.10–2.59×, median 1.25× | 85 ≥ 1.10×; 6 at 1.05–1.10×; none slower |
| 4, Qwen3 MoE (49) | 1.15–2.38×, median 1.44× | 1.13–2.49× |
| 5, Qwen3.8 router / LM head (4) | router 1.99× / 1.66× (M = 2/8); LM head 1.07× / 1.27× (M = 1/2) | not registered for SM103 |

- **One table for B200 and B300.** A separate sweep on B300 found SM103-specific winners for part 1's 49 cells. The B200 configs range from 2.7% faster to 4.9% slower than those, with a median difference of 0, so a separate SM103 table is not worth it.
- **The six dense entries at 1.05–1.10× on B300** are (1280, 5120) M=8; (5120, 1024), (5120, 1280) and (5120, 2048) at M=2; and the Qwen3-14B LM head (151936, 5120) at M=1 and M=2. Their spread over seeds is at most 0.02. They are kept because they are still faster than cuBLAS.
- **Routing.**
  - The N = 1 shared-expert gate needs no dispatch change to reach the skinny kernel on SM100. This was checked by logging the `shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm` calls during a Qwen3.6 run.
  - The Qwen3-MoE and Qwen3.8 routers reach these tables because their `GateLinear` has no `out_dtype` and a BF16 weight. They take the base `ReplicatedLinear` forward, and profiles confirm the swap.

## Testing

On B200 at the head of this branch, on main 04f0149d47:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -q
699 passed, 471 skipped
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k "plans_are_valid or qwen4_exp" -q
476 passed, 99 skipped
```

pre-commit passes. The E2E numbers above were measured on the individual commits before they were folded and rebased. The diff of each part is unchanged.

## Duplicates and overlap

- **#64982** (open): SM90 plans and an eager fast path for Qwen3.5 MoE.
- **#64979** (SM90 dense), **#65306** (SM90 GLM-5.3-Flash) and **#67622** (SM120 GLM-5.3-Flash), all open: each adds a table to `skinny_gemm_plans.py` and one line to `SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY`. Whichever lands second gets a one-line conflict.
- **#57848** (open): SM103 router entries in the Qwen3.8 table. Part 5 is SM100 only.
- No other open or merged PR adds SM100 or SM103 entries to the generic table.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code, three cooperating sessions on B200 and B300 nodes) was used to identify the layers, run the sweeps and benchmarks, and draft this change and description. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix AFMoE router precision and output-head loading
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Align AFMoE BF16 router computation with the reference implementation and pass the output-head prefix so ModelOpt honors `lm_head` quantization exclusions. The output-head fix from #68263 is included here; that PR is closed as a duplicate.

## Claims

- Use BF16 router weights and projection outputs for unquantized and ModelOpt NVFP4 BF16 loads, then promote logits to FP32 for expert selection.
- Preserve FP32 expert correction biases and existing FP32 routers for FP16, FP32 and other quantization paths.
- Honor checkpoint output-head quantization exclusions through the existing prefix mechanism.

## Validation

The submitted diff contains only `afmoe.py`. The router and output-head changes are unchanged from `33cced53`; the results below were collected on that revision. Public Trinity Nano loading/generation checks passed on H100/Humming and native NVFP4 GB300/FlashInfer CUTLASS; BF16, FP16, FP32 and FP8 cases passed. Local formatting, lint and type checks passed on cleanup revision `999e32739`. Upstream CI is checking the refreshed base.

On 512 zero-shot HellaSwag examples, NVFP4 normalized accuracy changed from 333/512 to 335/512; raw accuracy changed from 267/512 to 262/512. These mixed subset results do not establish quality parity.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and output</summary>

NVFP4 checkpoint: `arcee-ai/Trinity-Nano-Preview-NVFP4` at `6ffbc24c4d58965cc505401f2189272fd976503c`. The following results were collected at `33cced53` against `2159dc66` (the unquantized BF16 fix plus the output-head fix). The test files remain available at `33cced53` for reproduction; they are omitted from the submitted diff. Copy the same test into the baseline checkout for the before/after comparison. No checkpoint edits or model-configuration patches.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py -v -k 'afmoe and humming'
# Native NVFP4 on GB300:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py -v -k 'afmoe and flashinfer_cutlass'
```


commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Allow only the Omni shared span among overlapping multimodal placeholders
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preprocessed multimodal features (`features` on `/inference/v1/generate`, and the Rust gRPC preprocessed features) carry each item's placeholder range in the prompt. The Python frontend rejected every overlap between ranges, including the shape its own render step produces for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni with `use_audio_in_video=True`, while the Rust frontend accepted every overlap, including partial and nested ranges the engine cannot handle. This PR gives both frontends one rule: ranges must not overlap, except that items of different modalities may share one span when their `is_embed` masks are disjoint.

## Claims

- Python `/inference/v1/generate` now accepts the Omni audio-in-video features that Python's own `/render` produces, so rendering such a request and handing it to `/generate` no longer fails with "mm_placeholders must be globally non-overlapping and sorted".
- Both frontends reject every other overlap (partial, nested, same start with another length, same modality, or intersecting `is_embed` masks) as a request validation error: 400 on HTTP, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on Rust gRPC. Before this PR, the Rust frontend passed such features to the engine.
- An absent `is_embed` mask counts as covering every position of its range.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on `df81d7583b` based on `ab1c06419c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # bans ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2904 tests run: 2904 passed, 13 skipped
```

Python, on `df81d7583b`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py -q
# 43 passed, 2 warnings in 10.56s
```

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, typos and the other hooks) passed on the commit.

- Rust (`multimodal::preprocessed` tests): the Omni shape (a video and an audio item on one span with complementary masks) is accepted, and seven rejected shapes are pinned (`inline_features_reject_other_overlaps`).
- Python: `test_multimodal_features_accept_a_span_shared_across_modalities` (new) and `test_multimodal_features_reject_overlapping_placeholders` (now six cases).
- Red-green: with the Rust check disabled, `inline_features_reject_other_overlaps` fails; with the Python change reverted, `test_multimodal_features_accept_a_span_shared_across_modalities` fails, because the old check rejects the Omni shape.

## Details

- **Root cause, Python.** The check from vllm-project/vllm#51898 rejects any overlap. The Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni processors put a video and its audio track on the identical span (same offset and length) and separate them with complementary `is_embed` masks (`_derive_audio_from_video_placeholders` in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py` and `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py`), and `/render` forwards those masks (`mm_features.py`).
- **Root cause, Rust.** Since vllm-project/vllm#55047 the Rust frontend accepts any overlap. The engine assumes otherwise: `get_mm_features_in_window` (`vllm/multimodal/utils.py`, used by the scheduler, block pool and encoder runners) bisects features sorted by offset on the assumption that their ends are sorted too. Identical spans keep that order and nested spans break it. With ranges `[0,6)` and `[1,3)` and window `[4,5)`, it returns `(2,2)` and omits the outer feature.
- **Why this rule.** The shared span is the only overlap any processor produces. The rule depends only on ranges, modalities and masks, not on the model.
- **Layering.** Each frontend already validates the ranges in one place, and the rule goes there. In Python, that is `MultiModalFeatures`' validator in `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py`: it groups spans by `(offset, length)`, and its error message keeps "non-overlapping". In Rust, it is `validate_features` (behind `MultimodalModelInfo::prepare_preprocessed`, shared by HTTP and gRPC) in `rust/src/chat/src/multimodal/preprocessed.rs`. After sorting by offset, its new `validate_overlaps` walks the features once, groups identical spans, and checks modalities and masks within each group. The new check returns the existing `Error::InvalidPreprocessedMultimodal`. That variant's request-error classification (400 / `INVALID_ARGUMENT`) is already shared by its other triggers, so the tests pin the rule at the validator level.
- **Test replaced.** One Rust test pinned an image and a video on one Qwen3-VL range with intersecting masks. No processor produces that shape. It is replaced by the Omni shape and the rejected shapes.
- **Python tests and the Rust e2e lane.** The Python tests are unit tests of the request model. No server-level test sends Omni audio-in-video features, so nothing changes in the Rust e2e lane.
- **Remaining differences.** Both frontends apply the same rule; only the error wording differs, as elsewhere between the frontends.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for overlapping placeholders, `mm_placeholders`, and audio-in-video on `/generate`. Three are related, and none applies this rule:

- vllm-project/vllm#68905 validates Qwen2-VL ranges in Rust by matching `model_type`. This PR replaces that per-model approach with a model-independent rule in the shared validator.
- vllm-project/vllm#66237 delegates Python feature validation to the multimodal processor.
- vllm-project/vllm#64721 edits the same `MultiModalFeatures` validator for reused prompt token IDs but leaves the overlap rule unchanged.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][ROCm][Muse Spark] FP8 DSpark draft through the speculative config
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

At small batch the Muse Spark DSpark draft is weight-bandwidth bound: each draft step reads the context projection `fc`, the five decoder layers, the vocab-sharded `lm_head` and, once per sequential round, the Markov head `markov_w2` (207 MB in BF16 per rank). This PR lets users store them as FP8 through the existing speculative-config fields:

```bash
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 ... \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark", ...,
                         "quantization": "fp8_per_channel", "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}'
```

- `quantization` quantizes `fc` and the decoder linears with the generic online method.
- `draft_lm_head_quantization` builds the draft's own lm_head and its Markov head (a second vocabulary head) with the generic FP8 lm_head method from #64368. DSpark accepts it for Muse only on ROCm and only as `"fp8"`.
- The quantized lm_head pads its vocabulary so that each rank's shard is a multiple of 16 rows, as the FP8 GEMM requires. Unpadded, TP8 gives 202048 / 8 = 25256 rows per rank and fails at startup.

No new kernels: every FP8 layer runs on vLLM's generic FP8 linear kernels.

It also fixes the Muse draft under `speculative_config.quantization` on ROCm, which today crashes or silently corrupts it:
- The context K/V weight sliced rows from the quantized `qkv_proj.weight`. It is now built from the dequantized rows.
- The fused QKV + O-gate layer bypassed the parameter's loader, which online quantization wraps, so its weights were quantized from uninitialized memory. The same 4-line change is in the Muse target FP8 dense-linears PR; whichever lands first carries it.
- The `fc` input cast used `fc.weight.dtype`.

These fixes also stand alone and can be split out if preferred. The Muse drafter now rejects `quantization` on CUDA, whose drafter still slices and casts the weight directly, and per-tensor FP8 (`"fp8"`, `fp8_per_tensor`) on ROCm, where hipBLASLt per-tensor FP8 fails at the draft `fc` shape (N=8192, K=40960) for M in 296..320 and 584..640, including at graph capture.

The draft only proposes. Rejection sampling keeps the target's output distribution, so this can only move the acceptance length.

## Results

MI355X, Muse Spark TEP4 (TP4 + EP), FP8 KV, DSpark k=7. Timing runs use synthetic acceptance 4.05 with 100k-token contexts; 5 interleaved server starts per arm on one otherwise idle node.

| requests | 1 | 2 | 6 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| draft GEMM time per step, BF16 -> FP8 draft (µs) | 888 -> 667 | 831 -> 659 | 955 -> 693 | 1229 -> 866 |
| saving, % of the BF16 decode step | 1.2% | 0.8% | 0.9% | 0.8% |
| decode step p50, BF16 draft (ms) | 18.77 [18.75-18.78] | 21.16 [20.91-21.19] | 29.07 [28.97-29.74] | 45.02 [44.83-45.06] |
| decode step p50, FP8 draft (ms) | 18.55 [18.52-18.56] | 20.82 [20.63-21.20] | 28.55 [27.84-28.66] | 44.27 [43.69-44.59] |

Draft GEMM time is rank 0 from a profiled decode window, including activation quantization. At 1 request: Markov head (7 rounds) 219 -> 167, dense layers 413 -> 351, lm_head 136 -> 68, `fc` 106 -> 65; the context K/V bmm stays at 15. Step p50 is the median [min-max] over the 5 starts. Only the 1-request delta is clean (-0.22 ms, disjoint ranges, matching the GEMM saving); at 2-16 requests the p50 differences are within the start-to-start variation of the target step.

KV cache: +1.35 GiB per rank (122.22 -> 123.57 GiB).

**Acceptance.** Real acceptance on 200 GSM8K problems (5-shot, greedy, concurrency 16), two passes per arm: acceptance length 3.892 / 4.032 (BF16 draft) and 3.899 / 4.006 (FP8 draft); GSM8K 0.99 / 0.985 and 0.995 / 0.985. The pass-to-pass spread within an arm is up to 0.14.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_draft_fp8.py   # gfx950
pytest tests/test_config.py -k dspark_refuses_unsupported_draft_quantization
```

- A tiny Muse DSpark checkpoint with the real tensor names is loaded through the real loader (`get_model`) twice: once in BF16, and once with `quantization="fp8_per_channel"` plus `draft_lm_head_quantization="fp8"`.
- Every draft linear (including the fused QKV + O-gate, loaded shard by shard), the Markov head and the lm_head hold the `fp8_per_channel` weights of the BF16 checkpoint.
- The context K/V projection, `fc`, and the base and Markov logits stay within FP8 rounding error of the BF16 draft, and its heads are FP8.
- Sharing a target lm_head with equal weights leaves the FP8 draft its own FP8 head.
- Without the loader and K/V fixes, the model-level tests fail.
- The draft model built at TP8 (TP size faked, meta tensors) gives its FP8 lm_head a 16-aligned shard of the released vocabulary; without the `padding_size` argument it does not.
- CPU: draft quantizations no platform supports for the drafter are refused at config time.

4 passed on MI355X; the CPU cases pass. With both fields, Muse Spark TEP8 (TP8 + EP) and TEP4 servers start and answer coherently; before the padding, TEP8 failed at startup (`torch._scaled_mm`: `mat2 shape (8192x25256) must be divisible by 16`).

## Notes

- With `--monokernel`, #66051 (open) declines the FP8 Markov head ("Markov weights not bf16") and the regular loop runs.
- The loader's "Quantizing N layers" and "Online quantization ... took" lines read the target's quant config, so they do not count the draft; its `Selected ... for Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` kernel lines show it is quantized.
- The context K/V projection keeps a BF16 copy of the K/V rows (40 MiB per rank), as the BF16 draft already does; it runs once per context token, not per draft round.
- Weight reload goes through the generic layerwise path; it was not tested here.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR. I have carefully reviewed the changes, tests, and results.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Add encoder cache events
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add an encoder cache (EC) event stream that mirrors KV cache events, so routers
and cache-aware orchestrators can learn which vLLM instances already hold the
encoder output for a given multimodal input. Refs #66991.

## Claims

- New `--ec-events-config` (`ECEventsConfig`) with `enable_ec_cache_events`,
  defaulting to off and to the `null` publisher.
- Three events keyed by `mm_hash` — `ECStored(mm_hashes, medium)`,
  `ECRemoved(mm_hashes, medium)`, `AllECCleared()` — delivered in an
  `ECEventBatch` over the same ZMQ publisher, replay buffer, topic handling and
  data-parallel port offset as KV events.
- The scheduler's own encoder cache reports `medium="GPU"` stores, evictions and
  full clears; EC connectors can report their own tier through
  `ECConnectorBase.take_events()`.
- Pure refactor for KV events: `PublisherConfig` is extracted as the transport
  base class, `KVEventsConfig` keeps the same fields and behavior (including the
  DP-offset endpoints reported by the publisher).

## Validation

- Lint/format on all touched files:
  `uvx ruff@0.14.0 check <files>` and `uvx ruff@0.14.0 format --check <files>`
  → all checks passed, 86 files already formatted.
- New unit tests:
  - `tests/distributed/test_events.py::test_ec_event_publisher_factory`
    (disabled → null publisher, enabled → ZMQ with DP-offset endpoints, caller
    config is not mutated)
  - `tests/distributed/test_events.py::test_ec_event_batch_roundtrip`
    (msgspec encode/decode round-trip of all three event types)
  - `tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py::test_events_disabled_by_default`,
    `::test_events_report_gpu_store_and_eviction`,
    `::test_events_report_full_clear`
- Run with:

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_events.py \
      tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -v
  ```

  These were not executed in my environment (no GPU/torch install); CI runs them
  as `cpu_test` / distributed unit tests.
- The two semantics this change relies on were verified standalone (throwaway
  scripts, not committed): pydantic dataclass inheritance + `@property`
  override + `dataclasses.replace` preserving the config subclass, and the
  msgspec `tag=True` / `array_like` batch round-trip.
- Manual smoke test:

  ```bash
  vllm serve <mm-model> \
    --ec-events-config '{"enable_ec_cache_events": true, "publisher": "zmq", "endpoint": "tcp://*:5658", "topic": "ec-events"}'
  ```

  then subscribe as in `examples/features/kv_events/kv_events_subscriber.py` and
  decode `ECEventBatch`.
- No model output, accuracy or serving behavior changes, so no eval results are
  included.

## Details

- **Why not reuse `KVEventBatch`:** KV events carry block-level data
  (`block_hashes`, `parent_block_hash`, `token_ids`, `lora_name`, `group_idx`,
  ...) that has no meaning for encoder cache. EC events only need the
  `mm_hash` set, the medium and a clear-all signal.
- **`PublisherConfig` extraction:** `EventPublisherFactory.create()` previously
  hard-required `KVEventsConfig` and popped `enable_kv_cache_events`, which ties
  the transport layer to one event kind. The base class owns the transport
  fields plus `enable_events`, subclasses override `enable_events` and the
  existing `__post_init__` still resolves `publisher` to `"zmq"`/`"null"`.
- **Keeping the config subtype in `get_publisher_config()`:** the ZMQ publisher
  now stores `dataclasses.replace(config, endpoint=..., replay_endpoint=...)`
  instead of rebuilding a `KVEventsConfig`, so callers get a config of the same
  kind with the DP-offset endpoints they actually need to connect to.
- **GPU events come from `EncoderCacheManager`, not a connector:** the scheduler's
  own encoder cache is a valid event source even when no EC connector is
  configured, so emitting from `allocate()` / eviction / `reset()` is required
  rather than optional.
- **`EncoderDecoderCacheManager` emits nothing:** enc-dec models do not reuse
  encoder outputs across requests, so it only inherits the empty queue.
- **Limitations / follow-ups:** non-GPU media only appear once a concrete
  connector implements `take_events()` (Mooncake etc. currently inherit the
  empty default); `ec_events_config` is not yet exposed through
  `EngineCoreReadyResponse` / the Rust frontend; no `ECEventAggregator` is
  added because the scheduler is the only emitter per rank.
- **Duplicate work:** `gh` credentials were unavailable in my environment, so
  `gh pr list --search "66991 in:body"` / `"encoder cache events"` still need to
  be re-run before this is opened. No known PR implements EC events.
- **AI assistance:** this change was written with AI assistance; the submitter
  reviewed every changed line and must be able to defend it end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Enable XPU graph mode for 6 recipes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Port of vllm-project/recipes#1269 now that recipes live in `recipes/models/` of this repo.

### Summary


Remove `--enforce-eager` from the Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60 / B70) configs of the following recipes so they run with torch.compile + XPU graphs
(`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). Single-request decode throughput improves by up to 7.9x.

| Recipe | XPU mode | Other XPU changes |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B | graph | mark Arc Pro B60 as verified |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B | graph | – |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | graph | `--max-num-seqs 32` (needed on B60) |
| google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | graph | add `arc_pro_b60` / `arc_pro_b70` to BF16 `supported_hardware` |
| google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it | graph | – |
| meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct | graph | – |

### Test setup

- vLLM 0.33.0+xpu, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.15.4, `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu` image
- Recipe XPU args with `--max-model-len 8192`
- Perf: `vllm bench serve`, random ISL/OSL 4096/1024, concurrency 1, 10 prompts, mean of ≥2 rounds

### Performance: eager vs graph (output tok/s, TPOT ms)

| Model | TP | B60 eager | B60 graph | B60 speedup | B70 eager | B70 graph | B70 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | 12.42 (79.5) | 89.71 (10.0) | **7.22x** | 13.79 (72.1) | 104.63 (8.7) | **7.59x** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 1 | 43.30 (22.8) | 46.07 (21.4) | 1.06x | 46.77 (21.0) | 61.00 (16.0) | 1.30x |

commits.pr_title: [Core][PP] Admit new requests past idle empty steps, and size prefill microbatches from the backlog
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Two scheduling changes for pipeline parallelism with async scheduling, both active only with PP > 1 (admission also requires DP == 1). The original optimization and first implementation are by @gau-nernst (the first two commits). The later commits rework them onto the existing wait-for-output input handling, simplify them, and cut the per-step CPU cost.

- **Admission:** don't let empty steps fill the batch queue and hold back newly arrived requests.
- **PP microbatch cap:** split the outstanding prefill backlog into roughly `pp_size` chunks so a light prefill load fills every stage instead of crossing them one stage at a time.

## Claims

MiniMax-M2.7 (FP8), PP4 × TP1 on one 4×GB200 node, prefill-only traffic (180k-token prompts: 161,984 cached prefix + 18,016 new tokens, 1 output token):

- Mean TTFT at 31% of capacity: **−60%** (5.1 s → 2.06 s); −42 to −47% at 51–66%; −14 to −22% at 82–99%.
- Closed loop: c=1 TTFT halves (3.25 s → 1.62 s); c=2 throughput 0.31 → 0.97 req/s.
- Saturated throughput unchanged (~0.98–1.0 req/s); p90 near capacity about equal.
- No decode regression (2k in / 256 out); decode throughput at c=4/c=16 is 13–18% higher with the cap.
- No behaviour change without PP.

## Validation

### Unit tests

Run on `9ff0cd87561` (this branch's head), CPU only:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_batch_queue_pp_admission.py tests/v1/engine/test_inputs_during_step.py
361 passed, 18 warnings in 68.18s
```

New/changed tests (`-k "pp_microbatch or decode_awaiting or admission or stop_on_add"`: 18 passed in 3.10s, slowest 0.10s):

- `test_batch_queue_pp_admission.py::test_empty_step_admission`: after an unneeded empty step, PP stops scheduling more while it is in flight and waits for a new request; PP=1 and steps a decode needs keep the existing loop. Fails without the last commit (an empty step could otherwise be replaced as soon as the previous one completes, keeping the queue full).
- `test_inputs_during_step.py::test_stop_on_add_returns_at_first_add`: returns at the first added request, including one arriving after the spin period.
- `test_async_scheduler.py`: `test_decode_awaiting_cadence`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_cached_backlog`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_skips_decode_only_steps`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_default_on`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_progress`.

The fast tests also pass at every commit of the branch.

### End-to-end

Arms: `main` = `94de867077c`; `admit` = this branch with `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens 0` (admission only); `full` = this branch with defaults. Benchmarked on this branch's code before its rebase onto current main (same diff; the rebase only resolved conflicts with #64145). ## Details

**Admission** (`EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue`, PP > 1 and DP == 1). With V2 + PP + async scheduling, the engine keeps scheduling steps while the scheduler has requests, even empty ones, because empty steps advance the PP decode cadence (#42187). With prefill-only traffic the empty steps fill the batch queue (`max_concurrent_batches` slots), the engine blocks on the oldest batch, and a request arriving meanwhile waits up to a full PP pass before it is scheduled. This PR:

- keeps at most one empty step in flight that no request needs (`Scheduler.has_decode_awaiting_cadence()` is false). Requests that will decode keep the existing behaviour. Schedulers without the method keep the existing behaviour (interface default `True`).
- with a free batch slot, waits on the oldest batch through the existing input handling in `_wait_for_output` (#65466, #65773), but returns as soon as a request is added so it is scheduled into the free slot. Past the 1 s spin period this keeps checking every 1 ms (sleeping, so the GIL is free) rather than blocking for the rest of the step, which matters when one step takes seconds to cross the stages.
- is off with DP, whose busy loop runs a dummy batch on every step that executes nothing.

**PP microbatch cap** (`Scheduler._pp_microbatch_cap`, PP only; new `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens`, default 4096, 0 disables). The step budget is

`min(max_num_batched_tokens, max(pp_microbatch_min_tokens, num_prefill_lookahead, ceil(uncached prefill backlog / pp_size)) + running decode tokens)`

where the backlog is the remaining prompt tokens of running prefills plus the uncached tokens of waiting requests. A lone 18k-token prompt runs as ~4.5k-token chunks that overlap across the 4 stages; a backlog of `pp_size × max_num_batched_tokens` or more gets the full budget, so throughput under load is unchanged. It is skipped without chunked prefill, with `disable_chunked_mm_input`, or with Mamba-aligned splits, and is never below `num_prefill_lookahead`, so a prefill always progresses.

CPU cost: decode-only steps skip the scan (~0.6 µs at 1,024 running decodes, vs ~150 µs for a full scan); the waiting-queue scan stops once the cap reaches the full budget; only the first `pp_size` waiting requests get a prefix-cache lookup, memoized per request (a 180k-token prompt's lookup is ~4 ms once, then ~2 µs).

**Relation to other PRs.** #68560 (draft) also splits a lone prefill under PP, by applying `long_prefill_token_threshold` to it. This PR sizes chunks from the whole backlog without a user-set threshold, so it keeps splitting when 2–3 prefills are outstanding and returns to the full budget under load, and it adds admission. #68560 reports that admission made 2 × PP2 P/D prefill TTFT p90 worse in their setup; that was a different implementation, but PP2 and P/D are not measured here. #50410 balances decode batches across PP steps and does not overlap.

**Limitations.** Measured on one model and PP size (PP4) with prefill-heavy traffic plus a decode guard; not measured with PP2, multi-node PP (remote readers fall back to blocking), P/D, or mixed prefill/decode traffic. The 1 ms poll after the spin period was not benchmarked in isolation. `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens 4096` may want a larger value on models with a higher fixed per-step cost.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to port, rework, test and benchmark this change.

Not a duplicate: vllm-project/vllm#61310 adds XPU LoRA for FP8/W4A16 by re-implementing the grouped path, and leaves MXFP4 without LoRA. Hooks avoid a second copy of the fused MoE flow; #61310 could reuse this approach instead.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Add workload snapshots to iteration metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #61690. With `--enable-logging-iteration-details`, stat loggers now also get two workload snapshots, for consumers that model iteration time from the batch composition: the KV context lengths of the requests each iteration ran, and a summary of the waiting queues.

One commit (`a7afc65068`) on `main` (`013ae19bf6`), plus the CI bot's merge of `main`: 14 files, +540/−10, of which `vllm/` is +274/−8 and `scheduler.py` +30/−3.

Changed since the approved revision (`37113e7a3d`): rebased onto current `main`, where the scheduler's `log_stats` argument is now `collect_stats` (#68674), and three of the new tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` are removed, as asked in review.

Not a duplicate: #61424 and #61690 (merged) provide the per-iteration counts and the GPU time this builds on; neither reports context lengths or the waiting queues. #53550 (open) adds Prometheus histograms of those counts and reports neither snapshot. Related RFC: #61423.

## Claims

**1. What is added.** Two dataclasses in `vllm/v1/metrics/iteration_workload.py`. All lengths are logical token counts.

| Where | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SchedulerIterationDetails.scheduled_workload`, in every iteration record | `sum_prefill_kv_tokens`, `var_prefill_length` | The iteration's prefill requests: sum of their KV context, and population variance of context plus half of the tokens scheduled |
| | `sum_decode_kv_tokens`, `var_decode_kv_tokens` | The iteration's decode requests: sum and population variance of their KV context |
| `SchedulerStats.queued_workload`, in every stats message | `num_prefill_requests`, `sum_prefill_tokens`, `var_prefill_length` | Waiting requests other than those in the next row, counted with all their tokens |
| | `num_decode_requests`, `sum_decode_kv_tokens`, `var_decode_kv_tokens` | Waiting requests that are preempted or wait for remote KV, counted with their computed tokens |

The request and token counts of an iteration are already in its record (#61424). `scheduled_workload` is taken in `schedule()` before the computed tokens advance, and is `None` for dummy iterations. `queued_workload` covers the three waiting queues (`waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting`, `async_kv_waiting`) when the stats are made.

**2. How the queued workload is maintained.** `QueuedWorkloadTally` holds a count, a sum and a sum of squares per category, so reading the summary does not depend on the queue length.

- With the flag, `create_request_queue` wraps each waiting queue in `TalliedRequestQueue`, which reports every request that enters or leaves it. The queue classes and the queue calls in `scheduler.py` are unchanged.
- The tally remembers how it counted each request and subtracts exactly that when the request leaves, because a request's status and computed tokens change while it waits.
- Four places change a waiting request without moving it, and call `Scheduler._refresh_queued_workload(request)`: a streaming session gets its next input, and a remote KV load arrives, fails, or reports invalid blocks. Any new such place has to call it too, or the summary is wrong (see Details).

**3. How the flag controls it.** `--enable-logging-iteration-details` is the only switch.

- Off (default): both fields are `None`, the queues are the plain classes, and no tally exists. `vllm/config/vllm.py`, `arg_utils.py` and `loggers.py` are not touched.
- On: every iteration record carries `scheduled_workload`, and a scheduler built with `collect_stats` keeps the tally and fills `queued_workload`. What is logged does not change (the Iteration lines do not print the workloads), and GPU timing is as in #61690.
- To get the records without the Iteration lines, pass a custom stat logger with `--disable-log-stats` (the third real-engine run below).

## Validation

On commit `a7afc65068` (main `013ae19bf6`), PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130. Two results are from the previous revision (`adc55cd401` on main `878ae13ff0`, same tally code) and are marked.

**The tally equals a scan.** A pytest plugin (not part of the PR) turns the flag on for every scheduler the tests build, and after every `schedule`, `update_from_output`, `add_request`, `finish_requests`, `make_stats` and `reset_prefix_cache` compares the tally with its own scan of the three queues.

| Run | Checks | With waiting requests | Mismatches |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduler tests (12 files, 698 tests) | 31,373 | 28,351 | 0 |
| KV and EC connector, streaming, spec-decode and offload tests (40 files, 2,233 tests) | 5,840 | 1,526 | 0 |
| Random driver, 58 configurations × 20 seeds × 150 steps | 1,075,797 | 1,068,058 | 0 |

The driver runs a real `Scheduler` with FCFS and priority queues, sync and async scheduling, async KV loads that arrive, fail or report invalid blocks, `async_kv_waiting`, streaming sessions, aborts and prefix cache resets. On the previous revision, with all four refresh calls disabled, `make_stats()` returned a wrong summary in 15,561 of 52,200 steps, and with any single one disabled in 93 to 9,223. With the flag forced on, 40 tests fail in this environment; 39 of them fail without the flag too, and the other one asserts that there are no iteration details.

**Real engine, one GPU.** `AsyncLLM` with a custom stat logger, `facebook/opt-125m` on one RTX 6000 Ada, `max_num_seqs=4`, 24 concurrent requests with known prompt lengths (20 to 600 tokens) and output lengths (2 to 37 tokens). The check compares what the stat logger received with what those lengths imply.

| Run | GPU timing | Records | Iteration lines | Decode KV tokens, received = implied | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flag off | – | 0 | 0 | – | pass: no records, `queued_workload` is `None` |
| flag on | yes | 139 | 139 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass |
| flag on, `--disable-log-stats` | yes | 139 | 0 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass |
| flag on, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` | no | 139 | 139 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass, `elapsed_ms` is `None` |

In the three runs with the flag, the prefill tokens (6,870) and decode steps (450) also match, every record carries a workload, each of the 144 stats messages carries a queue summary whose request count equals `num_waiting_reqs + num_skipped_waiting_reqs`, and up to 21 requests were waiting.

**Cost per engine step** (previous revision). `schedule()` + `update_from_output()` on one CPU core (i9-10920X) with 256 running requests; the arms alternate on one scheduler, and the numbers are the median time added over the same step without a queue summary.

| Waiting requests | Scan, FCFS | Scan, priority in order | Scan, priority heap unordered | Tally |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | +0.05 ms | +0.10 ms | +0.05 ms | < 0.004 ms |
| 1,000 | +0.27 ms | +1.12 ms | +0.24 ms | < 0.004 ms |
| 10,000 | +2.7 ms | +16.1 ms | +2.2 ms | < 0.004 ms |

The tally column is from the same measurement with 8 running requests, where a step is short enough to resolve it (at most 3.5 µs at 0 to 10,000 waiting); with 256 running it is within the noise of ±0.02 ms. The worst case for the tally is a step in which no request can run and every waiting request is skipped: with 1,000 requests waiting for remote KV, a scan adds 0.13 ms to such a step and the tally 0.86 ms (0.014 ms and 0.087 ms with 100).

**Unit tests.**

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py tests/v1/worker/test_iteration_timing.py
3 failed, 367 passed in 187.37s (0:03:07)
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "workload or cached_reservations"
8 passed, 304 deselected in 9.08s
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_engine_logger_apis.py::test_iteration_workload_reaches_custom_stat_loggers
1 passed, 1 warning in 18.76s
```

The three failures need two or three GPUs (`World size (2) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`): `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output`, `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`. The second command selects the new tests and the existing randomized test that now checks the tally; the third starts a real engine. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

- **Why a tally and not a scan.** The previous revision scanned the queues on every step. That is linear in the number of waiting requests, on the engine's scheduling thread, and largest when the engine is overloaded: 0.27 ms per step at 1,000 waiting requests and 2.7 ms at 10,000, and 1.1 ms and 16 ms where a priority queue is read in order, which copies its heap. Reading the heap unordered removes that copy but stays linear. The tally reads in constant time.
- **What the tally costs.** About 0.9 µs per request that enters and leaves a queue. `schedule()` pops and re-queues each waiting request it skips, so a step that skips many pays that for each (the worst case above).
- **Drawback: every in-place change needs a call.** A scan reads the current state; the tally is only right if it is told about every change. The queue wrapper reports the requests that enter and leave, but code that changes the status or token counts of a request that stays in a waiting queue must call `_refresh_queued_workload`. A future change that misses the call raises no error: that request is reported with its old category and length until it next leaves its queue (the error does not accumulate). The streaming-session call has its own test, and the existing randomized async-load test (`test_cached_reservations_admit_like_on_demand_sum`) now asserts on every step that the tally equals a scan, which fails without any one of the other three calls; a new in-place change on a path these tests do not drive would not be caught.
- **Limits.** `queued_workload` is taken when the stats are made, which is later than the iterations in the same message ran, and an idle engine does not update it. A request that was never preempted and whose remote KV has arrived counts as prefill work with all its tokens until it is scheduled. With more than one API server each server's stat loggers get only some of the iterations, as before. With async scheduling and speculative decoding a decode context can exceed the true one by the draft tokens the previous iteration rejects.
